issues.title: Pack the bits
issues.author: martinduke
issues.body:
Individual comment:

There are tons of variable fields in some of these messages that take up a whole byte to communicate 1-2 bits of information. These can at least be consolidated, and in many cases can be brought directly into the message type byte. This saves a bandwidth and eliminates error cases for invalid values.

Another possibility is to push more of this into parameters.

For example:
SUBSCRIBE has 3 filter types (maybe going to 5) and 3 possible Group Orders, for 9-15 possible configs. If ranges are a rare 

special case, they could become parameters.

SUBSCRIBE_OK needs 1 bit for group order and 1 for content exists.

SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE updates up to 4 properties of the subscribe (counting all parameters as one priority), but all the fields are included. Assuming one property is being updated in most messages, this could be more compact by making each property a parameter.

FETCH has three types with very different fields, as well as three values for group order, for 9 possible configurations encoded in 2 bytes.

FETCH_OK: one bit for group order and one for end of track.

issues.title: Make SUBSCRIBE filters into optional parameters
issues.author: vasilvv
issues.body:
Currently, SUBSCRIBE has mandatory fields specifying the parts of the track that the subscriber asks to subscribe to.  This made a lot of sense back when SUBSCRIBE could go back in the past, but I feel like this is not really consistent with our new definition that "SUBSCRIBE gives you newly published objects".

Proposal:
- By default, SUBSCRIBE is unfiltered.
- We define parameters that correspond to the currently defined filters.
- If multiple filters are specified, the object has to match all of them to be forwarded.

This naturally solves the extensibility problem (#790).

```
  Subscriber Priority (8),
  Group Order (8),
  Filter Type (i),
  [Start (Location)],
  [EndGroup (i)],
```

Maybe the proposal is adding the following parameters

PRIORITY (default to 128 if not present)
GROUP_ORDER (default to ASC if not present)
START_LOCATION (defaults to the next object larger than current largest, or 0,0 if no-content)
END_GROUP (default to open ended)

I would say that it's a Session Error if any appear more than once, to avoid nonsense.  Regarding #758, I think setting START_LOCATION={0,0} is the same as #853 's All Objects, right?

issues.title: Ranged DNE Objects
issues.author: martinduke
issues.body:
Individual comment:

It is helpful to subscriber/relay accounting to not have gaps of omission in group and object IDs (at least when group IDs increase with time). Hence, the Group Does Not Exist and Object DNE object status. These are useful even if not required.

However, a potential obstacle to this is the overhead of sending potentially very large numbers of Does Not Exist status objects.

A fix for this would be to allow range in these messages, i.e. the status code would be followed by a varint specifying the number of object IDs that are missing. It could go in the same subgroup as the preceding object ID.

For example, an original publisher could produce:
Group 3, Subgroup 0, Object 0.
Group 3, Subgroup 0, Object 1, ObjectDoesNotExist, Range: 1000, FIN
Group 3, Subgroup 1, Object 1001.

Since we have accepted that group IDs not increase with time, we can't make this inclusion of status objects mandatory for Groups. However, since object IDs *do* increase with time, we could do so for Object Does Not Exist, which I would support. However, the mandate question is separate from allowing the encoding.

An immediately apparent use case is Group IDs that are timestamps, where gaps can be arbitrarily large.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: FETCH fixes this problem because a gap of arbitrary size is encoded implicitly. Because of DELIVERY_TIMEOUT, putting these gap messages in subscriptions might have limited utility - you might not get the gap message.

It is said that Object with DNE "_SHOULD be cached_", I don't know how the Range DNE Objects would be cached in that case.

issues.author: gwendalsimon
issues.body:
The Original Publisher may now create groups such that group_ID does not increase with the time of production. In Section 2.3: "_Within a track, the original publisher SHOULD produce Group IDs which increase with time._" A recent added sentence is "_SUBSCRIBE and FETCH delivery use Group Order, so a FETCH cannot deliver Groups out of order and a subscription could have unexpected delivery order if Group IDs do not increase with time._" I am not sure what we can do with these track where group ID do not increase if neither FETCH nor SUBSCRIBE work properly. Anyway, this sentence does not address all the problems in the current spec.

Section 2.3 Groups. "_Subscribers to tracks which do not follow this requirement SHOULD NOT use range filters..._" The Subscriber cannot know whether the track follow strictly increasing group ID or not, it is thus impossible for the Subscriber to know whether it can use ranger filters or not.

Section 6.2 Priority: "_If two objects have the same subscriber and publisher priority, but belong to two different groups of the same track, the group order of the associated subscription is used to decide the one that is sent first._" The Relay cannot use the Group ID to check the order. It should know the order by another mean.

Section 8.6 SUBSCRIBE. The "Filter Types" part should be re-written. For example "_Absolute Start [...] If the start group is prior to the current group, the subscription starts at the beginning of the current object_" can hardly be implemented. The Relay has to ask the Publisher whether, in its full history, there existed a group with this ID. If so, then the Relay should go with beginning of the current object. If not, the Relay should wait for this group to eventually be generated. It is one of the many inconsistencies.

Section 8.6 SUBSCRIBE "_A publisher MUST NOT send objects from outside the requested start and end._" This cannot be implemented.

Section 8.9 SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE "_The end Group MUST NOT increase_" This cannot be implemented. Another sentence "_Like SUBSCRIBE, EndGroup MUST specify the same or a later object than StartGroup and StartObject._" requires a Publisher to check whether the specified end group is later or not. 

Section 9.1.1.1. The bullet "_0x4 End of Track_" must be rewritten since it refers to comparisons of groupID.

For all these group orders problem, one solution could be a specific message to query order to the original Publisher. Something like "is_prior(groupID_a, groupID_b): return TRUE if groupID_a was prior to groupID_b, else FALSE". But it is obviously quite an overhead.

If we add a flag on the track "is_not_increasing" to inform Subscribers that this track does not implement increasing group ID, then this flag may be reused to indicate some patterns for the group ID (+=1 , +=6219 , x=2 , any other).

issues.title: Do we need to allow multiple ranges in a FETCH request
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
Consider this case:

A track has two subgroups, base layer, with the even objects and enhancement layer, with odd objects.
Because of delivery timeout, a caching relay ends up with only the base layer (objects=0, 2, 4, 6, ...)
A client sends a FETCH for the whole group

This will generate one FETCH _per object_ from the relay to the upstream.

A solution would be to amend FETCH to have N ranges, eg:

```
Range {
  Start (Location),
  End (Location)
}

FETCH Message {
  ...
  Num Ranges (i),
  [ Requested Range (Range) ]+
  ...
}
```

I think the response is unambiguous(?), all objects after the End returned in FETCH_OK are implicitly not available yet.

comments.author: gwendalsimon
comments.body:
It is a good idea. 

What about the response to it? In your example, I would assume FETCH_ERROR No Object for every range (1-1, 3-3, 5-5, ...).

What happens in another case:
Subscriber A subscribed to the (gapped) Track from 14 to 27. Relay cached all groups it dealt with: 14-17-22-23-24-27.
Subscriber B subscribed to the Track from 49 to 53, Relay cached all groups it dealt with: 49-50-52-53.
Relay receives FETCH 20-56 from Subscriber C.

The Relay would send upstream a unique FETCH [ 20-21, 25-26, 28-48- 51-51] according to the proposal.
Which would generate
- FETCH_ERROR No Object 20-21
- probably a FETCH_OK for the range between 27 and 49 and some transmitted groups
- FETCH_ERROR No Object 51-51

We may generate _one_ FETCH response (either ERROR or OK) _per range_ (but it would make a lot of FETCH_ERROR messages in your example). Or we may group FETCH responses too, but the number of ranges in the first response may not be equal to the number of ranges in the initial FETCH (as shown in my example). It may be acceptable.

comments.author: wilaw
comments.body:
In principle I like the idea. One issue to address is scale.  think multiple ranges works fine with examples of 3 gaps. But imagine the same situation of odd numbers where your range is 0 - 10000. Now you want a FETCH with 5,000 ranges in the message. We would need an upper limit of how many ranges can be specified in one message.

Since FETCH responses are sent down a single stream, the results don't need to be grouped. There may be multiple sparse errors for missing objects. I thought that we weren't explicitly declaring missing objects. The FETCH response would close and any objects not returned were ipso facto missing?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> What about the response to it? In your example, I would assume FETCH_ERROR No Object for every range (1-1, 3-3, 5-5, ...).

No, it will be a FETCH_OK.  From the current draft:

> A subscriber issues a FETCH to a publisher to request a range of already published objects within a track. The publisher responding to a FETCH is responsible for retrieving all available Objects. If there are gaps between Objects, the publisher omits them from the fetch response. All omitted objects have status Object Does Not Exist.

I think the response is unambiguous.

* Any gap between the start of a range and an object within a range -> DNE
* Any gap between two objects in range -> DNE
* Any gap between an object and the end of a range -> DNE
* Any gap between ranges in the request -> No information

If a range overlaps the `End` in FETCH_OK, all objects with IDs larger than `End` remain in an unknown state, including all subsequent ranges.  I'd say the request ranges have to be in ascending order and non-overlapping.  We can probably make it a delta encoding to enforce this.

comments.author: afrind
gwendalsimon
comments.body:
> > What about the response to it? In your example, I would assume FETCH_ERROR No Object for every range (1-1, 3-3, 5-5, ...).
> 
> No, it will be a FETCH_OK. 

I did not understand the same. We should probably clarify then. 

Example: For any reason, a Relay has in cache 0 2 4 6 14 16. It receives FETCH [0-16] from downstream. It issues a FETCH range { [1-1], [3-3], [5-5], [7-13] } upstream. 

My understanding is: The Publisher interprets this FETCH as being four independent FETCH requests
FETCH [1-1], which generates FETCH_ERROR No Object 1-1
FETCH [3-3], which generates FETCH_ERROR No Object 3-3
FETCH [5-5], which generates FETCH_ERROR No Object 5-5
FETCH [7-13], which generates Object 8, Object 10, Object 12, and FETCH_OK

It looks like that I am wrong. I try another interpretation: The Publisher should interpret this FETCH as being a unique "FETCH [1-13] \ {2, 4, 6}". It would process the full range and just omit to transmit the objects 2, 4, and 6. If one single object is sent overall (here Objects 8, 10, and 12), it is enough to emit one FETCH_OK? If not then FETCH_ERROR. Am I correct?

> From the current draft:
> 
> > A subscriber issues a FETCH to a publisher to request a range of already published objects within a track. The publisher responding to a FETCH is responsible for retrieving all available Objects. If there are gaps between Objects, the publisher omits them from the fetch response. All omitted objects have status Object Does Not Exist.
> 
> I think the response is unambiguous.
> 
> * Any gap between the start of a range and an object within a range -> DNE
> * Any gap between two objects in range -> DNE
> * Any gap between an object and the end of a range -> DNE
> * Any gap between ranges in the request -> No information

Haha, the fact that you edited your initial message to add the latest bullet kind of indicates that it was not so unambiguous :-D 

I am a bit lost about the DNE. The draft says that an Object with DNE status "SHOULD be cached." (Section 9.1.1.1) so we are talking about something that may require processing and storing. What does "All omitted objects have status DNE" mean? Is an "omitted Object":
- an Object that is transmitted (with all the headers including DNE status) and the Relay should cache it 
- or is it excluded from the communication between Publisher and Subscriber, but it is implicitly a DNE Object so the Relay should create and cache an Object DNE.
- or is it excluded from the communication between Publisher and Subscriber, but it is implicitly an indication there is a gap, the Relay does not cache anything but it may somehow keep the information that it does not miss any Object, this being outside of MoQT spec.

One use case is a Publisher who generates groupID based on timestamp in ms. If all Objects with DNE should be transmitted from Publisher to Relay and/or cached by the Relay, then we are talking about thousands of DNE Objects between consecutive actual groups. An Object DNE with all headers is probably around 1kB (+ associated cache keys and management). Is it acceptable?

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body: I expect that most relay implementations would start by serving stuff from cache for as long as they can, and then switch to a proxy mode for the missed part.  Doing clever things with ranges means locking all of the things that are already in cache, and that can be bad if the client reads slowly.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> I did not understand the same. We should probably clarify then.

> My understanding is: The Publisher interprets this FETCH as being four independent FETCH requests
> FETCH [1-1], which generates FETCH_ERROR No Object 1-1
> FETCH [3-3], which generates FETCH_ERROR No Object 3-3
> FETCH [5-5], which generates FETCH_ERROR No Object 5-5
> FETCH [7-13], which generates Object 8, Object 10, Object 12, and FETCH_OK

Oh I see the confusion.  If an endpoint issued 4 fetches, then it would get 3xFETCH_ERROR and 1 FETCH_OK as you describe.  I think this makes sense for independent fetches, since it doesn't makes sense to open the response stream, send no objects, and close it.  However, I'd say for multiple ranges in FETCH, you only get ERROR NO_OBJECTS if none of the requested objects exist.

Regarding DNE Object Status - it is a little strange.  To me it's clear one should never send DNE in response to a FETCH, since it's implicit, though see also #757.  When would a publisher send in response to SUBSCRIBE?  Maybe if it wants to be nice to a downstream cache, but that may be better solved with #731 (with a similar extension for object), and we eliminate the code point for DNE to make it clear that you can't "send" something that doesn't exist.

comments.body:
> I expect that most relay implementations would start by serving stuff from cache for as long as they can, and then switch to a proxy mode for the missed part. Doing clever things with ranges means locking all of the things that are already in cache, and that can be bad if the client reads slowly.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: @gwendalsimon @wilaw please see #925

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: In order to make use of multi-range FETCH between a cache and an original publisher, you need to make two passes - one to find the gaps in your cache and another to merge the cache and upstream responses into a single response stream.  It's doable, but a little tricky, on top of an already tricky cache implementation.  My current fetch cache is single pass and sends a fetch upstream per gap.

issues.title: Existing Problems with Gapped Tracks
issues.author: gwendalsimon
issues.body:
A summary of problems related to gap, for the sake of documenting in one Issue rather than in multiple (sometimes loosely related) ones. Note that both PR #823 and #824 have greatly improved the solution. Here are the use-cases. (I consider here strictly increasing groupIDs)

### Tracks with Gaps from Publisher
Publisher sets groupIDs with multiples of 3. Relay has some groups in cache
9 - 12 - 15 - 18...
Relays receives FETCH from 0 to 250.

#### Current Approach
Relay checks in its cache. It sends upstream FETCH 0-8 and gets 3 and 6 . 
Then it delivers downstream 9 from cache. Then upstream FETCH 10-11, get FETCH_ERROR No_Object. 
Then it delivers downstream 12 from cache, Then upstream FETCH 13-14, get FETCH_ERROR No_Object
Then it delivers downstream 15 from cache. Then ...

This last lines repeat X times (with X for the number of groups in cache). 

#### Drawback
- Many unnecessary upstream messages for ERROR No_Object.
- The RTT to get the FETCH_ERROR No_Object may cause streaming problem, if RTT > group duration.
- Receiving FETCH_ERROR from upstream and delivering FETCH_OK to downstream is an odd behavior.

#### Solutions with current draft 
- Improve the cache management at the Relay, e.g. to include metadata to note the known gaps.
- Issue #899 makes all upstream FETCH gapStart-gapEnd be sent in once.
- Clarify the management of DNE Objects: Is it mandatory for the Publisher to generate DNE groups i%3+1 and i%3+2? Caching these objects can be a significant overhead (for example if groupID are generated with timestamps in ms, we would have thousands of DNE objects between actual groups!).

### Caching from Multiple Past Subscribers
Subscriber A subscribed to the (gapped) Track from 14 to 27. Relay cached all groups it dealt with: 14-17-22-23-24-27.
Subscriber B subscribed to the Track from 49 to 53, Relay cached all groups it dealt with: 49-50-52-53.
Relay receives FETCH 20-56 from Subscriber C.

#### Current Approach
Similar problems as previous use-case for all ranges in 20-27 and 49-53.
New problem in range 27-49 where the Relay has no object in cache because nobody has previously subscribed in this range, #899 would need a special response.

### Absolute Join FETCH 
Subscriber is currently getting track A Object (4,27). She wants to switch to Track B. In this track, Groups contain usually 30 Objects.
TRACK_STATUS Track B returns (37,2).
Subscriber decides to SWITCH at group 6, just for the sake of not hurrying the transition to 5 since the end of group 4 is soon. She sends SUBSCRIBE B LatestGroup and FETCH B Absolute Start (6,0).
The Relay sends upstream FETCH Absolute Start (6,0) to Publisher, and get FETCH_ERROR No_Object because the track had a gap between 4 and 37.

#### Drawback
With a FETCH_ERROR No Object 4-37, the switch is done immediately at 37, with high risk that Object (37,0) from Track B is not delivered on time, causing pause during the switch. (if she knew the gap 4-37, the Subscriber would set the transition to happen at group 38)

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> Receiving FETCH_ERROR from upstream and delivering FETCH_OK to downstream is an odd behavior.

I agree, though the alternative seems somewhat wasteful too, which is returning FETCH_OK, opening a uni stream, sending FETCH_HEADER+FIN.  Thanks for pointing this out, I don't think my cache implementation correctly handles NO_OBJECTs error :) 

> Improve the cache management at the Relay, e.g. to include metadata to note the known gaps.  

See #731, which I think will help but I assume there will be cases where there is a gap the size is unknown (eg: publisher crashed and restarted).

> Clarify the management of DNE Objects: Is it mandatory for the Publisher to generate DNE groups i%3+1 and i%3+2?

In the current draft, these are not mandatory to generate, and they are implicit in FETCH responses.  Does that work for you?

> New problem in range 27-49 where the Relay has no object in cache because nobody has previously subscribed in this range, https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/issues/899 would need a special response.

I'm missing what different about this use case or why 899 needs a different response.  Since the relay has no information about 27-49, it has to FETCH from origin to get the objects or determine that they don't exist before returning any information about 49+.

> Subscriber is currently getting track A Object (4,27)....TRACK_STATUS Track B returns (37,2).

I'm confused about the scenario.  Are A and B groups supposed to be time aligned, and subscriber is way behind on A?

> The Relay sends upstream FETCH Absolute Start (6,0) to Publisher, and get FETCH_ERROR No_Object because the track had a gap between 4 and 37.

The End of this FETCH should be 37/1, inclusive.  Shouldn't the publisher return FETCH_OK, and deliver 37/0 and 37/1?

comments.author: gwendalsimon
comments.body:
> > Improve the cache management at the Relay, e.g. to include metadata to note the known gaps.
> 
> See [#731](https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/issues/731), which I think will help but I assume there will be cases where there is a gap the size is unknown (eg: publisher crashed and restarted).

Yes, I support the addition of a pointer to the prior groupID. It would help.

> > Clarify the management of DNE Objects: Is it mandatory for the Publisher to generate DNE groups i%3+1 and i%3+2?
> 
> In the current draft, these are not mandatory to generate, and they are implicit in FETCH responses. Does that work for you?

Yes, it works. I would recommend adding some text in this section to make it more explicit.

> > New problem in range 27-49 where the Relay has no object in cache because nobody has previously subscribed in this range, [#899](https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/issues/899) would need a special response.
> 
> I'm missing what different about this use case or why 899 needs a different response. Since the relay has no information about 27-49, it has to FETCH from origin to get the objects or determine that they don't exist before returning any information about 49+.

This "example use-case" is: The Relay has some gaps in its cache, some of these gaps being due to the Publisher generating a gapped track (so maybe #899 or metadata or specific cache management techniques may help), and some of these gaps being due to other reasons. In my example, past subscribers were not covering the full history of the track. Another example may be crashed Publishers. This example shows that Relay does not know the status of all gaps (whether each gap is full of DNEs or not).

With #899 (which is very good, I support it too), the Relay gets some responses that are different (a mixture of FETCH_ERROR 
 No_Object and FETCH_OK with Objects). It adds complexity to the process.
 
> > Subscriber is currently getting track A Object (4,27)....TRACK_STATUS Track B returns (37,2).
> 
> I'm confused about the scenario. Are A and B groups supposed to be time aligned, and subscriber is way behind on A?

Sorry for the lack of details. Publisher generates group-aligned tracks A and B with groupID 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 37, 38, 45 ... The concept of switching with Absolute_Joining_FETCH is that the Subscriber must choose a groupID in the future for the switch to happen.

The Subscriber is behind live... but she does not know how much late she is. She is currently getting (4, 27), track_status says the latest is (37, 2). The Subscriber has no clue on the best switching transition group to choose. She chooses (6, 0) because she _hopes_ that both group 5 and group 6 exist and she wants to switch quickly but not immediately. Unfortunately, there is no group at all between 4 and 37.

Should she know the actual gaps of the track, she would choose a transition at 38 or 45. When the Track_Status indicated (37, 2), she thought she was 33 groups behind the live stream while in reality she was only a handful of objects behind.

Note that gap is also a problem in the original Joining_FETCH. The range calculation is a mathematical subtraction between group ID integers. I interpret the offset as being the number of groups the Subscriber wants to have in its buffer. It would be better to count the number of Objects rather than to use subtraction.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> With https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/issues/899 (which is very good, I support it too), the Relay gets some responses that are different (a mixture of FETCH_ERROR No_Object and FETCH_OK with Objects). It adds complexity to the process.

I agree there's complexity, but I don't think there's a _functional_ problem here.  In my implementation, any requested object that is not in cache and not known not to exist will generate an upstream FETCH of some kind.  But your example highlights that gaps in the cache can happen for multiple reasons, even if we added a restriction that the original publisher has to make a track with no gaps.  The difference with allowing gaps in the original track is that there's a chance that the cache will make a request upstream for a useless gap.  Gaps are encoded very efficiently in the response though, and are negatively cacheable (you shouldn't have to re-request a known DNE gap).  I think with solutions for 731 and 899, it should be ok.

> Publisher generates group-aligned tracks A and B with groupID 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 37, 38, 45

I think Abs Joining Fetch (6,0) will do the "right thing", you won't get FETCH_ERROR/No objects as long as there's at least one object in the range between the joining fetch start group (6) and the subscribe latest (37, 1) [from your original example].

> The range calculation is a mathematical subtraction between group ID integers. I interpret the offset as being the number of groups the Subscriber wants to have in its buffer

To the degree that WARP is going to define how its ABR switching works, rather than MoQT, it may be fine to put additional restrictions on group IDs in WARP.  It's also going to have a timeline track or other mechanism to determine how groups correspond to time, right?  CC: @wilaw WARP enthusiast.

Your other comments describe issues for how a relay will manage its cache, which is definitely MoQT.

comments.author: gwendalsimon
comments.body:
> > With [#899](https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/issues/899) (which is very good, I support it too), the Relay gets some responses that are different (a mixture of FETCH_ERROR No_Object and FETCH_OK with Objects). It adds complexity to the process.
> 
> I agree there's complexity, but I don't think there's a _functional_ problem here.

OK, let me summarize. Since draft 10, four issues have addressed, from a functional perspective, the problems related to gap:
- #801 adds an explicit No_Object in the list of FETCH_ERROR codes
- #899 enables issuing one FETCH for all gaps in the range, all in one. It reduces the overhead of signaling.
- #823 indicates that gaps in a FETCH response are implicit DNE Objects
- #824 clarified the use of FETCH_OK with end Groups/Objects

I still maintain that having a pointer to the Previous Object would simplify the caching process at Relay.

In my opinion, the original draft 10 was not a consensus on the management of gaps. I agree with you that Today's draft is better. That being said, I think #899 is only half-baked at this stage. 

> > The range calculation is a mathematical subtraction between group ID integers. I interpret the offset as being the number of groups the Subscriber wants to have in its buffer
> 
> To the degree that WARP is going to define how its ABR switching works, rather than MoQT, it may be fine to put additional restrictions on group IDs in WARP. It's also going to have a timeline track or other mechanism to determine how groups correspond to time, right? CC: [@wilaw](https://github.com/wilaw) WARP enthusiast.

I will create a separated issues on the problem of gaps for Joining_FETCH.

comments.body:
> To the degree that WARP is going to define how its ABR switching works, rather than MoQT, it may be fine to put additional restrictions on group IDs in WARP. It's also going to have a timeline track or other mechanism to determine how groups correspond to time, right? CC: @wilaw WARP enthusiast.

comments.body:
> Yes. WARP will constrain group IDs to start at 0 and increment by 1. See [moq-wg/warp-streaming-format#48](https://github.com/moq-wg/warp-streaming-format/issues/48) and [moq-wg/warp-streaming-format#49](https://github.com/moq-wg/warp-streaming-format/pull/49)

issues.title: Prevent Rapid Reset style attacks
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
Rapid reset style means one peer can send a lot of control messages per packet, causing work for the peer, without requiring any feedback from peer and not violating protocol rules.

Currently possible:

ANNOUNCE+UNANNOUNCE
SUBSCRIBE_ANNOUNCES+UNSUBSCRIBE_ANNOUNCES
TRACK_STATUS_REQUEST*
SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE*

SUBSCRIBE+UNSUBSCRIBE and FETCH+FETCH_CANCEL are not currently vulnerable because of Subscribe IDs.

I propose we merge Subscribe ID and Control Message ID (#898), and update MAX_SUBSCRIBE_ID + SUBSCRIBES_BLOCKED to apply to all control messages except those that cancel work (to prevent deadlocks).

issues.title: Need an alias to represent AUTHORIZATION INFO objects to minimize wireline size and decryption operations
issues.author: wilaw
issues.body:
The following methods all allow the transmission of an AUTHORIZATION INFO object.

ANNOUNCE
SUBSCRIBE_ANNOUNCES
SUBSCRIBE
FETCH

The object will usually be a token. A token such as CAT can contain claims that apply to multiple actions. A client will therefore need to transmit this token multiple times to the relay, each time it calls one of the above actions.  The token will be much larger in size than the message. In cases such as ABR switching, where speed is of the essence, the token must be processed very quickly and repeatedly within a session. 

Additionally, decrypting tokens and verifying their signature is a computationally expensive operation for a relay. If the same token is being reused during a session, we would prefer a scheme in which the token need only be decrypted and verified once. 

To optimize the size of the control messages and to prevent relays from having to repeatedly decrypt the same token, it would be efficient of the client could send an alias (or label) for a token the first time it sends it. Then in the future, it can simply send this pointer to the previously transmitted token, instead of having to retransmit the token.  

If an alias is supplied with a token, then the relay must cache the decrypted version of that token for the life of the session. If the token is supplied without an alias, then the relay may discard the token after processing it.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Can you explain how this is handled in the HTTP CDN world right now?  If tokens are passed as headers, the same token doesn't need to be repeated _on the wire_ because of HPACK/QPACK, but decrypting/caching them must be handled at a higher level, since HTTP requests are stateless.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Also, moq implementations need to take care when designing APIs around this kind of feature.  If two separately authenticated entities are coalesced onto the same first-hop connection, I shouldn't be able to add an ALIAS and have that refer to a token inserted by someone else.

To take another example from HTTP: the cookie header is taken verbatim to the "send request" API, and the compression happens under the hood on the sender side *only* the cookie exactly matches one known to be in the shared cache.

I will say this entire problem could just be punted to "just use HPACK", which is capable of compressing any name/value pairs and has minimal dependencies on HTTP.

comments.author: wilaw
comments.body:
> Can you explain how this is handled in the HTTP CDN world right now? If tokens are passed as headers, the same token doesn't need to be repeated on the wire because of HPACK/QPACK, but decrypting/caching them must be handled at a higher level, since HTTP requests are stateless.

In HTTP media world, tokens are passed with every media object request (i.e every 2 seconds or so). You are correct that HPACK/QPACk can reduce the wireline size. However each token must be repeatedly and independently decrypted by the edge server. Some specialized edge servers will store the decrypted version if they have some prior application knowledge, but most public facing edge servers don't. MOQT applications have a large advantage over HTTP-ones in that tokens need be passed only at the start of a subscription and not repeatedly during the lifetime of that subscription.

comments.author: wilaw
comments.body:
> I will say this entire problem could just be punted to "just use HPACK", which is capable of compressing any name/value pairs and has minimal dependencies on HTTP.


HPACK is built for compression efficiency for text-based name/value pairs. Yes there is Huffman Encoding for the text, but that is still not as efficient as sending the raw binary. With MOQT, neither the alias (name) nor token (value) are text based. We would need to encode the binary token to a base64 equivalent and then Huffman encode back to binary. 

A simple alias scheme will work better than HPACK for MOQT auth. 

> Also, moq implementations need to take care when designing APIs around this kind of feature. If two separately authenticated entities are coalesced onto the same first-hop connection, I shouldn't be able to add an ALIAS and have that refer to a token inserted by someone else.

On the relay side, the token store is the tuple (SessionID | alias) which is independent of the connection. We should add some language to this effect.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> On the relay side, the token store is the tuple (SessionID | alias) which is independent of the connection. We should add some language to this effect.

This isn't quite what I mean.  Let's say an application maintains a "MoQ session" pool to the relay and allows two different callers to access a session object in this pool. An API like:

`subscribe(track, token, alias)`

where token is optional can be misused:

Caller A:

`subscribe(track, mytoken, alias=1)`

Caller B

`subscribe(track, None, alias=1)`

It's much safer to not expose alias to the application, and just have:

`subscribe(track, token)`

and the MOQT library maintains a sender side map of token -> alias.  The library sends the alias if the application sends a token that has a valid alias.  This can also be an issue when proxying multiple downstream sessions into a single upstream session at a relay.

This is just something for the security considerations section, it doesn't impact what goes on the wire.

issues.title: gaps management in Joining FETCH
issues.author: gwendalsimon
issues.body:
Gaps in GroupID may require clarification for JONING_FETCH.

### Relative Joining FETCH

The draft says that the "_Subscriber can use a Joining Fetch to, for example, fill a playback buffer with a certain number of groups prior to the live edge of a track._" Hence I understand that the "_relative starting offset_" (simply offset) is the number of Objects that the Subscriber wants to gets from the FETCH.

The Section 8.12.1 explains how to calculate the range from the Offset. It is said "_Fetch StartGroup: Subscribe Largest Group - Joining start_". (By the way "Joining start" is not defined but I guess it is the offset). Using a subtraction between integers here does not take into account the case with gaps. If we want the offset to be a number of Objects, we must define Fetch StartGroup as being the Group ID _i_ such that the number of Objects in the range [i, Subscribe Largest Group] is exactly equal to the offset.

#### Problem
It is not only an editorial problem. Imagine a Relay without cache who has an ongoing Subscribe (for any other subscriber). It receives a new SUBSCRIBE + a Joining_FETCH with offset=10. It cannot upstream the Joining_FETCH to the Publisher since it does not have any Subscribe ID to attach to the Joining_FETCH. The Relay should instead sends a Standalone FETCH upstream, but since it does not know whether gaps exist, it cannot know how to set Start_Group.

### Absolute Joining FETCH

Absolute Joining FETCH has been designed to enable SWITCH by letting the Subscriber decide the exact _transition group_ at which the switch should happen. The Subscriber knows the groupID it is currently downloading (say _x_). It may know the latest groupID at the Publisher (say _y_). It chooses the transition groupID (say _z_) between _x_ and _y_, based on multiple criteria: whether it wants the transition to happen fast, whether it can take the risk to not have the data on time wrt playback speed, whether some events are planned.

With gaps, the Subscriber is blind on the status in the range _[x,y]_. It does not know how many groups are in the range and which groupID exist. It is thus hard to take any decision. Consequences include pause during switch due to bad choice. An example is shown in #902.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
An application needs to have some reasonable expectations of when there might be gaps in Group ID.  I'd expect most applications would have few to no gaps, in which case Joining Fetch is ok.

If you're doing unusual group numbering, hopefully the Subscriber knows that.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> Imagine a Relay without cache who has an ongoing Subscribe (for any other subscriber). It receives a new SUBSCRIBE + a Joining_FETCH with offset=10. It cannot upstream the Joining_FETCH to the Publisher since it does not have any Subscribe ID to attach to the Joining_FETCH

This is part of the design of Joining Fetch.  If a relay does not have a subscription yet, there are two options:

1) Subscribe upstream first and wait for SUBSCRIBE_OK, then process Joining FETCH locally
2) Send both the SUBSCRIBE and Joining FETCH upstream, and let the FETCH resolve at some upstream endpoint

In any case it needs to send a SUBSCRIBE upstream in order to handle the SUBSCRIBE that it received.

CC: @englishm 

> An application needs to have some reasonable expectations of when there might be gaps in Group ID.

+1 - WARP may mandate sequential groups (https://github.com/moq-wg/warp-streaming-format/pull/49) and it has a timeline track that can inform the app about group gaps.

If we think of each group as an HTTP object - then in HLS/DASH the URLs of these objects is defined by the manifest.  In effect, _every group_ has an unknown gap, right? You can't really attempt to switch without the out-of-band information provided there.  The purpose of Joining Fetch in MoQT is to offer the necessary transport mechanics but some of the usage concerns need to be delegated to the next higher layer.

comments.author: gwendalsimon
comments.body:
> > Imagine a Relay without cache who has an ongoing Subscribe (for any other subscriber). It receives a new SUBSCRIBE + a Joining_FETCH with offset=10. It cannot upstream the Joining_FETCH to the Publisher since it does not have any Subscribe ID to attach to the Joining_FETCH
>

> 
> 1. Subscribe upstream first and wait for SUBSCRIBE_OK, then process Joining FETCH locally
> 2. Send both the SUBSCRIBE and Joining FETCH upstream, and let the FETCH resolve at some upstream endpoint

My point was about a Relay who has an upstream subscription, but it does not have all objects requested in the Joining_FETCH that it just received from downstream. It can happen when: 
- The Relay does not have any cache
- The objects in the cache do not fulfill the Joining_FETCH request (for example it has only 5 objects in cache although the Offset of the Joining_FETCH is 10).

In that case, the Relay must:
- either send upstream a Standalone_FETCH to get the missing Objects based on the latestGroup in the existing subscribe. But with gaps, it is not possible to know the range to request.
- or send upstream a Joining_FETCH associated with the existing subscription. It means changing the Subscribe_ID of the Joining_FETCH, which is not clear in Today's description of Joining_FETCH. (Note also that the Relay may receive duplicated objects if it has some of these objects in its cache but a FETCH_CANCEL may be done to prevent it).

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> My point was about a Relay who has an upstream subscription, but it does not have all objects requested in the Joining_FETCH

The joining part is just to resolve the request range of the fetch, the rest of the problem you describe exists with normal FETCH too, right?  If there's already a subscription, the joining range can be resolved _locally_, and then treated as a standalone FETCH.  If there are missing objects, the range to pass upstream is computable:

> The Relay does not have any cache

FETCH upstream for {largest group - joining start, 0} - {largest group, largest object}

> The objects in the cache do not fulfill the Joining_FETCH request

Serve 0-5 from cache, then FETCH upstream for  5 - largest object

Or if the cache has only even numbered objects -- make fetch requests for the odds, or a single request if we have fetch with multiple ranges.

> It means changing the Subscribe_ID of the Joining_FETCH, which is not clear in Today's description of Joining_FETCH

This is a good point, I think my relay has a bug in this case :)

comments.body:
> > The Relay does not have any cache
> 
> FETCH upstream for {largest group - joining start, 0} - {largest group, largest object}
>

Yes, so it is my suggestion of Standalone FETCH. Unless you propose that Relative Joining FETCH is not the number of objects the subscriber wants to have in buffer but rather the ID of a group in the past. Imho, it challenges the main point of Relative Joining FETCH.

comments.body:
> Unless you propose that Relative Joining FETCH is not the number of objects the subscriber wants to have in buffer but rather the ID of a group in the past. Imho, it challenges the main point of Relative Joining FETCH.

As the document reads, it's neither a number of objects nor the ID of a group (that's Absolute Joining Fetch).  It's the offset from the current group ID to the group ID you want to start from. issues.title: Feature modularity
issues.author: vasilvv
issues.body:
Currently, in order to ship an MoQ client (or a server), the implementer has to implement all features.  This makes sense as a requirement for relays, or maybe as something that we generally expect of an MoQ library.

I am worried, however, that "features actually used" to "features defined and mandatory to implement" ratio, as it currently stands, will hinder the adoption of the protocol.  If I am asking a smart TV vendor to implement a MoQ video playback, I don't want to require them to implement SUBSCRIBE_ANNOUNCES, probably ANNOUNCE itself as well.

ROLE was an underbaked version of that, and MAX_SUBSCRIBE_ID is definitely a component, but I feel like we need to do more (both in terms of ability to make things optional, and editorially)

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Thinking of HTTP - not every *client* needs to implement POST, HEAD, CONNECT or OPTIONS if it only wants to send a GET and receive a response.  Servers need to be ready to handle any of these, even if it only wants to serve GET.  The difference here is - in HTTP the server can't randomly send simple clients messages, but in MoQT it can.

All the MoQT verbs (except TRACK_STATUS?) now define a "Not Supported" error code.  If the concern that simple clients want to tell the peer in advance of what verbs they support, so the implementations can be even simpler?  Is it too much to say, you need to at least be able to receive the known frame types and send a well formed _ERROR?

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body:
> Servers need to be ready to handle any of these, even if it only wants to serve GET.

Yes, but HTTP serializes all methods (that are not CONNECT) the same way, which makes rejecting unknown methods easy.

> Is it too much to say, you need to at least be able to receive the known frame types and send a well formed _ERROR?

Well, I do not expect most people to implement those in reality.  So if you need a read-only MoQ video server, and you're writing a library for that case, sending ANNOUNCE to it will most likely result either in the server closing your connection with an "unsupported message" error, or (worse) it just ignoring it entirely.  Thinking more about it, closing the connection is probably fine for most of those cases, but the text currently implies that all endpoints implementing MoQ will implement all of those frames, which will not be the case in practice whether we want it or not.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
I agree that ANNOUNCE and SUBSCRIBE_ANNOUNCES, at least as currently specified, aren't useful for many deployments.

I'd like to re-evaluate whether some parts of MoQT are optional once we've landed PUBLISH and such.

comments.author: Sy0307
comments.body: +1 agree with vasilvv. We (XQUIC) use MOQ in production, but we do not use all functions of MOQ. In fact, we do not use half of functions (especially those related to relays). Supposed that users focus on real-time media transport instead of CDNs, they may not need to implement msgs like fetch or announce.

comments.author: Sy0307
comments.body:
A proposal: Should we consider providing a new message type as a response when the server receives a message that it hasn't implemented yet? I know there are messages like ANNOUNCE_ERROR that could potentially serve this purpose, but you would need to implement several different ERROR messages. I believe that ERROR messages should be reserved for more detailed error feedback. 

For the simple case of an unsupported message type, we could provide an additional, dedicated message to handle this. This would make it easier for the server to process and allow different types of applications to tailor a minimal MoQ implementation that suits their needs.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I dispute the original premise in this issue:

> Currently, in order to ship an MoQ client (or a server), the implementer has to implement all features. 

If my client or server is, say, only a subscriber, then the only incoming control messages I need to handle are SETUP, GOAWAY, SUBSCRIBE_OK, SUBSCRIBE_ERROR and SUBSCRIBE_DONE.  What would I do with SUBSCRIBE or FETCH?

Control messages have a Type and Length up front.  The complexity of sending error code "Unsupported" if you receive an ANNOUNCE, or SUBSCRIBE_ANNOUNCES etc you don't want to handle is strictly the cost of serializing the appropriate error control message.  We're close to having all such messages have identical formats (currently SUBSCRIBE_ERROR and TRACK_STATUS need a little work), which makes it even more trivial to handle unsupported verbs.

A general purpose MoQ library probably does this automatically - as moxygen [does](https://github.com/facebookexperimental/moxygen/blob/main/moxygen/Subscriber.h#L72-L80)

So I don't think any additional work is necessary to support feature modularity at a "MoQT Verb" level.  @vasilvv are you looking for even more granularity of optional features?

We do that too.  Again, if your goal is "implement an MoQ library", this is not an issue, since you already have read the entire spec for that and understand how everything works.

If you, by contrast, have no context, and your goal is to write software that connects to an endpoint and gets live video from it, you're faced with a 60+ page spec, half of which has little to do with what you're trying to accomplish.

--------

I think I can see two things that would improve this:
1. Making it clear that you can close the connection if someone sends ANNOUNCE and you don't expect announces.
2. Editorial re-arrangement which makes it easier to ignore parts of the spec one does not need.

Moving some of the optional features into their own doc would also help, though I'm not sure I see any candidates right now.

issues.title: Wire efficiency for Subgroup ID
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
Subgroup ID can be optimized away in the most common cases:

Subgroup-per-group => subgroup ID=0
Subgroup-per-object => subgroup ID=object ID

We can use a couple bits from the stream header type to indicate this.  With #821 we use the LSB to determine if extension header length is present.  We can use the next two bits:

0x2: Subgroup ID present
0x4: Subgroup ID=Object ID

There's only 3 valid states, if 0x2=1 then 0x4=1 is a protocol error.

issues.title: Proposing BATCH_SUBSCRIBE
issues.author: Johan511
issues.body:
Envisioned [PR](https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/pull/914)
Description of PR is outdated, kindly ignore it.

Often multiple channels of media such as subtitles, audio, base layer / enhancement layer video are subscribed to simultaneously.

It would make sense that they are all within the same track namespace

Consider the following object model

```
very_long_namespace_prefix/media_id/subtitles/eng
very_long_namespace_prefix/media_id/audio/eng
very_long_namespace_prefix/media_id/base_layer_video
very_long_namespace_prefix/media_id/enhancement_layer_video
``` 

Currently this would require 4 different subscribe messages to be sent, each with the same track namespace prefix of  "`very_long_namespace_prefix/media_id`"

We propose a simple fix to this redundancy with the `BATCH_SUBSCRIBE` message to subscribe to multiple tracks using a single message.

```
BATCH_SUBSCRIBE Message {
  Type (i) = 0x6,
  Length (i),
  Track Namespace Prefix (tuple),
  Number of Subscriptions (i),
  (
    Subscribe ID (i),
    Track Alias (i),
    Track Namespace Suffix (tuple),
    Track Name Length (i),
    Track Name (..),
    Subscriber Priority (8),
    Group Order (8),
    Filter Type (i),
    [StartGroup (i),
     StartObject (i)],
    [EndGroup (i)],
    Number of Parameters (i),
    Subscribe Parameters (..) ...
  ) ...
  Number of Common Parameters (i),
  Common Subscribe Parameters (..) ...
}
```

This also provides the implementation an hint that these subscriptions are related and possibly optimise delivery accordingly.

Adding common parameters, these parameters are to be appended to all subscribe sub-messages in the `BATCH_SUBSCRIBE`. One use case for "Common parameters" would be parameters we would be authorization related parameters.

If there is a parameter repeated in "Common parameters" and "Subscription specific parameter" we treat it same as how we treat duplicate parameters.


Answers to some possible questions
1. **Why not update the existing `SUBSCRIBE` message?** : Updating the existing subscribe message adds an overhead of 1-2 bytes in situations where no batched subscriptions are being made. I do not have a strong opinion on whether the 1-2 bytes are significant

2. **How do we handle the numerous interactions associated with `SUBSCRIBE`?** : The receiver of the `BATCH_SUBSCRIBE` must treat it to be identical to receiving multiple `SUBSCRIBE` messages, this means it should reply to it using multiple `SUBSCRIBE_OK`/`SUBSCRIBE_ERROR` messages and `SUBSCRIBE_DONE` when the subscription is fulfilled, allow updates or cancels on each of the subscriptions individually using `SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE` or `UNSUBSCRIBE`. This removes much of the complexity associated with handling `BATCH_SUBSCRIBE` separately. 

3. **There are already talks of wildcard subscription, why do we need this?** : Assuming wildcard subscriptions to mean all tracks within a namespace; this might seldom be the right solution. Consider the above mentioned case, a wildcard subscription to all tracks within `very_long_namespace_prefix/media_id` would mean the client receives all subtitles and audio they are authorized to, this might include languages the client is not interested in receiving and data which would end up being discarded by the client. There might also be multiple post processed versions of the for censorship, better experience for specially-abled (), etc.,  



Design choices to mull on:
1. **Do we need explicit subscribe parameters for each subscription sub-message?**
Why not to have them? 
- `BATCH_SUBSCRIBE` is not suggested as a way to lazily buffer multiple subscribes into a single message, but rather allow for multiple subscriptions related to a single media experience to be sent together, does it make sense to have difference parameters for sub-subscription of them?
- More prone to duplicate parameter bugs, currently handling duplicate parameters is very simple; we just flag it as protocol violation but, in the last interim there has been discussion about changing this behaviour to allow duplicate parameters making it more complicated. Having multiple parameter arrays (per subscription parameter array and common parameter array) associated with a subscription can lead to unexpected bugs.

Why have them?
- More comprehensive extensibility, consider the case where each track is supposed to have a different delivery timeout
- Making sure the protocol is used correctly is responsibility of the user and not the standard

comments.body: I don't think BATCH_SUBSCRIBE adds very much value over sending multiple subscribes independently, unless you are planning extremely long track namespaces or common parameters (note that Auth will be getting a re-use scheme in #760), or you are subscribing to a very large number of tracks.  Do you have a concrete example of how much wire space you are saving in your application?

comments.author: Johan511
comments.body:
I have tried gathering some statistics on how many bytes BATCH_SUBSCRIBE would save,
But I believe they are going to be minuscule compared to the amount of data actually transmitted over MOQ. My primary motivation for BATCH_SUBSCRIBE is the intent being communicated upstream that the objects requested over these subscribe messages are related.

I am closing this issue for now, if there is favorable consensus on this topic we can re open it.

--- 

Statistics of how many bytes are possibly saved

I tried looking up some other media dissemination services to check what could be the length of a track namespace prefix

fwiw, given there often isn't any documentation on what each parameter means, I could be mistaken

### Netflix
All HTTP requests made to receive media segments have a "t" parameter (I am going to assume "t" means "track") in the query string which around 320 bytes long, 
 
Some UNIX magic later, I found the track request pattern is "ABABAABABABABABABABAABABAABACDCDEFFEFFEFFFFEFFFFEFFEFFEFEEFEFFFEFFEFEFEFEFFEFFFEFFEEFEFFEEGHGHGHHGHGHGHGHHGGHGGHGHGHHGHGHGGHGGHGGHGHGGHGGHHGHGHGHGGHGHGHGHHGHGHGHGGGHGHHGHGHGHG"

Based on observation we often 2 request tracks one after the other which leads me to believe they correspond to 2 components of the media

Assuming a similar track identifier in case of MOQT with a 300 byte prefix and 20 bytes for track name, we save around 300 bytes for every segment requested

### Youtube

Each video in case of youtube seems to be identified by a 11 byte base 64 encoded string, assuming that to also be the track namespace prefix to identify the video in case of MOQT, that is around 11 * (n-1) bytes saved for segment of video streamed, where n is the number of subscribe message for each segment. I believe currently in most cases youtube combines audio and video into a single segment, so I don't really have a track request pattern to reproduce over here. But it is not hard to convince oneself that 2 tracks (one for video and one for audio) is possible if youtube was redesigned today with MOQT

comments.body:
> My primary motivation for BATCH_SUBSCRIBE is the intent being communicated upstream that the objects requested over these subscribe messages are related.

This is more valuable than the byte savings.  I wonder if this will come back in some form in the context of server-side ABR.

issues.title: How to deal with malformed tracks?
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
There are currently several ways a group or track can be malformed by the publisher:

1) Subgroup with decreasing or duplicate object ID
2) Subgroup FIN in the middle of an object
3) A duplicate subgroup ID with object IDs higher than received on the previously FIN'd subgroup
4) Objects in a Group following "End of Group"
5) Objects or Groups in a Track following "End of Track"
6) The same object produced twice with different content or other immutable properties
7) mixing Subgroup and Datagram in the same track

There may be more...

We should add a section that mentions these conditions, and tell relays and consumers what to do if they receive a malformed track

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: I added some text in #806 but I agree we probably need more.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
HTTP/3 has the following section: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9114#section-4.1.2

We have the beginnings of "relays/proxies/intermediaries MUST NOT forward malformed tracks".  The other bit that HTTP has is that if you receive something malformed, you reset the stream.  What's the MoQ equivalent?

I'll note that the wire format is basically identical to the old OBJECT_STREAM - especially once #924 lands and you can omit Subgroup ID.

issues.title: Suspected Conflict Between Different Parts of the Draft describing subgroups
issues.author: Sy0307
issues.body:
Look at this example about multi-layer encoding (from [here](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-10.html#name-object-data-model) ):

> The temporal layers are sent as separate sub groups to allow the priority mechanism to favour the base layer when there is not enough bandwidth to send both the base and enhancement layers. Each frame of video on a given layer is sent as a single object.

But this conflicts with the explanation about the dependency relationship between objects in the following text [here](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-10.html#name-subgroups).

> An example strategy for using stream properties follows. If object B is dependent on object A, then delivery of B can follow A, i.e. A and B can be usefully delivered over a single stream. Furthermore, in this example:
> If an object is dependent on all previous objects in a Subgroup, it is added to that Subgroup.
> If an object is not dependent on all of the objects in a Subgroup, it goes in a different Subgroup.
> There are often many ways to compose Subgroups that meet these criteria. Where possible, choose the composition that results in the fewest Subgroups in a group to minimize the number of streams used.

If you don't understand where the conflict is here, let me explain: We use multiple subgroups to apply multiple encoding layers, let's say we call them the base layer and the enhancement layer, but obviously, our enhancement layer must depend on the transmission of the base layer, otherwise it cannot be decoded. Then they should obviously exist in one subgroup, because they are "not dependent" [Note: The user likely meant "dependent" here].

Is there a problem here? Or is my understanding wrong?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I think you are right that the text is oversimplifying here.  In the case of base / enhancement, the choice to put enhancement in a different subgroup might be more about "future base objects will not depend on current enhancement objects".  There are also cases where an object doesn't neatly fall into "depends on all previous / depends on no previous", and there's an application specific tradeoff between the risk of unnecessary head-of-line blocking vs reassembly complexity on the receiver.

comments.author: afrind
Sy0307
comments.body: Yes, thanks

issues.title: Draft 10/11 client version negotiation
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
We changed the format of SETUP parameters in the current editors copy, which is also where version negotiation is done.  We also changed the *SETUP code points to make it possible for a server to easily accept either version 10 format or version 11 format SETUP.

However, if a client can speak both 10 and 11, it cannot send both SETUP messages, because a version 10 server MUST reject unknown control messages.

So a client that supports both and doesn't know what the server supports has the following options:

1. Send v10 setup, if the session is closed (with #788?), try again with v11

2. Send a v10 setup that includes 11 as a choice, but do not include the MAX_SUBSCRIBE_ID (MAX_REQUEST_ID) param, because only that has a different serialization.  Send MAX_SUBSCRIBE/REQUEST_ID message after the handshake completes.  Hopefully no one has custom SETUP params with even numbers.  Note that Victor proposed dropping this param entirely in #511, which is Parked pending our 0-RTT story.

I'm not sure any specific changes are required, but wanted to document and get agreement on how to interop this.

comments.author: Sy0307
comments.body: I think this issue is actually very similar to #908 . Assuming the client discovers that the server hasn't fully implemented all MOQ features (in fact, I think this is highly likely, and we don't need all MOQ features), what should we send?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I'm less concerned about #908 because we already have an `Unsupported` error code for every message a MoQ endpoint doesn't want to support.  This is just figuring out how to do version negotiation over this specific draft format change.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: This is more broken than I thought due to the change to 16 bit length.  I recommend if a server is v11+ only, it reject v10 CLIENT_SETUP immediately without parsing the length, preferably with Version Negotiation Failed.  A v10/v11 server needs to parse the length of a v10 CLIENT_SETUP with a varint length.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Closing this issue - I mostly wanted to document handling of this case.

issues.title: Is No Objects the correct error code when FETCH start > Largest Object?
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
> If StartGroup/StartObject is greater than the latest published Object group, the publisher MUST return FETCH_ERROR with error code 'No Objects'.

If the Largest Object is (10,10) and I make a FETCH for (10,11), and the publisher returns NO_OBJECTS, then I should be able to cache Object Does Not Exist for (10,11).  This doesn't seem quite right, since the publisher can publish (10,11) later.

I can't remember our rationale for returning NO_OBJECTS past the known Largest Object, but it seems like a different error code - either `Invalid Range` or a new code like `Future Range` would be better.

There's a sub-case which is when the track is _complete_ and the FETCH start is past the end of the track - No Objects is also bad here because I need to cache that, it would be better to error the request in some way.

issues.title: Clarify that subscriptions with Forward=0 still get SUBSCRIBE_DONE
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
> A Subscription can also request a publisher to not forward Objects for a given track by setting the Forward field to 0. 

It's kind of implied that only _objects_ are withheld, but I think an explicit callout that SUBSCRIBE_DONE is forwarded even when forward=0.

issues.title: Relays need to reset open streams for subscriptions with forward=0 when receiving an object
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
Consider this case:

S->P: SUBSCRIBE, forward=1
P->S: SUB_OK
P->S: Object (g=0, sg=0, o=0)
S->P: SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE forward=0
P: receives g=0, sg=0, o=1
S->P: SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE forward=1
P->S: Object (g=0, sg=0, o=2)

The receiver will get o=0, o=2 on the same stream, which is not allowed.

Instead, the relay/publisher MUST reset the open subgroups on paused subscriptions when a new subgroup object arrives.

issues.title: Reuse of Authz Alias Parameter
issues.author: suhasHere
issues.body:
Current text says

Token Alias - a session-specific integer identifier that references a Token Value. The Token Alias MUST be unique within the Session. Once a Token Alias has been registered, it cannot be re-registered within the Session without first being deleted. Use of the Token Alias is optional.


IIRC from the interim discussion, there was in general support for not reusing the token alias in a session for a diff token , even if the token is deleted.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
The concern about Alias reuse as I recall was before the DELETE operation was introduced - eg you could just set a new value for the same Alias, and the text was unspecific about how that might impact a previous operation that conveyed the token in using the same Alias -- essentially is the token passed by "reference" to a higher layer, or by "value".

Now there's this:

> Using an Alias to refer to a previously registered Token Value is for efficiency only and has the same effect as if the Token Value was included directly. Retiring an Alias that was previously used to authorize a message has no retroactive effect on the original authorization

This indicates "value" semantics, hence disallowing re-use of Alias strikes me as unnecessary now.  Does allowing re-use break something?

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: I'd like to close this with no action unless there's strong objection?

issues.title: FETCH stream stalls if Objects exist and will be published, but are lower priority
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
It is possible that an original publisher has multiple tracks (ie: 1080p, 720p, 360p) and the highest quality is lower priority than the others.

In such a case, the original publisher may want to eventually publish all the content from all tracks, but might not consistently have the bandwidth.

In cases such as live sports, the jitter buffer may be 10-30 seconds and so a SUBSCRIBE+Joining FETCH would likely be used.

If the FETCH happened to hit Objects that had been created, but the original publisher doesn't have bandwidth to send yet, I believe it would have to hang until those Objects were published, since otherwise FETCH indicates a permanent gap is present.

Having a FETCH pause for a moment because it has to go upstream will be normal, but having a FETCH potentially pause for minutes to hours with no clear reason why seems problematic.

A fairly simple solution to this problem is to add an Object Status that is "Not Yet Available" or "Currently Unavailable" or something similar to indicate that it might be available in the future, but it can't be retrieved in a timely manner.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Yes the fetch stream will stall in this scenario, subject to the subscriber's timeout.  Is it that bad if the fetch stream times out?  Let's say the FETCH was for objects 1-10.  Is there a scenario where your implementation would return object 1 as "Currently Unavailable" but deliver Object 2 for real?

I'm also not sure how as an original publisher I would know to send currently unavailable - I'm more likely to put the real objects into my stream send buffer and discover some time later that the stream is getting starved.  The publisher can also reset the stream if detects it's not making progress.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Discussed in Stockholm - we can add a new fetch error that indicates this request is retryable, but now @ianswett is questioning his life choices and is unsure how an implementation would detect starvation without opening a stream and sending some objects (which is likely not a FETCH_ERROR).

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I'm removing the object model tag here since this seems more FETCH specific.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
I realized a similar issue could happen with SUBSCRIBE.  A subscriber could be only subscribing to a single quality of live content (including VC), and it would want to know immediately if the publisher stopped producing that content temporarily.

It'd be nice to tell clients this data isn't being published at the moment.  If it will never exist, then whenever the publisher decides to not publish a quality, it can publish that Object status and the subscriber will know to switch to a different quality.  In the 'not available yet' case, it's unclear what to do.

comments.author: afrind
