> BTW, Sec. 2.2 includes the following sentence: "Objects from two subgroups cannot be sent on the same stream." I did not check whether such sentences exist also in other places. A clarification should be made to the text to make it clear that such statement(s) do not apply when Objects are sent as a response to a FETCH request.

@afrind Any opinion herein?

comments.author: suhasHere
comments.body:
Since fetch talks about objects matching the request  and how it is sent on a unidirectional stream, subgroups doesn't seem to apply. Object header carry subgroupIds, but from fetch perspective it is filling in objects from the requested range.

"The publisher responding to a FETCH is responsible for delivering all available Objects in the requested range in the requested order. The Objects in the response are delivered on a single unidirectional stream"

Would you think adding some text that says Object's SubGroupID is not used in determining the stream mapping ?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> Objects from two subgroups cannot be sent on the same stream. 

We could add "in a subscription" to differentiate from FETCH.

I'm marking this issue past deadline since sending FETCH responses on a single stream represents working-group consensus.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Also, if you want subgroups on different streams in a FETCH response, then #1164 might allow you to make N fetches, each filtering for a particular subgroup.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
> Would you think adding some text that says Object's SubGroupID is not used in determining the stream mapping ?

But in response to a SUBSCRIBE with Forwarding Preference = Subgroup, each Subgroup is sent in its own stream, isn't that essentially saying that there is a one-to-one mapping between Subgroup ID and stream?

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
> > Objects from two subgroups cannot be sent on the same stream.
> 
> We could add "in a subscription" to differentiate from FETCH.
 
Is that sufficient, since a joining FETCH is associated with a subscription?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I'm repurposing this issue to be Editorial, for the purpose of clarifying that "Objects from two subgroups cannot be sent on the same stream." applies only to subscriptions and not FETCH.

issues.title: Datagram encoding should allow STATUS with omitted object ID
issues.author: martinduke
issues.body:
The obvious use case is missing groups where object 0 is an end-of-group object.

I can't figure out why 0x24 and 0x25 were omitted from the table.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: +1 no reason to disallow it.  I think we missed the case in OBJECT_DATAGRAM_STATUS when adding Object ID 0 to OBJECT_DATAGRAM, then we merged the tables.

issues.title: Unclear sentence on treating a track as Malformed in Sect. 8.1
issues.author: yekuiwang
issues.body:
In Sect. 8.1:

An endpoint that receives a duplicate Object with an invalid Object Status change, or a Forwarding Preference, Subgroup ID, Priority or Payload that differ from a previous version MUST treat the track as Malformed.

What does "a previous version" mean?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Receiving a duplicate means you receive object X after you have already received object X.  "previous version" is meant to refer to the first copy of X received.

Maybe:

> An endpoint that receives an Object that it has already received with an invalid Object Status change, or a _different_ Forwarding Preference, Subgroup ID, Priority or Payload MUST treat the track as Malformed.

issues.title: Inconsistent and unclear descriptions of Forwarding Preference
issues.author: yekuiwang
issues.body:
In Sec. 2.2, we have

> When a Track's forwarding preference (see [Section 10.2.1](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-14.html#object-properties)) is "Datagram", Objects are not sent in Subgroups and the description in the remainder of this section does not apply.

This sentence seems implying that there is a track-level indication of Forwarding Preference signalled somewhere. But I could not figure out where is such a signalling.

In Sec. 7.1, we have a sentence using a different wording of the same thing, "delivery preference":

> An Object in response to a subscription that belongs to a Track with delivery preference Datagram.

In Sec. 7.2, we have also have a sentence using the different wording "delivery preference" (twice):

> If two objects in response to the same request belong to the same group of the same track, the one with the lowest Subgroup ID (for tracks with delivery preference Subgroup), or the lowest Object ID (for tracks with delivery preference Datagram) is scheduled to be sent first.

Since the wording of Forwarding Preference is used more in the document, the three instances of "delivery preference" should be changed, for consistency.

In Sec. 10.2.1 (Canonical Object Properties), we have

> Object Forwarding Preference: An enumeration indicating how a publisher sends an object. The preferences are Subgroup and Datagram. When in response to a SUBSCRIBE, an Object MUST be sent according to its Object Forwarding Preference, described below.

This sentence seems implying that there is an Object-level indication of Forwarding Preference signalled somewhere. But I could not figure out where is such a signalling, either.

In Sec. 10.3 (Datagrams), we have

> An Object received in an OBJECT_DATAGRAM or OBJECT_DATAGRAM_STATUS message has an Object Forwarding Preference = Datagram.

This sentence seems implying that the value of Forwarding Preference is inferred based on how an Object is received. OK, let's assume this is the case for now.

In Sec. 10.4.2 (Subgroup header), we have

> All Objects received on a stream opened with SUBGROUP_HEADER have an Object Forwarding Preference = Subgroup.

This sentence seems also implying that the value of Forwarding Preference is inferred based on how an Object is received. OK, good. Let's continue the study.

In Sec. 10.4.4 (Fetch header), we have

> The Subgroup ID field of an object with a Forwarding Preference of "Datagram" (see [Section 10.2.1](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-14.html#object-properties)) is set to the Object ID.

Hmm, this sentence seems contradicting with the above two places that imply that the value of Forwarding Preference is inferred based on how an Object is received. Because in that case, an Object with a Forwarding Preference of "Datagram" is received in an OBJECT_DATAGRAM or OBJECT_DATAGRAM_STATUS message, not in a FETCH stream, right? But here the context is a FETCH stream. 


So, what's going on?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
The current state of play is:

Forwarding Preference is a **Track** property that is _implicitly_ signaled by the delivery of any object using either subgroups or datagrams.

There's this in section 10:

> Every Track has a single 'Object Forwarding Preference' and the Original Publisher MUST NOT mix different forwarding preferences within a single track

At the very least, the doc could be updated to consistently reflect this.  Let's use this issue to track that.

However, in Madrid someone (I forget who) approached me with a use case requiring mix-and-match -- eg: making Forwarding Preference an Object property rather than a Track property. 

See also https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/issues/1103#issuecomment-3124466086

CC: Enthusiast @ianswett

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
> The current state of play is:
> 
> Forwarding Preference is a **Track** property that is _implicitly_ signaled by the delivery of any object using either subgroups or datagrams.
> 

Adding such a sentence would make things much clearer. But even with this clarification added, my point above on the Subgroup ID field of an object with a Forwarding Preference of "Datagram" in Sec. 10.4.4 (Fetch header) seems not (sufficiently) clarified yet. In the in the FETCH context, what does an object with a Forwarding Preference of "Datagram" mean?

> There's this in section 10:
> 
> > Every Track has a single 'Object Forwarding Preference' and the Original Publisher MUST NOT mix different forwarding preferences within a single track
> 

I noticed that sentence. With it, even there is an Object-level signalling or inference, it is still OK to say it is a track-level property. But it is not directly related to whether it is signalled or inferred, thus I did not include this sentence earlier in the discussion. 

> At the very least, the doc could be updated to consistently reflect this. Let's use this issue to track that.
> 

Good.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Another editorial action needed, on the following sentence:

> When in response to a SUBSCRIBE, an Object MUST be sent according to its Object Forwarding Preference, described below.

This sentence should be removed, as Forwarding Preference is determined by how the Objects are sent, not the other way around.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> This sentence should be removed, as Forwarding Preference is determined by how the Objects are sent, not the other way around.

Sort of?  The original publisher makes the initial decision and all relays follow that.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
> > This sentence should be removed, as Forwarding Preference is determined by how the Objects are sent, not the other way around.
> 
> Sort of? The original publisher makes the initial decision and all relays follow that.

OK, to avoid confusion, it is probably good to avoid use of Object Forwarding Preference, just stick to the fact that it is a track level property, and once established based on the sending of one Object of track, it never changes for the entire track.

With that established, then changing the sentence from

> When in response to a SUBSCRIBE, an Object MUST be sent according to its Object Forwarding Preference, described below.

to something like

> When in response to a SUBSCRIBE, an Object MUST be sent according to the Forwarding Preference established earlier for the track.

would be good and clear.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body: And BTW, what about the very first to-be-sent Object of a track in response to a SUBSCRIBE? The sentence does not apply herein, and something should probably be said like that would be up to the sender to decide, right?

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body: Another issue: Currently the draft says Forwarding Preference may have either of two values, Subgroup or Datagram. However, for very first to-be-sent Object of a track, the value of Forwarding Preference is not determined until it is determined by the sender. Because of this (that Forwarding Preference could have three states, Subgroup, Datagram, or undetermined), it is sufficient in Sec. 10.4.4 (Fetch header) to just specify the Subgroup ID for the case of Forwarding Preference = Datagram? If the case of Forwarding Preference = Subgroup is sort of clear, what about the case of undetermined Forwarding Preference?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> what about the very first to-be-sent Object of a track in response to a SUBSCRIBE? The sentence does not apply herein, and something should probably be said like that would be up to the sender to decide, right?

The Original Publisher determines the Forwarding Preference for the entire Track.  All subsequent publishers of the same object use the preference determined based on how the object was received.  If the object was received only via FETCH, it can't be sent in response to a SUBSCRIBE (because it's earlier than Largest Object), it can only be sent in FETCH, in which case the original preference doesn't matter and the Object can be serialized with the received Subgroup ID (even if it was originally a datagram).

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
> If the object was received only via FETCH, it can't be sent in response to a SUBSCRIBE (because it's earlier than Largest Object), it can only be sent in FETCH

Wow, great to learn this! Thank you!

issues.title: Minor editorial: Remove obsoleted, remaining "OBJECT_DATAGRAM_STATUS"
issues.author: yekuiwang
issues.body:
In Sect. 10.3:

> An Object received in an OBJECT_DATAGRAM or OBJECT_DATAGRAM_STATUS message has an Object Forwarding Preference = Datagram.

Remove "or OBJECT_DATAGRAM_STATUS " from the above sentence, as there is no more OBJECT_DATAGRAM_STATUS message (it has been merged into the OBJECT_DATAGRAM message).

issues.title: Datagram Object serialization optimization?
issues.author: yekuiwang
issues.body:
Object-level signalling optimizations have been done pretty well for Subgroup streams in the current draft through the Subgroup Header, and are being worked on for Fetch streams in PR #949. But for Objects sent in datagrams, an optimization for Object ID is done in the current draft, but nothing is done for Group ID and Priority; they are always present in each Object when sent in datagrams.

I am curious whether there has been any special reason why Object-level signalling optimizations for Group ID and Priority have not been done and are not been worked on. Appreciate any information and/or opinion.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I think we can optimize out `Priority` but not `Group ID`.  If we specify the default Publisher Priority in SUBSCRIBE_OK / PUBLISH, the we can add another bit in the OBJECT_DATAGRAM type field to indicate that priority inherits this "default".  See #1056 for a beginning to this strategy.

I think the minimum set of fields in a datagram is Track Alias (which track does this belong to) and Group ID (where does this belong in the track).

issues.title: Step 4 of the Scheduling Algorithm should be updated
issues.author: yekuiwang
issues.body:
At the beginning of Sect. 7.2 ([Scheduling Algorithm](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-14.html#name-scheduling-algorithm)), we have: 

> When an MOQT publisher has multiple schedulable objects it can choose between, the objects SHOULD be selected as follows:
> 1. If two objects have different subscriber priorities associated with them, the one with the highest subscriber priority is scheduled to be sent first.
> 2. If two objects have the same subscriber priority, but different publisher priorities, the one with the highest publisher priority is scheduled to be sent first.
> 3. If two objects in response to the same request have the same subscriber and publisher priority, but belong to two different groups of the same track, the group order of the associated subscription is used to decide the one that is scheduled to be sent first.
> 4. If two objects in response to the same request belong to the same group of the same track, the one with the lowest Subgroup ID (for tracks with delivery preference Subgroup), or the lowest Object ID (for tracks with delivery preference Datagram) is scheduled to be sent first.

Step 4 should be changed to be as follows:

> 4. If two objects in response to the same request _have the same subscriber and publisher priority and_ belong to the same group of the same track, the one with the lowest Subgroup ID (for tracks with delivery preference Subgroup), or the lowest Object ID (for tracks with delivery preference Datagram) is scheduled to be sent first.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
It's a little redundant, but ok.

If two schedulable objects had different subscriber or publisher priority, the algorithm would have terminated at step 1 or 2.  Further, since there is only a single subscriber priority per track, then these necessarily have the same subscriber priority.

I guess step 3 mentions it, so we should be consistent one way or the other though.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
> Further, since there is only a single subscriber priority per track, 

Another new fact to me! I just went through all places containing the 50 instances of "Priority" in -v14, but could not find where is this specified or implied. Could you please let me know?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: > Subscriber Priority is a priority number associated with an individual request. It is specified in the SUBSCRIBE or FETCH message, and can be updated via SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE message. The subscriber priority of an individual schedulable object is the subscriber priority of the request that caused that object to be sent.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Hmm, that only determines that Objects associated with the same request have the same subscriber priority, but Objects of a Track may be requested by multiple requests, thus Objects of one track can have different subscriber priorities.

However, you are right that in steps 3 and 4, since they talk about "two objects in response to the same request", indeed it is redundant to mention "if they have the same subscriber priority", as they have to have the same subscriber priority. 

The publisher priority part is still needed in both steps 3 and 4, right?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Ah sorry, I didn't mean to confuse things.  Indeed the same track can have a different subscriber priority in each concurrent fetch and subscribe (at present only one subscribe per track is allowed).

> The publisher priority part is still needed in both steps 3 and 4, right?

I still maintain that if the publish priority were different between any two schedulable objects, the algorithm would terminate at step 2, so in step 4 the two objects being compared necessarily have the same publisher priority.

I think it's fine to have both 3 and 4 read "have the same subscriber and publisher priority", for completeness and consistency.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
> at present only one subscribe per track is allowed

So it is not allowed for a subscriber to first send a SUBSCRIBE with the "AbsoluteRange" filter type with an end Group ID, and after a while send another SUBSCRIBE for the same track but for a range of Groups with greater Group IDs?

> 
> > The publisher priority part is still needed in both steps 3 and 4, right?
> 
> I still maintain that if the publish priority were different between any two schedulable objects, the algorithm would terminate at step 2, so in step 4 the two objects being compared necessarily have the same publisher priority.
> 

I understand why you say that. Usually, if steps other than step 1 start with "Otherwise," then indeed that is an obvious interpretation.

> I think it's fine to have both 3 and 4 read "have the same subscriber and publisher priority", for completeness and consistency.

OK, sounds good.

issues.title: Can you update the subscriber priority of a FETCH?
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
> Subscriber Priority is a priority number associated with an individual request. It is specified in the SUBSCRIBE or FETCH message, and can be _updated via SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE message_. The subscriber priority of an individual schedulable object is the subscriber priority of the request that caused that object to be sent. 

SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE only applies to subscriptions though.  HTTP does provide a way to change the priority of requests in flight.  Seems like FETCH might need that.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body: Hmm, herein (whether to allow update of subscriber priority or not) there seems to be no reason to make a difference between SUBSCRIBE and FETCH.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Wire Format Options:

1) Add a new message for this (FETCH_UPDATE or PRIORITY_UPDATE)
2) Depending on how SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE looks after parameters settle, allow use of this message to update FETCH priority

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: It feels like we could use SUBSCRBE_UPDATE for this, but I agree it's useful.  It also would be useful to be able to end a FETCH earlier than originally requested in a clean way.

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body: This sounds like an argument for FETCH_UPDATE but I wonder if it is just better to cancel the current fetch and make a new fetch. It would be good to talk about use case for this but I can imagine that it probably is common in an app that is pre caching stuff in case you scroll. Seems relatively easy to add.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
My current proposal is to add PRIORITY_UPDATE, which can be used to update fetch priority or the default publisher priority (see #1056).

> I wonder if it is just better to cancel the current fetch and make a new fetch

I think the publisher-side processing for FETCH can be non-trivial so update makes more sense than cancel and re-fetch.

> It also would be useful to be able to end a FETCH earlier than originally requested in a clean way.

STOP_SENDING + FETCH_CANCEL is not clean enough?

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
In Toronto:

The consensus was that this might be useful, but was not clearly necessary for any usecase, so we should punt this to an extension/etc.

issues.title: Potential wording issues of "newly published objects" and "already published objects"
issues.author: yekuiwang
issues.body:
In Sect. 9.7 (SUBSCRIBE): 
> A subscription causes the publisher to send _newly published objects_ for a track.

In Sect.  9.16 (FETCH): 
> A subscriber issues a FETCH to a publisher to request a range of _already published objects_ within a track.

Clarification questions:

1. Aren't "newly published objects" a kind of "already published objects"? They were already published even though they were newly published, right?

2. An original publisher has Objects of a track of a VOD content stored for a very very long time, thus it does not have any "newly published objects" for the track. For such an original publisher, can a subscriber send a SUBSCRIBE to it to request for Objects of the track?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I agree this could use some clarification.

An object is "newly published" in this context when a Publisher sends the Object in a subscription, or is received via an established subscription.  Only such objects can be received via SUBSCRIBE.

So can you SUBSCRIBE to a VOD?

There's no way for a _generic_ caching relay to play the VOD back to you at anything other than line rate.  That said, you could write a VOD server that understands the media rate and acts like an original publisher.  I believe Zafer Gurel has implemented something like this in the demos he's shown at recent interims.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Regarding whether SUBSCRIBE can be used for a VOD content, let me try an example, for a better understanding.

Below is my understanding how streaming of VOD content could work:

C: client, R: relay, OP: Original Publisher (i.e., server)

1. C->R: SUBSCRIBE trackA
2. R->OP: SUBCRIBE trackA
3. OP->R: Objects of trackA
4. R->C: Objects of trackA

However, if SUBSCRIBE can only be used for "newly published objects", then is step 2 above OK? Because in step 2 the relay uses SUBSCRIBE to request Objects that do not seem to be "newly published objects".

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I think VOD in your example can be somewhat fraught, because MOQ relays are designed to work with live content.  Think about how the relay would process a second SUBSCRIBE AbsoluteStart=0,0 -- it will coalesce it with the existing subscription, causing the second subscriber to join the first wherever it is watching (which is a different kind of application -- watch party!).  You would need some kind of specialized VOD server rather than a _Relay_ to make this work.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Hmm, I am learning a lot! Thanks! 

Are you saying that MOQT does not really fully support VOD streaming? Or it does, but just my example is not a good one? If MOQT does fully support VOD streaming and my example is not a good one, could you please educate me how VOD streaming based on MOQT typically works?

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Or, if in step 2, FETCH is used instead of SUBSCRIBE, as in below, things would be (a little) better?

C: client, R: relay, OP: Original Publisher (i.e., server)

1. C->R: SUBSCRIBE trackA
2. R->OP: FETCH trackA
3. OP->R: Objects of trackA
4. R->C: Objects of trackA

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
CC: MoQ-VOD enthusiast @wilaw 

For sure you can do with with FETCH, though C->R _also_ needs to be FETCH (since #588).  This is basically how VOD works today with HTTP GET.  I think you can do something more interesting than that too, which avoids the so-call "FETCH loop", but someone needs to work out the details and identify the protocol gaps, if any.  It's also on the fringe of our charter, if not completely outside.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
@afrind Many thanks! Appreciate if you could give a bit information on what is the so-called "FETCH loop".

I think it would make a lot of sense for MOQT to fully support VOD streaming, since most apps (at least the major ones) that support live streaming also support VOD streaming, thus it'd be a lot more convenient for developers of such apps to develop the app using the set suite of protocols for both live streaming and VOD streaming.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
By FETCH loop I mean the client will FETCH for example 1 group at a time in order to play VOD.  I would say that this meets the definition of "supporting VOD".

However, I think conceptually it might be nicer to be able to issue a single SUBSCRIBE and let the publisher drive the delivery.  I suppose it also depends on the partial reliability model required -- eg FETCH would be fully reliable but in SUBSCRIBE you could specify a DELIVERY_TIMEOUT and have some VOD enhancement subgroups dropped.  I do think this _is_ possible as well with the current draft, **if** the publisher is specialized and has some knowledge about the playout rate of the tracks, and the 1 subscriber per-track-per-session would not be a problem.  But a MoQ _Relay_ (per the spec definition) does not work like this.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Yes it is nice to be able to use a single request for a track and let the the publisher drive the delivery. On the other hand, the publisher needs to be able to cancel continuing sending data of the track when the receiver becomes not longer interested in the track. Otherwise the traditional bandwidth waste problem of progressive download arises (and that's why segment based adaptive streaming like DASH and HLS got widely deployed). That should be true for both on-demand and live.

So based on the current MOQT draft, how is that problem solved for live streaming based on a single SUBSCRIBE for a track? How does the publisher gets to know that the subscriber is no longer interested in the track? Is the subscriber mandated to send UNSUBSCRIBE to inform that it is no longer interested?

Regarding the publisher knowing about the playout rate of a track, would it be good enough to derive that from the media bit rate associated with the track (and that information is known to both sides, through the catalog track specified by the WARP draft), at least initially?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> How does the publisher gets to know that the subscriber is no longer interested in the track? Is the subscriber mandated to send UNSUBSCRIBE to inform that it is no longer interested?

Yes.  The publisher sends until the subscriber sends UNSUBSCRIBE, the track ends, the subscriber disconnects, etc.

>  Regarding the publisher knowing about the playout rate of a track, would it be good enough to derive that from the media bit rate associated with the track (and that information is known to both sides, through the catalog track specified by the WARP draft), at least initially?

MOQT Relays treat the object payloads (including WARP catalogs) as opaque.  Can you write a WARP aware Relay?  Sure.  But MOQT does not have a solution for this problem right now, which might be OK?

comments.author: yekuiwang
afrind
comments.body:
You can SUBSCRIBE with an End Group that is before Largest Object, but this does not cause older objects to be delivered to you from a Relay unless these objects before Largest Object arrive at the Relay via another subscription.  eg: even if the Relay has cached these objects, it will not re-publish them in response to such a subscribe.  If you need them, use FETCH.

What a non-relay Publisher does isn't as tightly constrained right now.  There isn't a prohibition against the publisher re-publishing older objects if it gets a subscription with a filter covering a range that has already been published.

Do you have any suggestions for how you'd like to address this issue?  Are you looking for wording clarification, or do you think the design needs to change?

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
@afrind Thanks a lot! Right now I am trying to get a better understanding of the status. Then the next step is to think about whether there is anything is wrong (besides some editorial wording issues that we sort of agreed above) that needs to be changed, or something should or could be changed for some improvements, e.g., thinking about supporting both live and on-demand streaming in some optimized ways with minimum changes, if any, to the draft.

One more question, regarding the following:

> You can SUBSCRIBE with an End Group that is before Largest Object, but this does not cause older objects to be delivered to you from a Relay unless these objects before Largest Object arrive at the Relay via another subscription. eg: even if the Relay has cached these objects, it will not re-publish them in response to such a subscribe. 

Could you please let me know the place(s) in the draft that specify this? For this round of review, I am already in Section 9.13 (PUBLISH) thus have passed Section 8 (Relays), but I don't know where is this specified.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> Could you please let me know the place(s) in the draft that specify this? 

Hmm, well, it looks like it's not as clear in the document as it is in my mind.  You've found one of the closest hints -- the reference to SUBSCRIBE being for "newly published" objects and FETCH begin for "already published objects".  There's also a bit in SUBSCRIBE which is subtly hinting:

> All filters have a Start Location and an optional End Group. _Only objects published or received via a subscription_ having Locations greater than or equal to Start and strictly less than or equal to the End Group (when present) pass the filter.

eg: Objects sitting in a Relay's cache do not pass a subscription filter.

We definitely should clarify this up in the "Subscriptions" section, and possible call out a bit more of the theory of FETCH operation.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
>> Yes it is nice to be able to use a single request for a track and let the the publisher drive the delivery. On the other hand, the publisher needs to be able to cancel continuing sending data of the track when the receiver becomes not longer interested in the track. Otherwise the traditional bandwidth waste problem of progressive download arises (and that's why segment based adaptive streaming like DASH and HLS got widely deployed). That should be true for both on-demand and live.
>
>> So based on the current MOQT draft, how is that problem solved for live streaming based on a single SUBSCRIBE for a track? How does the publisher gets to know that the subscriber is no longer interested in the track? Is the subscriber mandated to send UNSUBSCRIBE to inform that it is no longer interested?
> 
> Yes. The publisher sends until the subscriber sends UNSUBSCRIBE, the track ends, the subscriber disconnects, etc.
>

issues.title: Filter / select across multiple tracks in a namespace
issues.author: mzanaty
issues.body:
Many important use cases can benefit from the ability to filter or select objects across multiple tracks in a namespace. A few examples below.

1. Meetings
    100 person meeting, but subscribers only want to see and hear the last 4 active speakers (voice activity computed by each publisher).

2. Security Cameras
    100 live cameras, but a human viewer can only monitor the top 4 most suspicious activity scores (computed by each camera).

3. Viral Videos
    100 live video feeds, but subscribers only want to see the top 4 most popular (upvotes sent to each publisher).

4. Sensors (or other non-media cases)
    100 temperature sensors, but staff can only monitor the top 4 hottest (computed by each sensor).

5. Feedback Tracks (media or non-media)
    100 subscribers send feedback tracks to a publisher, but the publisher only wants one feedback signal or a count of subscribers.

6. ABR Videos (a different animal which may not be tamed the same way)
     10 resolutions, but the subscriber only wants the one with highest quality within current bandwidth limits.

Today, these require a central server/cloud to receive all tracks from all publishers, filter them, then republish the selected tracks to all subscribers. This floods the ingest relay network and central server with excessive traffic that will be discarded. Traffic not discarded is centrally bottlenecked or hairpinned and incurs higher latency compared to direct relay network routing.

Alternatively, publishers can only publish their computed selection scores as metadata tracks to the central server which then republishes the selected metadata tracks to all subscribers who must rapidly un/subscribe to the real media tracks indicated in the selected metadata tracks. This metadata can still be excessive (consider 100k not 100 pubs), cause a sustained storm of control messages and relay state churn, and add even higher latency to selections.

To address these use cases efficiently and scalably, the relay network can filter or select objects across multiple tracks in a namespace. This can guarantee pruned paths that never exceed the final selected small number of tracks regardless of how many publishers are sending.

Design options for how to achieve this will be presented in the Toronto interim.

comments.author: suhasHere
comments.body: I fully support us spending some time on the approach for implementing object filtering within and across tracks. This covers real-world use cases and addresses key pain points where MoQ can be effectively leveraged to significantly enhance the end-user experience, reduce bandwidth costs, and achieve substantial improvements in scalability.

This is assuming we add Forward to SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, which we should probably do sooner rather than later.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Originally there was no length field, but we added it universally because #474.  It was a varint until draft-11, when it became 16 bit to both enforce the 64k limit on control messages and make the parsing uniform.

I'm not sure we've ever considered making the message length optional based on type.  There's also this open issue #915, which is incompatible with your proposal.

comments.body: @afrind Thanks for the pointers! From those past discussions, I learned that adding the length was for making parsing easier. That makes a lot of sense for messages with complicated payload structures. However, the problem of not-easy-to parse actually did not and does not exist for those messages with very simply payload. So IMHO it is a good tradeoff to not have the length field for messages with very simply payload and to have it for others. Of course if a lot of people prefer uniform control message header than getting rid of redundant 16 bits for those messages with very simply payload, then be it.

> If the Token structure cannot be decoded, the receiver MUST close the Session with Key-Value Formatting error.

Not sure whether this is an error at all, but the style of "Key-Value Formatting error" seems not aligned with other places of closing the Session with an error code, and it is not resolved in PR #1159.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> Not sure whether this is an error at all:

I think it is an error.  By Token Structure, we mean:

```
Token {
  Alias Type (i),
  [Token Alias (i),]
  [Token Type (i),]
  [Token Value (..)]
}
```

as opposed to the application specific "Token Value" contents might be.

So an example might be 

`Type=AUTH_TOKEN, Length = 1, Value={Alias Type=2}`

Here the value ends after the Alias Type, but it should also include a Token Alias.  Key-Value Formatting error is chosen because the length or value is incorrect.

I'd say it's editorial to change it to KEY_VALUE_FORMATTING_ERROR.

issues.title: Concepts of Client and Server might need clarifications
issues.author: yekuiwang
issues.body:
In 1.2:

> Client:
> The party initiating a Transport Session.
> 
> Server:
> The party accepting an incoming Transport Session.
> 

Given a Publisher and a Subscriber, if the Subscriber initiates the Transport Session, then it is straightforward that the Subscriber is the Client, and the Publisher is the Server. However, if the Publisher initiates the Transport Session (that is not disallowed, right?), then is it true that the Publisher is the Client while the Subscriber is the Server?

Unless it is disallowed for a Publisher to initiate the Transport Session, there are places in the draft that need to clarified to make things clear. For example, in many (or maybe most) places of the draft, it seems that the term Server is used implying that it is the Publisher, and that would be problematic if the Session is initiated by the Publisher.

comments.body:
“Client” and “Server” are strictly transport-session roles. The Client is the endpoint that initiates the QUIC/WebTransport session, whereas the Server is the endpoint that accepts it.

I think it's fairly clear, but if we want some additional clarity, we could add something like: "Client" and "Server" are independent of the roles “Publisher” and “Subscriber”. A Publisher or a Subscriber can be either the Client or the Server.

- 2.4.3: "An MOQT scope is a set of servers (as identified by their connection URIs) for which the tuple of Track Namespace and Track Name are guaranteed to be unique and identify a specific track." "MOQT provides subscribers with the ability to alter the specific manner in which tracks are delivered via Parameters, but the actual content of the tracks does not depend on those parameters; this is in contrast to protocols like HTTP, where request headers can alter the server response."
- 3.1: "Both provide streams and datagrams with similar semantics (see [[I-D.ietf-webtrans-overview](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#I-D.ietf-webtrans-overview)], [Section 4](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-webtrans-overview-10#section-4)); thus, the main difference lies in how the servers are identified and how the connection is established."
- 3.1.1: "An MOQT server that is accessible via WebTransport can be identified using an HTTPS URI ([[RFC9110](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#RFC9110)], [Section 4.2.2](https://rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-4.2.2)). An MOQT session can be established by sending an extended CONNECT request to the host and the path indicated by the URI, as described in ([[WebTransport](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#WebTransport)], [Section 3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-webtrans-http3-13#section-3))." Herein the second sentence provides more hint on what the "server" in the first sentence is.
- 3.1.2: "An MOQT server that is accessible via native QUIC can be identified by a URI with a "moqt" scheme." "The client can establish a connection to a MoQ server identified by a given URI by setting up a QUIC connection to the host and port identified by the authority section of the URI." Again herein the second sentence provides more hint on what the "server" in the first sentence is.
- 3.5: "However, a service provider needs the ability to shutdown/restart a server without waiting for all sessions to drain naturally, as that can take days for long-form media." "The server sends a GOAWAY message, signaling the client to establish a new session and migrate any active subscriptions."
- 6: "Discovery of MOQT servers is always done out-of-band."
- 9.3.2.1: "When connecting to a server using a URI with the "moqt" scheme, the client MUST set the AUTHORITY parameter to the authority portion of the URI."
- 9.3.2.2: "When connecting to a server using a URI with the "moqt" scheme, the client MUST set the PATH parameter to the path-abempty portion of the URI; if query is present, the client MUST concatenate ?, followed by the query portion of the URI to the parameter."

Places in the MOQT draft with "client" used seemingly as a Subscriber:

- 2: "This allows the client to join at the logical points where decoding of the media can start without needing information before the join points."
- 3.1.2: "The client can establish a connection to a MoQ server identified by a given URI by setting up a QUIC connection to the host and port identified by the authority section of the URI."
- 3.5: "The server sends a GOAWAY message, signaling the client to establish a new session and migrate any active subscriptions."
- 5.1: "Relays MUST NOT send any PUBLISH messages without knowing the client is interested in and authorized to receive the content. The communication of intent and authorization can be accomplished by the client sending SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, or conveyed in other mechanisms out of band."
- 6.1: "It does not prohibit original publishers from sending further PUBLISH_NAMESPACE or PUBLISH messages, but relays MUST NOT send any further PUBLISH messages to a client without knowing the client is interested in and authorized to receive the content."
- 9.3.2.1: "The AUTHORITY parameter (Parameter Type 0x05) allows the client to specify the authority component of the MoQ URI when using native QUIC ([[QUIC](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#QUIC)])." "When connecting to a server using a URI with the "moqt" scheme, the client MUST set the AUTHORITY parameter to the authority portion of the URI."
- 9.3.2.2: "The PATH parameter (Parameter Type 0x01) allows the client to specify the path of the MoQ URI when using native QUIC ([[QUIC](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#QUIC)])." "When connecting to a server using a URI with the "moqt" scheme, the client MUST set the PATH parameter to the path-abempty portion of the URI; if query is present, the client MUST concatenate ?, followed by the query portion of the URI to the parameter."

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body: Thank you for tracking all of thoses down.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
I think the assumption is that Relays are servers, and if you connect to something via a URI, it's considered a 'server'.  Most of the ones above seem to fall into one of those two categories.

I was tempted to try to fix: 3.5: "The server sends a GOAWAY message, signaling the client to establish a new session and migrate any active subscriptions.", but the text reads well in context.  Maybe we want to widen the entire section to just talk about endpoints and not servers?

issues.title: One option for EndOfTrack is Malformed
issues.author: martinduke
issues.body:
In 2.4.2 one definition of Malformed Track is

An Object is received in a Group whose Object ID is larger than the final Object in the Group. The final Object in a Group is the Object with Status END_OF_GROUP or the last Object sent in a FETCH that requested the entire Group.

but 10.2.1.1 says

0x4 := Indicates End of Track. Group ID is either the largest Group produced in this Track with Object ID one greater than the largest Object produced in that Group, or Group ID is one greater than the largest Group produced in this Track with Object ID zero. This status also indicates the specified Group has ended. Publishers MUST NOT publish an Object with a Location larger than this Location (see [Section 2.4.2](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#malformed-tracks)). This SHOULD be cached.

If End of Track uses the final group ID, the track will be malformed. So either we can force a new group ID for EOT, or change the definition of Malformed.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I think the intent is:

If you know the track is ending with the current group, send END_OF_TRACK with Group ID=Current and Object ID=previous Object ID + 1.  This Object is the final object in the group, hence not malformed.

If you don't know the track is ending with the current group, send END_OF_GROUP with Group ID=Current and Object ID=previous Object ID + 1.  This Object is the final object in the group.  If you discover that you have no more Groups for this track, you send END_OF_TRACK as the first Object with Group ID=Previous + 1 and Object ID=0.  This is not malformed.

And this is how the text reads to me.  Am I missing something?  Can you suggest the text that needs to change?

comments.author: martinduke
comments.body:
The second case is fine.

Are you suggesting that there cannot be EndOfGroup and EndOfTrack in the same group?

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
I think the following phrases have some problems:
- Group ID is either the largest Group produced in this Track with Object ID one greater than the largest Object produced in that Group,

If before adding the last Object with this 0x4 object status "the largest Object produced in that Group" is ObjectA with Object ID equal to ObjectIdA, then after adding the last Object with this 0x4 object status "the largest Object produced in that Group" becomes ObjectB with equal Object ID to ObjectIdA+1. However, in the sentence this context is not clear and thus the sentence is confusing to most (maybe Alan you are the only exception as you have the context in your mind :-).

-  or Group ID is one greater than the largest Group produced in this Track with Object ID zero.

The problem is similar as above.

How about the following wording for the first two sentences?

0x4 := Indicates End of Track. In this case, either of the following is true: a) The largest Group produced in this track has at least two Objects, the last Object has this Object Status, and the Object ID of the last Object is one greater than the Object ID of the second last Object. b) The largest Group produced in this track has only one Object, which has Object ID equal to 0 and this Object Status.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body: Similar wording changing should be made to "0x3 := Indicates End of Group. Object ID is one greater than the largest Object produced in the Group identified by the Group ID."

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> Are you suggesting that there cannot be EndOfGroup and EndOfTrack in the same group?

There cannot, since End of Track says:

> This status also indicates the specified Group has ended. 

Sending anything in a group after END_OF_GROUP, including END_OF_TRACK is malformed.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Something probably needs more clarity here, but I don't think any design changes are needed.  END_OF_TRACK implicitly ends the group.

comments.author: martinduke
comments.body: What a stupid I am

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
> > Are you suggesting that there cannot be EndOfGroup and EndOfTrack in the same group?
> 
> There cannot, since End of Track says:
> 
> > This status also indicates the specified Group has ended.
> 
> Sending anything in a group after END_OF_GROUP, including END_OF_TRACK is malformed.

I still think @martinduke's question has a point. Although there can not be two Objects in Group, one being END_OF_GROUP and the other being END_OF_TRACK, it is possible to have just one Object in a multi-Object group to indicate that the Object is both the end of a Group and the end of a Track. 

Of course, to do that, we need to change the semantics of Object Status to be something like the following, and allow an Object indicating End of Group or End of Track to also have non-zero length payload (and I do think that's a better design, as then you do not NEED (but you can still do that if you want) to add empty Objects to indicate End of Group or End of Track:

> Status can have following values:
> 
> 0x0 := Normal non-zero length object that is not the final Object in a Group or Track.
> 
> 0x1 := Indicates Object Does Not Exist. Indicates that this Object does not exist at any publisher and it will not be published in the future. This SHOULD be cached.
> 
> 0x3 := Indicates End of Group but not End of Track. The Object may or may not have a non-zero length payload. This SHOULD be cached. A publisher MAY use an end of Group object to signal the end of all open Subgroups in a Group. A non-zero-length Object can be the End of Group, as signaled in the DATAGRAM or SUBGROUP_HEADER Type field (see [Section 10.3.1](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#object-datagram) and [Section 10.4.2](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#subgroup-header)).
> 
> 0x4 := Indicates End of Track (hence also End of Group). The Object may or may not have a non-zero length payload. Publishers MUST NOT publish an Object with a Location larger than this Location (see [Section 2.4.2](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#malformed-tracks)). This SHOULD be cached.

With this suggestion, I request that this issue is reopened. Thanks!

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body: Or, if either of you prefer, I can generate a new issue and make the above suggestion.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> it is possible to have just one Object in a multi-Object group to indicate that the Object is both the end of a Group and the end of a Track.

I don't think we need to support this case (non-empty object that is end-of-track).  It will only save at most a few bytes on the wire, once per track.  I think the discussion in #1093, or this [thread](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/moq/NrXJFNGt4BfXdp2pk9CWQqEZXnY/) might be a good place to discuss it further.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body: @afrind Thanks for the pointers. I will study all these carefully and check whether anything should be done herein, in addition to the above clarification (https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/issues/1218#issuecomment-3287136516) that something like it needs to be done in any case.

issues.title: Requiring known Parameters to be understood and optimizing the framing
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
@fluffy suggested that there be a set of Parameters that are required to be understood.  As a result, these can use. Tag-Value format similar to QUIC frames, instead of Tag-Varint and Tag-Length-Value.  The intent is not just to save bytes, but also require them to be known and parsed.

We have a registry of Params with an algorithm for determining which param values have which value encoding.  This algorithm has changed once already and is still somewhat in flux.

For known Params, I suggest we make them the first N sequential param values and after that, the unknown section begins.  This avoids having a separate section for known params and gives them the lowest codepoints.

For example, if MoQT defined 5 known params with their own TV formatting and one negotiated an extension that had 2 more, then every Param value 7 and above would use the existing formatting approach of certain codepoints being varints and others length-value.

It's possible this approach could be used for Objects headers as well?

This is related to #1184, but I think it makes sense to separate the wire encoding question from what params/fields belong in what category.

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body: Something like this could work but gets messier when future version of the protocol define new known parameters  - might just need to write down some example IANA sections and start seeing this would actually look like in the document and might be easier to get everyone on the same page.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Any TV parameters in MOQT have to be understood or they can't be parsed.  #794 has a sketch for how we could allocate the param and extension type spaces which needs revision for possible TV, but I think we should just reserve some extra 1 byte codes for future TV.  Or are you proposing to split the encoding such that TV and TLV have different spaces?

I'd really like to consolidate the issues, if possible.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
I generally support the idea of specifying there be a set of Parameters that are required to be understood, including those are reserved to be specified in a future version. This allows specifying parameters that are either "non-essential" (with which if you don't understand you just ignore it and continue do you thing with the associated Object or Track) or "essential" (with which if you don't understand it then you MUST not try to do anything with the associated Object or Track). This piece of operation IMO should be clearly specified.

> Or are you proposing to split the encoding such that TV and TLV have different spaces?

I think that would work.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
1) What handling is required for unknown _request_ parameters?
2) How to choose parameter values for custom parameters (negotiated via _setup_ parameters) such that they won't conflict with new standard request parameters introduced in subsequent MOQT versions?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: #1390 requires Message Parameters to be known (not Setup Parameters, because extensibility).  It does _not_ make any attempts to optimize framing.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Can we use #1184 to track framing optimization, so 1390 would close this?

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: I'm happy to close this now that #1390 has landed.

issues.title: Do we ever need to explicitly send "Object Does Not Exist" on the wire?
issues.author: vasilvv
issues.body: Between other existing object status codes, and the Prior Object ID extension we added recently, I am not sure if there is a scenario under which we would need to explicitly send one of those on the wire.  Should we remove it?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: +1 I do not think there's a reason to send this on the wire.  It originated before we sorted out FETCH and added the Gap extension headers, which meet the use cases better than sending DNE.

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body:
Consider if original publisher had published some packets but then discarded the first object in first group due to it being old. Then the original publisher got a fetch asking for objects in first group. Would it just send what it has or what would happen in this case?

Working thought text in -14 and seems like it would all work and just the first object that the publisher still had would go a the first object in the fetch stream and receiver would exist everything between that and start location did not exist.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Discussed in Toronto, it's not in the minutes, but I don't think anyone advocated a use case to send DNE status on the wire in a subscription and it's clearly not useful in FETCH.

issues.title: Do we need Object Status and Prior Group/Object ID extensions in FETCH replies?
issues.author: vasilvv
issues.body:
For both of the current Prior ID Gap extensions, we say:

> This extension can be added by the Original Publisher, but MUST NOT be added by relays. This extension MUST NOT be modified or removed.

This makes sense for SUBSCRIBE, but when you FETCH those, you can already figure out there is a gap from the fact that there are no objects in that range.

End of Group (and other status codes) has a similar issue.  If a FETCH reply has an object (6, 0), followed by an object (7, 0), one does not need a special End of Group at (6, 1); the only extra information there could come from the associated subgroup ID, or from the extensions.  I've heard people express at one of the recent calls skepticism as to whether using End of Group extensions is a good idea (we do currently say that "Any Object may have extension headers except those with Object Status 'Object Does Not Exist'").  If don't allow those, we can remove End of Group from FETCH replies; I think this actually applies to all objects with non-Normal status.

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body: One thing to think about is if we were doing end to end integrity checking, it seems like we want this to data to not be modified by relays even if it was in a fetch

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
You need to store the gaps in your fetch cache and be ready to serve them in any case, because the FETCH might not span the gap -- it could start at the object containing the extension.

If needed for e2e integrity checks, the Gap extension needs to be inside the Immutable Extensions block, and there's already language that you can't mess with that value.

I'm inclined to keep it simple and keep this as-is.  Does it create problems?

Regarding removing extensions from all non-normal objects - please file another issue.

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body:
> One thing to think about is if we were doing end to end integrity checking, it seems like we want this to data to not be modified by relays even if it was in a fetch

That's fair, I've thought about this for a bit.  Authenticating non-existing objects is a bit tricky, though, since (1) those have no payload, meaning you'd have to put authentication into an extension, and (2) MoQT allows the original publisher to expire objects.

Ultimately, I think that if you need to authenticate existence/non-existence of objects, you'd want to do something like "add an auth'd sequence of previous object into each object".  I'm not sure people would want to do that in practice, since in most cases, we do expect to lose some objects due to network conditions, and those are not distinguishable from the attacker-controlled drops.  Does SRTP do anything about this?

> I'm inclined to keep it simple and keep this as-is. Does it create problems?

I think this would make things simpler, since you don't have to store non-Normal objects in cache or serve them in FETCH.

Let me try to elaborate on why I think this makes sense from the cache implementation point of view.  Currently, when you are implementing a cache, you have two ways to deal with End of Group:
1. Store the End of Group object.  When you're iterating over an object range, you have to explicitly check the object status to know if you need to jump ahead.
2. Store the End of Group object, and a gap: if the sequence for End of Group is `(x, y)`, then `[(x, y + 1), (x + 1, 0))` gap is added.  There is no need to check object status at all.

I would expect most implementers to go with the second option (they already have to deal with gap ranges, so there's more code reuse), in which case this proposal is just a natural simplification of that.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Discussed in Toronto:

We can remove Object Status from FETCH, with some consideration for how we will solve #1265.

I think(?) we said relays can remove Prior Group/Object Gap extension when delivering via FETCH, so long as they are not in the immutable section.

issues.title: More minor editorial changes
issues.author: yekuiwang
issues.body:
(Note: This issue is also to just to document some newly identified minor editorial problems, for which the fixes, probably together with fixes for some earlier editorial issues, are to be provided in one PR.)

Sect. 10 ([Data Streams and Datagrams](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#name-data-streams-and-datagrams)) starts with the following sentence:

> A publisher sends Objects matching a subscription on Data Streams or Datagrams.

For readers to get a complete understanding, it is suggested to add the fetch aspect, i.e., to change the sentence to be as follows:

> A publisher sends Objects matching a subscription on Data Streams or Datagrams and sends Objects matching a fetch request on one Data Stream.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Sect. 10.2.1:

> Group ID: The object is a member of the indicated group ID [Section 2.3](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#model-group) within the track.

"member of the indicated group ID [Section 2.3](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#model-group)" -> "member of the Group with the indicated group ID ([Section 2.3](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#model-group))"

> Publisher Priority: An 8 bit integer indicating the publisher's priority for the Object [Section 7](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#priorities).

"priority for the Object [Section 7](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#priorities)" -> "priority for the Object ([Section 7](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#priorities))"

> Subgroup ID: The object is a member of the indicated subgroup ID ([Section 2.2](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#model-subgroup)) within the group.

"member of the indicated subgroup ID" -> "member of the Subgroup with the indicated subgroup ID"

> Object Status: As enumeration used to ...

"As enumeration" -> "An enumeration"

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Sect. 10.2.1.2:

> Any Object metadata never accessed by the transport or relays SHOULD be serialized as part of the Object payload and not as an extension header.

"never accessed by" -> "intended never accessed by"

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Sect. 10.3:

> The Track Alias field [Section 10.1](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#track-alias) indicates the track this Datagram belongs to.

"The Track Alias field [Section 10.1](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#track-alias)" -> "The Track Alias field ([Section 10.1](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#track-alias))"

> When the total size is larger than maximum datagram size for the session, the Object will be dropped without any explicit notification.

"maximum datagram size" -> "the maximum datagram size"

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Sect. 10.4.2:

> All Objects on a Subgroup stream belong to the track identified by Track Alias (see [Section 10.1](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#track-alias)) and the Subgroup indicated by 'Group ID' and Subgroup ID in the SUBGROUP_HEADER.

"in the SUBGROUP_HEADER" -> "present in and/or inferred for the SUBGROUP_HEADER"

> {
>   Object ID Delta (i),
>   [Extensions (..)],
>   Object Payload Length (i),
>   [Object Status (i)],
>   Object Payload (..),
> }
> [Figure 33](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#figure-33): [MOQT Subgroup Object Fields](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#name-moqt-subgroup-object-fields)
> 

"Object Payload (..)" -> "[Object Payload (..)]"

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Sect. 10.4.3:

> - the Object ID is one greater than the previous Object sent on this Subgroup stream.
> 
> - the Object was received on the same upstream Subgroup stream as the previously sent Object on the downstream Subgroup stream, with no other Objects in between.
>  
> - it knows all Object IDs between the current and previous Object IDs on the Subgroup stream belong to different Subgroups or do not exist.
 
Change "the" in the beginning to "The" (for both the first two bullet items), and "it" in the beginning of the third bullet item to "It".

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Sect. 10.4.3:

> A relay MAY treat receipt of EndOfGroup, GroupDoesNotExist, or EndOfTrack objects as a signal to close corresponding streams even if the FIN has not arrived, as further objects on the stream would be a protocol violation.

What is a "GroupDoesNotExist object"? This seems not defined anywhere in the document. Was it intended to be "ObjectDoesNotExist object"? If so, it is actually correct to say that "A relay MAY treat receipt of DoesNotExist objects as a signal to close corresponding streams even if the FIN has not arrived, as further objects on the stream would be a protocol violation."?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> What is a "GroupDoesNotExist object"? 

It was removed a while ago and this place was missed.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Sect. 10.4.4:

> {
>   Group ID (i),
>   Subgroup ID (i),
>   Object ID (i),
>   Publisher Priority (8),
>   Extensions (..),
>   Object Payload Length (i),
>   [Object Status (i)],
>   Object Payload (..),
> }
> [Figure 35](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#figure-35): [MOQT Fetch Object Fields](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#name-moqt-fetch-object-fields)

"Object Payload (..)" -> "[Object Payload (..)]"

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Sect. 11.1:

> - An Object contains more than one instance of Prior Group ID Gap
> - A Group contains more than one Object with different values for Prior Group ID Gap
> - An Object has a Prior Group ID Gap larger than the Group ID
> - An endpoint receives an Object with a Prior Group ID Gap covering an Object it previously received
> - An endpoint receives an Object with a Group ID within a previously communicated gap

Add a period '.' in the end of each of the above bullet items, which are complete sentences.

Sect. 11.2:

> - An Object contains an Immutable Extensions header that contains another Immutable Extensions key
> - A Key-Value-Pair cannot be parsed

Similarly, add a period '.' in the end of each of the above bullet items, which are complete sentences.

Sect. 11.3:

> - An Object contains more than one instance of Prior Object ID Gap
> - An Object has a Prior Object ID Gap larger than the Object ID
> - An endpoint receives an Object with a Prior Object ID Gap covering an Object it previously received
> - An endpoint receives an Object with an Object ID within a previously communicated gap

Similarly, add a period '.' in the end of each of the above bullet items, which are complete sentences.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> "Object Payload (..)" -> "[Object Payload (..)]"

I go back and forth, since (..) can also be 0 bytes, and the payload length is included.  But we should be consistent in all the sections in any case.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Sect. 12.1:

> The publisher and subscriber MUST cancel a stream, preferably the lowest priority, after reaching a resource limit.

"preferably the lowest priority" -> "preferably the one with the lowest priority"

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Sect. 12.2 (Timeouts): 

> Each implementation is expected to set its own limits.

"limits" -> "timeouts"

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body: OK, I am done with this round of review (of -v14). Let me make a PR to include changes for these minor editorial issues.

issues.title: Use of the word "subscription" in abstract and other sections than 5.1
issues.author: yekuiwang
issues.body:
As discussed in PR #1222, the intro and other sections in the draft might need updating regarding the use of the word "subscription", which should mean "a flow of objects initiated via the SUBSCRIBE or PUBLISH messages".

For example, in the very first instance of "subscription" in the abstract: "MOQT allows a producer of media to publish data and have it consumed via subscription by a multiplicity of endpoints." This sentence gives me an impression that it covers all means of consumption of published data, thus it includes fetches. There are many other places like this in the draft. Therefore, clarifications, or maybe a definition of "subscription", should be made/added, such that readers won't have confusions.

issues.title: Move the sentence on "an Object MUST be sent according to its Object Forwarding Preference" to the relay section

issues.title: Reconsider using Object Delta Value in Subgroup Object
issues.author: TimEvens
issues.body:
Using Object Delta Value might save a few bytes in wire/transmission, but it comes at a cost...

## Proposal: Use Object ID and not Object Delta Value

The current delta value approach introduces mandatory processing requirements for all relays and subscribers. Object ID derivation becomes susceptible to errors if largest group information or GAP extension headers are missing or not available.

The wire format efficiency gains are quantifiably limited. Even in scenarios with long-lived groups, practical limitations suggest that object IDs rarely exceed a 4-byte varint value of 1,073,741,823. For example, a video stream at 60 FPS would require continuous transmission for over 200 days before requiring 8 bytes.

If the MOQT specification defined a maximum object ID value or implemented maximum object ID negotiation, the delta approach would only save 3 bytes per object. 

The specification requires updates regarding object status, specifically where it states "If the Object ID is 0, it indicates there are no Objects in this Group," as this becomes a derived value with stream objects.

Based on the 90/10 principle (where 90% of object IDs require 4 bytes or less), the additional complexity and processing requirements of the delta approach may not justify the minimal bandwidth savings, particularly given the architectural differences between datagram and stream handling of object IDs.

## TL;DR

> Every MOQT receiving relay will have to derive the object ID for every object in the stream

Currently when using `Object ID` the receiver did not have parse extension headers to fan-out or to cache. It was optional if the relay needed to parse them or not. Even if it did parse them, it may only do that on selected objects, not all of them.  In order to derive the object ID, the receiver MUST now parse the OBJECT GAP extension header in every object within a stream. It MUST also now use the PUBLISH largest location information to derive the object ID. 

The value of changing the MOQT message from number of extension headers to length of extension headers so that they could be skipped is lost.

> Every MOQT subscriber will have to derive the object Id for every object in the stream

Not all subscribers need the object Id, but it was useful for the application to know the sequence of objects. It was easy for the subscriber to issue a standalone fetch at any time because it had the group and object ID info from either objects received or from the subscribe OK largest location information. Now every subscriber that intends to use fetch or other features of MOQT will need to derive and maintain the object Id. 


> Impact of processing every object extension header

Pipeline forwarding of objects is the process of being able to forward data immediately without having to pause to parse, inspect and/or modify data before it can be forwarded. Start of stream header significantly improved forward efficiency for low latency fan-out per relay hop. A relay in the middle would no longer add more than a few microseconds of delay, vs having to store and forward hop-by-hop.  

With delta value, the relay MUST now parse every object extension header to detect if there is a gap and to store the object ID in cache for retrieval.

Parsing the extension headers is a store and forward operation that adds additional latency, especially when considering an application that heavily uses extension headers. It's not known by the relay that the extensions header has an object GAP extension header, so it has to process them all.  99% of the time, there will be no object gap, resulting in a lot of wasted processing.
 

> Cache Impact

Caching used the group and object IDs to uniquely identify an object for a track when storing. This made it easy to retrieve information from cache. No extra processing was required by the relay to provide this information for caching. Now the relay MUST derive the object ID for caching. 

> Subscribe OK and Track Status OK need to be synchronous operations

Before this change, the subscribe OK and track status OK messages were asynchronous to the subscribe data flow. They did not guarantee that the very next object to a subscriber would be plus one of the object Id conveyed in the largest location information.  Using `object delta value changes this operation to be synchronous, where a subscriber data will need to be delayed upon subscribe OK and for every track status request, otherwise the information provided in those responses
may result in the wrong object ID being derived by the subscriber.

> Lingering subscribers
  
Lingering subscribers provide essential functionality in peering scenarios where relay connections may not be synchronized or when publishers may connect at different times.  This is particularly valuable when two relays are not connected at the time of subscription, or when relay peering connections are established asynchronously, or when a publisher reconnects. This design ensures subscriber stability during publisher reconnections or intermediate relay peering connection changes.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> In distributed architectures, relays are typically deployed behind network/UDP load balancers or discovered via DNS-SD or similar mechanisms, supporting both anycast and unicast. When a publisher disconnects and reconnects, load balancing may direct it to a different relay. This new relay lacks historical context regarding the publisher's previous group/object IDs. Additionally, the new relay has no cached data, and peering connections may not be pre-established at the time of the publisher's connection.

During publisher reconnection scenarios, the MOQT specification should explicitly require that publishers either:
1. Initialize at object ID zero in a new group, or
2. Include an object GAP extension header to indicate the delta from 0

Furthermore, publishers must initiate a new group upon connection establishment and cannot resume a previous group during reconnection. This requirement presents implementation challenges since the publisher may lack information about the previous group ID, and the newly connected relay may not have access to the group ID history known to other relays and subscribers.

In peering reconnection scenarios, the complexity increases because publishers do not generate GAP extension headers, as from their perspective, no gap exists. The discontinuity occurs only in downstream relays where the connection was interrupted. To maintain data consistency, relays must now implement GAP extension headers across all tracks when re-establishing peering sessions. In large-scale deployments with tens of thousands of tracks, this requirement significantly impacts performance, as relays must:
1. Identify affected tracks
2. Calculate appropriate deltas
3. Modify original objects to include gap extension headers

For new peering connections, additional challenges arise when subscribers lack accurate largest location information for in-progress groups. This scenario requires relays to implement the same GAP extension header process described above. A significant architectural challenge emerges when considering state maintenance for disconnected peering sessions, particularly with relays behind NAT. Upon accepting a peering connection, relays create session state that typically gets cleared on disconnection. This state includes critical tracking information about group and object IDs for all tracks transmitted through that session.

The `object delta value` requirements introduce additional processing overhead and latency implications.

>
