issues.title: Does PUBLISH implicitly PUBLISH_NAMESPACE?
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
If a relay receives `PUBLISH namespace=(a), name=(b)` , can it also route a `SUBSCRIBE namespace=(a), name=(c)` to this publisher?

I assume the answer is *no* but @kixelated was of a different opinion.  

Related: #1349.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
As the draft is written, `PUBLISH` does not imply `PUBLISH_NAMESPACE`.

The ramification is that routing is now based on `namespace + track` instead of just `namespace`. This isn't inherently a bad thing, but it does increase the size of routing tables that need to be synchronized across a CDN.

It could be a problem if clients `PUBLISH` hundreds of tracks individually. If they were to `PUBLISH_NAMESPACE` first then it would reduce the load on the CDN. 

It mostly caught me by surprise because I thought the entire point of separating the `namespace` and `track` tuple was for routing. I'm not really sure what's the distinction between the two now, especially if routing is based on namespace prefix (not a full match).

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> The ramification is that routing is now based on namespace + track instead of just namespace

In my implementation, matching is based _first_ on Full Track Name -- a SUBSCRIBE matches an established subscription for that Track.  This is true regardless if the upstream subscription was established by a previous upstream SUBSCRIBE or PUBLISH -- it's symmetric.

If there isn't an active subscription, I route based on Namespace.  

So I dispute the statement that "routing" is based on Full Track Name.

> It could be a problem if clients PUBLISH hundreds of tracks individually. If they were to PUBLISH_NAMESPACE first then it would reduce the load on the CDN.

This is true -- if you have a large track set and expect sparse subscriptions, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE is better.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
@afrind that works for a single relay yes, but not for a CDN.

If a relay receives a SUBSCRIBE, it needs:
- check if any other relay has a matching PUBLISH (namespace+track), then SUBSCRIBE to it.
- check if any other relay has a matching PUBLISH_NAMESPACE (namespace prefix), then SUBSCRIBE to it.
- (optional) check if a relay closer to the origin has a matching SUBSCRIBE (namespace+track), then SUBSCRIBE to it.

In fact to support multi-publisher, all relays that receive PUBLISH or PUBLISH_NAMESPACE from a client need to be treated as separate publishers.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Relay to relay is explicitly out of scope for MOQT:

> While PUBLISH_NAMESPACE indicates to relays how to connect publishers and subscribers, it is not a full-fledged routing protocol and does not protect against loops and other phenomena. In particular, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE **SHOULD NOT** be used to find paths through richly connected networks of relays

I think you can write a relay<->relay system that maybe emits PUBLISH_NAMESPACE to other _relays_ when it receives a track in the namespace.  Then the regular multipublisher rules tell you to subscribe to all of them.  Some could fail with TRACK_NOT_FOUND, but at least one will succeed if the track is there.

Back to the original issue, I will add a sentence to the doc making it clear there's no implicit namespace publish in MOQT.

comments.author: TimEvens
comments.body:
I recommend you reviewing https://github.com/Quicr/laps/blob/main/docs/relay-protocol.md. The complexity is reduced. The edge origin relay facilitates matching subscriptions to establish forwarding planes of data.  The origin and subsequent relays implement their own logic to best deliver the data to the subscribing edge relays.  

Please correct me if I'm wrong, but the issue herein is asking if a PUBLISH namespace tuple should result in subscribes being sent by matching the `PUBLISH` namespace, sans the name matching...

IMHO, absolutely not.  

If the publisher intends to receive X names for a match on the namespace prefix (matching the tuples), then it should issue a `PUBLISH_NAMESAPCE` message.  This will trigger the relay to forward X names to the matching namespace prefix tuples. A publisher client that publishes using `PUBLISH` will result in exact matching of namespace and name only. The relay **MUST NOT** perform prefix matching of the `PUBLISH` namespace.  For example, the client issues a `PUBLISH` with namespace `1,2,3` with name `abc`.  A relay **WILL NOT** send a subscribe for namespace =`1,2,3` name = `xyz`.   Only if the client issued a `PUBLISH_NAMESPACE` = `1,2,3` would the the subscribe be sent to the publisher for name = `xyz`.   

In other words, only `PUBLISH_NAMESPACE` state triggers prefix matching of forwarding subscribe for X names.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Thanks Tim.  I think we're all in agreement and we'll make it a bit more explicit in the doc.

issues.title: Subscribing to the start of the current Group could be optimized
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
Assuming Joining FETCH stays as is, there is an optimization to joining at the current Group that I believe is worth considering.

Just because there is a Largest Object, doesn't mean all Objects less than that are available.  This means that a Joining FETCH could be blocked waiting for Objects the Relay has never seen.

For example, if there was a base layer and a temporal enhancement layer, and the base layer was higher priority, a Relay might have all of the base layer and none of the enhancement layer.  If a Joining FETCH came in, the Subscriber would receive the first Object in the base layer and then be stuck there until the enhancement layer started arriving.

In some cases, this is just underutilizing the available bandwidth, but in other cases if the enhancement layer doesn't arrive within the delivery timeout, the playback can't begin.

In contrast, if both the Joining FETCH and SUBSCRIBE start at the beginning of the current Group, the FETCH could skip over any Objects (PR #1331) that are not yet available and then they'd be delivered via SUBSCRIBE.

The farther back in time the FETCH is, the less likely this is an issue, but I think it could be a substantial issue for the "Join at the current Group" case that we expect to be extremely common.

comments.author: TimEvens
comments.body:
We use JOINING FETCH within the current group. Knowing the number of objects per group, if the count is less than X, we issue a joining fetch, typically targeting the current group. However, if the current group lacks the start object (e.g., iframe), the fetch is ineffective.

Groups usually operate on intervals, so waiting for the next group is expected. For example, a new group typically starts within 5 seconds, resolving any issues. In some cases, groups are long-lived and do not start a new group until explicitly instructed. This is where the NEW GROUP REQUEST comes into play-we trigger it to reduce delays.

Clients attempt to request objects within the group to obtain the start object and all current group objects, provided the start object is less than a few seconds old. Requesting a full group is often unnecessary since a new group will start shortly (often in less than a second). If a new group is imminent, clients wait for it. For long-lived groups, the NEW GROUP REQUEST parameter is used to initiate a new group.

I agree that the local relay often does not have all requested objects cached, especially considering load balancers and other factors. When a subscriber relay starts consuming with a new subscriber, it likely has no cache. Consequently, it must forward the FETCH request directly to the publisher to solicit unicast feedback, priming its cache to serve the requester and handle subsequent fetches.

In my opinion, cache distribution can be improved by implementing regional distributed caches. These regional caches could serve fetch requests for many horizontally scaled relays within a region. For example, if 100 relays are fronted by a network load balancer, none may have the cache, but a regional cache could. This would allow each relay to pull published content efficiently from the regional cache.

Determining when to engage the regional cache engine to start caching content involves challenges such as authorization and end-to-end encryption, which are beyond the scope of MOQT. Addressing this would be better suited for a new draft.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
I just implemented joining fetch and yes it will undoubtedly hurt startup time*.

**assumed**: The library ensures that _subgroups_ are delivered in the original order to the application.

1. The library has to buffer SUBSCRIBE objects if `group == largest` until the joining FETCH **ends**. We're blocked on FETCH delivering the start of the subgroup before SUBSCRIBE can continue to deliver the end.
2. The library has to buffer SUBSCRIBE objects if `group != largest` until the joining FETCH **starts**. We don't know if (1) applies until FETCH_OK or the first FETCH object.
3. Like Ian said, SUBSCRIBE delivers subgroups independently while FETCH introduces HoLB, aggravating (1).

\* compared to the old SUBSCRIBE or a hypothetical `FilterType = LargestGroup`

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I'm going to close this as a duplicate of #1023 unless someone can articulate some problem that is different.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I think the best solution is for apps that want to minimize join latency and have layered tracks -- apply a subgroup=0 filter to the joining fetch.  The other issue lists several other mechanisms.  #1331 offers another possible alternative which is to let the publisher skip over "unknown" elements in a FETCH (we'd probably want a subscriber signal).  Other possible approaches are listed in 1023 -- number objects differently, so subgroups use contiguous Object ID ranges, or use different tracks.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: I believe adding a "LargestGroup" to SUBSCRIBE can mostly solve this issue along with #1331 because then the FETCH can skip Objects the relay hasn't seen yet and they'll arrive later via SUBSCRIBE.

comments.body:
> I think you can start sending Subscribe Objects while completing the FETCH if there's available bandwidth. This could happen if it takes time to start the FETCH.

Yep yep but you have to be careful about flow control as it risks a deadlock. The subscriber can choose to buffer undecodable SUBSCRIBE data within the QUIC stream while it waits for FETCH to complete.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: There's not an inherent flow control deadlock possibility in MOQT, I don't think?  My current strategy is to never buffer subscribe data in QUIC or MOQT.  That goes straight to the app and if they can't handle it they need to unsubscribe or die.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
> There's not an inherent flow control deadlock possibility in MOQT, I don't think? My current strategy is to never buffer subscribe data in QUIC or MOQT. That goes straight to the app and if they can't handle it they need to unsubscribe or die.

Again this is assuming that your library flushes subgroups in order to the application. If it flushes objects in an arbitrary order then you're fine... because it's been offloaded to the application.

When doing a joining fetch, the library needs to buffer incoming SUBSCRIBE data until the FETCH finishes. It needs to buffer somewhere, perhaps not reading from the QUIC stream (flow controlled) or allocated within the library (can grow unbounded). The deadlock can happen with the easier first approach because MAX_DATA consumed by FETCH can block SUBSCRIBE progress.

The inherent difficulty is that joining fetch splits QUIC streams into two halves that may be transmitted independently, but there's an implicit dependency between the two halves.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> When doing a joining fetch, the library needs to buffer incoming SUBSCRIBE data until the FETCH finishes.

That's a library implementation choice, but not the one I'm making, at least not right now.  When the app joins, the fetch and subscribe data get delivered as they arrive.  In order delivery is a lie told by a buffering receiver.

> The inherent difficulty is that joining fetch splits QUIC streams into two halves that may be transmitted independently, but there's an implicit dependency between the two halves.

I see what you are saying here. If there's only subgroup in the group, and that's the only one you want, it now comes in two streams instead of one.  If there are > 1 subgroups or datagrams, they are already coming out of order, so it's an application concern already.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
> > When doing a joining fetch, the library needs to buffer incoming SUBSCRIBE data until the FETCH finishes.
> 
> That's a library implementation choice, but not the one I'm making, at least not right now. When the app joins, the fetch and subscribe data get delivered as they arrive. In order delivery is a lie told by a buffering receiver.

That's certainly a choice. IMO the intent behind subgroups is that they map to a QUIC stream for consistent ordering even across relays. Your API obviously doesn't need to provide that service, just like a QUIC library could emit raw STREAM frames to the application. But something has to buffer when delta encoding is involved because parsing must be in `object_id` order.

> I see what you are saying here. If there's only subgroup in the group, and that's the only one you want, it now comes in two streams instead of one. If there are > 1 subgroups or datagrams, they are already coming out of order, so it's an application concern already.

Yep, the library could ensure that objects within an individual subgroup are delivered in order because that's guaranteed 99% of the time. Multiple subgroups will be delivered out of order because they're over multiple QUIC streams and the application has to adjust. 

Like Ian points out, the only exception is during a joining FETCH at the start of a SUBSCRIBE. Objects will actually be delivered in order across all subgroups until some seemingly arbitrary (to the application) point at which point they'll go back to normal. This almost certainly introduces some HoLB because the application MUST be able to parse subgroups independently, but they're being forced onto the same FETCH stream.

Well the other exception might be datagrams but I would hope each one is part of a unique subgroup (ex. object_id == subgroup_id) to maintain the property that objects within a subgroup are delivered in order (because there's only one object). But it doesn't matter, datagrams can be their own thing.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: One related, but slightly different issue I forgot about (and @kixelated reminded me of) was that FETCH Objects have to go in order, so if the start is Group 5, and Group 6+ are in cache, you can't start sending Group 6 until you've sent 5.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
1) You can now start sending at group 6 by marking group 5 as Unknown.
2) Either you need 5 or you don't.  You can use descending if you want 6 before 5, but otherwise, you can fetch 6 while you are playing 5.  Or you can make two fetches.
3) This issue is about subscribing to the start of the current group, which can't be 5 in your example.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
I came up with another issue with JOINING FETCH while replying to @suhasHere .

**tl;dr** when using subscriber priorities, a JOINING FETCH will never be deprioritized, even if there's a new group.

Let's suppose we issue a hypothetical `SUBSCRIBE filter=LargestGroup order=DESC`. We'll download/decode the current group at network speed. However, if the next group starts, we'll prioritize it and potentially drop the old group we partially downloaded.

Today, we would issue a `SUBSCRIBE filter=LargestObject order=DESC priority=6` and `JOINING FETCH priority=7`. The priority is important, otherwise undecodable frames will arrive before their dependencies. However, if the next group starts, it will be lower priority than the FETCH until it completes. Basically it's not possible to skip the tail of the current group until we've reached `LargestObject` from SUBSCRIBE_OK.

----

A concrete example, the largest object is 1.5s into a 2s GoP, so it's almost done. Let's say the the media is encoded at 3Mb/s and our network speed is 4.5Mb/s. 

It takes 1s to download the JOINING FETCH (1.5s of media). At which point, the live playhead is already 0.5s into the next group. Now SUBSCRIBE is the highest priority request and will start delivering that 0.5s of the next group. Which IDK takes 0.33s or something for a final TTV of 1.33s.

But if we did a LargestGroup SUBSCRIBE, the TTV would be 0.5s. We would spend that time downloading 0.75s of the largest group, but the instant there's a new group, the SUBSCRIBE immediately prioritizes the next group instead and we're immediately at the live playhead.

---

I think you could work around this with JOINING FETCH by relying on publisher priorities. But I don't really feel like consulting the draft to see how FETCH/SUBSCRIBE priorities are supposed to interact.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Since @kixelated opened #1614, this issue remains fundamentally about Head-of-line blocking on missing enhancement layers.  This is addressed with FILL_TIMEOUT=0.

issues.title: FETCH doesn't use `track_alias`
issues.author: kixelated
issues.body:
Seems inconsistent that `SUBSCRIBE` uses `track_alias` and we need buffer streams until `SUBSCRIBE_OK`, but the same is not true for `FETCH`.

I probably shouldn't mention it because `request_id` is much easier to implement, but too late now.

comments.author: TimEvens
comments.body: I brought this up with @suhasHere but later realized that fetch is limited in design to only request a range. This could easily result in multiple parallel fetches for a series of ranges.   Request ID is need to distinguish the received content. For example, I want to get objects 10-20, 19-32, and 45-49... I have to issue multiple fetch requests for those ranges. Each of which would have their own fetch request id. At the same time I might be receiving data with the track alias. Data received from subscribe is distinguishable from fetch data received by type, but what range is being provided isn't so clear with fetch.  Utilizing request ID clears up the requested ranged.  For example, I know that stream X is for range 10 - 20, Y is for 19-32, and Z is for 45-49.  Alternatively, we could consume streams that start with a fetch header and reconcile the ranges to the request, but IMO it does seem to be more succinct to have request ID in this case instead of using track alias.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
That's good enough justification for me. You can technically reverse engineer which FETCH_OBJECT applies to which FETCH based on the start/end location but please no.

But I will point out that the same rationale applies to UNSUBSCRIBE+SUBSCRIBE. It doesn't really matter now, but if something like filters get added to the draft, it's reallllly useful to map objects to subscriptions.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
We went to avoid having both sides of the connection run the filter.  The receiver can just use the request ID.

FETCH can't use the range of the object to know which FETCH it belongs to, because there can be concurrent overlapping FETCHes, and ordering is very important for gap detection.

I'm not aware of any requests to change the current restriction of one subscription per Track.

Closing this.

issues.title: [Editorial] LARGEST_OBJECT can also be present in REQUEST_OK response to TRACK_STATUS.
issues.author: sandarsh
issues.body:
The LARGEST_OBJECT parameter (Parameter Type 0x9) MAY appear in SUBSCRIBE_OK, PUBLISH or in REQUEST_OK in response to SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE. It is a length-prefixed Location structure (see [Section 1.4.1](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-15.html#location-structure)) containing the largest Location in the Track observed by the sending endpoint (see [Section 5.1.2](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-15.html#subscription-filters). If Objects have been published on this Track the Publisher MUST include this parameter.


The above mentions only SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE. 
Should it also mention TRACK_STATUS?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Good catch.  Do you want to make a PR @sandarsh ?

comments.author: sandarsh
comments.body:
> Good catch. Do you want to make a PR [@sandarsh](https://github.com/sandarsh) ?

Will do!

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Closed by #1367

issues.title: Joining FETCH requires an "established" session
issues.author: kixelated
issues.body:
Editorial mostly. **Emphasis** is mine. Thanks Lorenzo.

https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-15.html#joining-fetches
> A Joining Fetch is associated with a Subscribe request by specifying the Request ID of an **Established** subscription.


https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-15.html#section-5.1
> The publisher either accepts or rejects the subscription using SUBSCRIBE_OK or REQUEST_ERROR. Once either of these sequences is successful, the subscription moves to the **Established** state and can be updated by the subscriber using SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE. 

This means it's not valid to pipeline a joining FETCH after a SUBSCRIBE, instead the subscriber has to wait for SUBSCRIBE_OK (transitioned to Established). That's obviously not the intent.

comments.author: lminiero
comments.body:
I agree that changing the requirement for Joining FETCH to be something like

> A Joining Fetch is associated with a Subscribe request by specifying the Request ID of an *Established or Pending* subscription.

would do the trick. Not sure if this means adding text to clarify that a Joining FETCH may not get a response right away, and that if you address a pending subscrption and that subscription fails, then the Joining FETCH should fail as well.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Heh we also just found this too.  It should be `Established` or `Pending (subscriber)`

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> if you address a pending subscrption and that subscription fails, then the Joining FETCH should fail as well.

I would expect if the SUBSCRIBE failed, the FETCH will fail because of this:

> If a publisher receives a Joining Fetch with a Request ID that does not correspond to an existing Subscribe in the same session...

But we should clarify this too.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body: I imagine the SUBSCRIBE could fail but the FETCH succeed if the track has ended?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I expect the publisher to tear down subscriber state when it sends REQUEST_ERROR.  Therefore a joining FETCH cannot succeed, since it needs the state of the subscribe to resolve the fetch parameters.

issues.title: If you can't deliver an entire Group, should you send any Objects for a Track?
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
There are times when you are certain you cannot deliver the entire Track/Group due to bandwidth constraints.  The draft today is written with the idea that you'd send what you could according to priority, but I think there are cases that's just going to risk causing congestion for other Subscriptions and delay their delivery.

I think there are potentially valid use cases for either behavior, so we might want a way to specify what you want?  Alternatively, we could add text pointing this out and leave it at that.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: So you want a GROUP_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT, and the publisher tries to estimate how long it will take to send the entire group?

comments.author: gwendalsimon
comments.body:
Shouldn't it be at the level of subgroup?
I thought that the subgroup would be the concept where we put together inter-related objects, although Groups are mainly join points. When I present MOQ, I often explain that subgroup is a key MOQ feature because it is where you can use QUIC stream reset and cancels to a specific set of consecutive video frames if you know for sure that these frames will arrive too late.

comments.author: wilaw
comments.body:
> There are times when you are certain you cannot deliver the entire Track/Group due to bandwidth constraints. The draft today is written with the idea that you'd send what you could according to priority, but I think there are cases that's just going to risk causing congestion for other Subscriptions and delay their delivery.

I don't believe it should be the publishers' concern. It should faithfully execute the prioritization instructions which were given to it by the subscriber. If the subscriber prioritizes tracks poorly, resulting in congestion, that congestion is a feedback mechanism to the subscriber that they should adjust their prioritization strategy. It is important for a control system that there is a deterministic output for the input actions of the initiator of the traffic, which is the subscriber. If the relay starts taking de-coupled actions, based on its own adjudged inability to deliver a group, it can lead to an unstable system with worse consequence for both parties.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: Thanks for the feedback.  It sounds like this might be a case where you only want the behavior I'm describing if you're doing some flavor of server-side ABR and you know that two (or more) Tracks are alternatives and there's no need in delivering them both?

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: If we were going to make a change, I was thinking it'd be something as simple as a bool for "FullGroupsOnlyPlease".  Somewhat similar to HTTP extensible priorities where you can indicate if you want incremental delivery or not.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: This sounds like an extension to me, or something to be tackled with publisher side ABR, which maybe should also be an extension.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Unparking for Boulder ABR discussions

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
Text in the current draft:

Not sending data if you don't think you'll be able to deliver the entire Object: Under the DELIVERY TIMEOUT Parameter:

> Publishers SHOULD consider whether the entire Object can likely be
> successfully delivered within the timeout period before sending any data
> for that Object, taking into account priorities, congestion control, and
> any other relevant information.

Not sending data if it might prevent higher priority data from being sent in the near future: Under the Data Forwarding prioritization section, there is text addressing reserving the congestion window:

> A publisher might not utilize the entire available congestion window,
> session flow control, or all available streams for lower
> priority Objects if it expects higher priority Objects will be available to send
> in the near future or it wants to reserve some bandwidth for control messages.

ABR will need the idea of not sending a Group/Track if there's not enough bandwidth, but in MoQ Transport, I think the above might b sufficient?

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: I'm inclined to close this with no action right now or declare it as NotTransport since it's something Sender side ABR would need to do.

issues.title: Do publishers need to remember that a subgroup received STOP_SENDING?
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
Because subscribers can join a subscription midway through a group, my fan-out logic will always open a new stream if an object is published on a subgroup that doesn't have a stream yet.

But what happens when the subscriber sends STOP_SENDING?  After RESET_STREAM, does the publisher need to hold state that it should never send another object in this subgroup to this subscriber?

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body: In that case, the subscriber has indicated that it is no longer interested in receiving that subgroup, then after acknowledging by sending RESET_STREAM (or  RESET_STREAM_AT), the publisher does need to honor "the agreement" and should never send another object in this subgroup to this subscriber, unless the subscriber indicates its interest on this subgroup again.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Just to use a concrete example, let's assume the following:

```
S->P: SUBSCRIBE
P->S: Subgroup 0, object 0
S->P: STOP_SENDING sg=0
P->S: RESET_STREAM sg-0
...
S->P: SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE Fwd=0
...
S->P: SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE Fwd=1
P: Publishes sg=0, object 1
```

Does sending a SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE with fwd=1 constitute "subscriber indicating interest in this subgroup again"?

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
Interesting example. 

Usually, I thought SG0 would be the most important SG, thus typically the subscriber either sends STOP_SENDING for one or more highest SGs or it sends UNSUBSCRIBE. 

Therefore, probably the example would make more sense when changing sg0 to sgN (with N > 0, say 7). With that, I would assume if the subscriber sends STOP_SENDING sg=7, it jus says that it is not interested in sg7, but still interested in the lower SGs. Then sending updates of Fwd should only indicate its preference of pausing or resuming receiving of interested SGs.

On the other hand, how can a subscriber indicate that it changed its mind and now is again interested in SG7? Currently there is no way of doing that I guess?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Yes sg=7 is a better example.

> On the other hand, how can a subscriber indicate that it changed its mind and now is again interested in SG7? Currently there is no way of doing that I guess?

Unsubscribe and re-subscribe is the only way maybe.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
> Unsubscribe and re-subscribe is the only way maybe.

Hmm, and that is probably OK for such a corner use case.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
`STOP_SENDING` is slightly better than `SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE` alone because the subscriber will immediately free up flow control, rather than wait for a `RESET_STREAM` in response to the `SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE`.

I don't see any benefit to transmitting the tail of a reset subgroup. The subscriber obviously doesn't want it, and even if it did, it would need to issue a FETCH to populate the gap.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Discussed on 12/1 Interim:

* Sending STOP_SENDING is like adding an implicit (subgroup != current subgroup ID) filter -- the publisher won't send any more.
* Reset streams for other reasons sometimes work like this (eg: Delivery Timeout)
* Resetting streams because of a subgroup discontinuity (caused by a filter or other weirdness) does *not* work like this -- eg: if I subscribe with a filter like Object ID != 7, I should get 0-6+RESET, then 8-10+FIN.

issues.title: WebTransport Section Reference Incorrect
issues.author: gmarzot
issues.body:
Draft-15 here indicates: 

  MOQT uses ALPN in QUIC and "WT-Available-Protocols" in WebTransport
   ([WebTransport], Section 3.4) to perform version negotiation.

But it looks like the relevant section is:  ([WebTransport], Section 3.3)

[[WebTransport], Section 3.3](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-webtrans-http3-14.html#section-3.3)

issues.title: Does the Client have to speak first (should the control stream be a pair of unis)?
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body: When establishing a session, particularly over QUIC directly without 0-RTT, the Server can speak first.  The current text indicates the client always speaks first, but I'm not sure if that's a requirement or just a convenient mental model?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I thought #242 was tracking something like this, but it was closed by #499, possibly inadvertently.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
The definitions of Client and Server in the MOQT draft are as follows:

Client: The party initiating a Transport Session.
Server: The party accepting an incoming Transport Session.

Thus, in MOQT draft isn't by definition that the Client speaks first when establishing a session, as what speaks first is defined as the Client?

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body: Those are not necessarily the same.  For instance, in TLS (1.3), the client initiates the session, but the server can send application data first (since it's the first party that has data keys).

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body: Well, in the TLS spec there are no such (weird IMHO) definitions of "client" and "server" as in the MOQT draft.  Actually, in TLS there are no definitions of "client" and "server", which imply that these two words are used in their plain meanings therein.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I think this issue is about whether the control stream should be a client-initiated bidirectional stream, as in the current draft, or a pair of unidirectional streams, as in HTTP/3. Decoupling the streams means that the server can send its SERVER_SETUP negotiation parameters (and non-extended control messages) as soon as the TLS handshake is complete from its side, even if it has not received CLIENT_SETUP.

It does mandate a certain kind of extension negotiation, which is essentially declarative (I support X, Y and Z) and has deterministic algorithms for each peer to run based on what it sent and what it received.  The current design allows the server to wait to see the client setup before indicating what extensions it wants to use.

comments.author: LPardue
comments.body:
https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8446#section-1.1

> client:  The endpoint initiating the TLS connection.

> server:  The endpoint that did not initiate the TLS connection.

comments.author: yekuiwang
comments.body:
> https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8446#section-1.1
> 
> > client:  The endpoint initiating the TLS connection.
> 
> > server:  The endpoint that did not initiate the TLS connection.

Oh, thanks! I looked at https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5246.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
I think with WebTransport, the server should speak first? Meanwhile with QUIC 1-RTT then yeah the client should speak first.

Another option is similar to HTTP/3 SETTINGS, where both sides would open a control stream simultaneously. It would mean no need to shard request ID by client/server, but I guess that might go away anyway.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: In QUIC 1-RTT the server can send in 0.5-RTT, I think.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
> In QUIC 1-RTT the server can send in 0.5-RTT, I think.

I think you're right? 

Either way with ALPN, the server should probably speak first because it knows the selected version first.

issues.title: Can a namespace tuple have zero bytes
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body:
say I have a namespace with two tuples and the second has the byte "a". Is it legal for the first tuple to have zero bytes. 



I would propose that this not be legal because it probably is a mistake but I can see arguments either way. Regardless of which way we go on this, I think we should mention it in the spec just so implementers are not surprised.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: This is a sub-case mentioned in #1041

issues.title: Text on reordering and Objects going from DNE to Exists is incorrect
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
While writing #1342, it was observed that the following text doesn't seem correct anymore.

"Note that due to reordering, an implementation can receive an Object after
receiving an indication that the Object in question does not exist.  The
endpoint SHOULD NOT cache or forward the object in this case."

This text might not be needed?

comments.author: sharmafb
comments.body: Why is this section of text incorrect?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
There are cases where a publisher is clearly breaking the object model, that is malformed, e.g.:

10,0, 10,1, 10,2, END_OF_GROUP, 10,4 <-- This is malformed

But here's a scenario that seems legit:

S->P: SUBSCRIBE
P->S: SUB_OK
Publisher creates object 0,0, sends it on a subgroup, then "forgets" it.
Subgroup delayed in network
S->P: FETCH 0,0
P->S: FETCH_OK, Empty Response -> 0,0 does not exist
0,0 arrives at S -> this is not malformed.

Our text is currently says both things and we need to clear this up.

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body:
So in the example above does not seem correct 

"P->S: FETCH_OK, Empty Response -> 0,0 does not exist"

Is not a valid response. That is a protocol violation. If a an original publisher "forgets" if an object exits or not, it can not send a response that claims it does not exist.

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body: It does not "forget" if the object exists or not, it "forgets" the object (evicts it from its local memory), meaning it no longer exists.

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body: I do not think there are any valid situations where a relay or subscriber can be get a definitive answer that an object does not exist and then later find out the object does exist. Similarly there is no situations where all the entities are correct following the protocol and get and object exists and later get a result that the object does not exist.

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body:
> It does not "forget" if the object exists or not, it "forgets" the object (evicts it from its local memory), meaning it no longer exists.

It's fine for it to do that, but in that case it must not claim the object exists or does not exist in future responses.

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body:
> I do not think there are any valid situations where a relay or subscriber can be get a definitive answer that an object does not exist and then later find out the object does exist.

The draft does explicitly state that "does not exists" state is permanent.

> Similarly there is no situations where all the entities are correct following the protocol and get and object exists and later get a result that the object does not exist.

This explicitly contradicts [the current text of the draft](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-19.html#section-2.1-3):

> From the perspective of a subscriber or a cache, an Object can be in three possible states:
>
> 1. The Object is known to not exist. This state is permanent.  All signals that an Object does not exist are authoritative.
> 2. The Object is known to exist. From this state, **it can transition to not existing**, but not vice versa.
> 3. The state of the Object is unknown, either because it has not yet been received, or it has not been produced yet.

(emphasis mine)

The trivial example is an original publisher that does not support DVR so it only keeps around two latest groups.  In that scenario, all groups before that are evicted and authoritatively no longer exist.

(for what it's worth, this rule has existed since at least draft-11, but I think it might even predate that)

issues.title: How does a caching relay handle different unknown extensions?
issues.author: afrind

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Discussed in 12/1 Interim:

The strawman proposal above is problematic.

WG would like:

1. Supported extensions are processed according to their own rules
2. Unsupported extensions are taken wholesale from a single publisher (no attempts to merge)
3. Caches SHOULD serve the unknown extensions that arrived most recently (this allows publishers to "fix" corruption).  SHOULD

issues.title: Datagrams and streams intermixed in the same subgroup.
issues.author: martinduke
issues.body:
PR #1350 allowed Datagrams and streams to coexist on the same track, as agreed in Toronto.

Here are the minutes of that discussion: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/minutes-interim-2025-moq-22-202509251330/ (Ctrl+F for "Delivery Timeout Mix and Match")

This PR is missing two parts of that discussion:
1) We agreed that a single subgroup cannot contain both datagrams and streams. 
2) I noted that we have to encode the subgroup ID in the DATAGRAM frame, or reserve a specific subgroup ID for datagrams, or something. The current mapping where subgroup_id == object_id does not work if subgroups have arbitrary IDs. I would propose that subgroup ID zero be reserved for datagrams. Datagrams exist outside of stream priorities, so that sort of works. If pub and sub priorities,  and group IDs , are equal, it makes sense that datagrams would be delivered to QUIC first. Zero is a special subgroup that has no implied dependencies between  its objects.

Upon further reflection, I'm not sure that the current state completely breaks any functions of the protocol, but it does confuse the idea that a subgroup has a particular priority. I would not like to wave through this change to the object model without at least discussing it.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I think 1) was an oversight in the PR.  Since datagrams only needed a subgroup value so they could be included in FETCH responses, maybe we can solve that a different way.

>  If pub and sub priorities, and group IDs , are equal, it makes sense that datagrams would be delivered to QUIC first

I don't know what that would be true.  If the publisher wanted one before the other it would give it a higher pri, and if it gave them the same priority, implementation dependent seems ok.  I don't see a reason why datagrams would be privileged by default.

comments.author: martinduke
comments.body:
OK, I clarified my thinking a bit on my walk home. Alan agrees with me there's a problem, I guess, but I'll record it here for posterity:

As it stands, for datagrams subgroup_id = object_id. So with arbitrarily large numbers of streams in groups, datagrams will be sprayed among the subgroups quasi-randomly. This has a bunch of problems:
a) Conceptually, subgroups imply a bunch of properties that are provided by a quic stream, in particular dependence and a shared fate. This makes no sense for datagrams.
b) Publisher priority is a property of a subgroup or a datagram. If a datagram is in a subgroup, there's a collision.
c) In intra-track prioritization, we are supposed to compare datagram object IDs with stream subgroup IDs if everything else is tied. This introduces weird dynamics into subgroup ID allocation that are hard to reason about.

I propose a PR that does the following:
a) subgroup ID = '0' means "no subgroup". Objects with this subgroup ID have none of the shared properties of subgroups.
b) received subgroup ID 0 on a stream is a protocol error
c) all datagrams use subgroup ID 0 in FETCH.
d) I was going to propose that datagrams use subgroup ID=0 in the intra-track prioritization algorithm. Alan seems to disagree, so maybe he can make an alternate proposal. I would argue that if you really want to do something different, use publisher priority. I thought @afrind was the one who wanted a deterministic algorithm in the draft, but again, I don't care that much. I can live with "implementation dependent" if that's what people want.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I think my proposal is:

1) Datagrams do not have a subgroup ID at all.  Subgroup IDs are for grouping things into streams, which you never do with datagrams.  
2) If a there are two scheduleable objects in the same track, same group, same pub priority and one is in a subgroup and one is in a datagram, Object ID is a reasonable tiebreaker, but I can live with implementation dependent, or subgroup wins.  Datagram wins feels yucky to me but I don't care.
3) Come up with some other encoding for datagrams in fetch responses that doesn't involve subgroup ID.  My best idea is to use one of the unused bits in the serialization flag.

comments.author: martinduke
comments.body: Except that we don't agree on the priority that we also don't care about, this then amounts to spelling in the FETCH (serialization flag vs group id 0). I do not see exactly how to use the serialization flag, but if you can make it work that's great.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I don't love this but:

Bitmask | Condition if set | Condition if not set (0)
-- | -- | --
0x04 | Object ID field is present | Object ID is the prior Object's ID plus one
0x08 | Group ID field is present | Group ID is the prior Object's Group ID
0x10 | Priority field is present | Priority is the prior Object's Priority
0x20 | Extensions field is present | Extensions field is not present
0x40 | PROTOCOL_VIOLATION | N/A

Change 0x40 to "Datagram" - if 1, the object is the datagram and the subgroup is meaningless.  bits 0-1 MUST NOT be 0x3 (subgroup ID present).

comments.author: martinduke
comments.body: oh, I hadn't noticed we landed those flags. sounds good.

issues.title: The draft does not explain how caching of Track Extensions works
issues.author: vasilvv
issues.body: It does not specify if/when it should cache them, it does not specify for how long it's supposed to cache them (presumably for as long as any objects related to the track are cached?), and it doesn't really specify what happens if a new response has different headers.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Proposal:

1. Cache track extensions as long as you have at least one object for that track cached, since you need them to send FETCH_OK
2. For extensions you understand, I think it's extension specific what to do.  For extensions you don't understand, see #1380.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I think this is purely editorial since it's evident from the design that you need to cache track extensions as long as you can serve objects from cache.  The "different" case will be resolved by the fix for #1380.

issues.title: How to support seeking or should seeking be discouraged when server is using the PUBLISH to control the subscription?
issues.author: laiDisney
issues.body:
From the application perspective, when the server is using the PUBLISH to start the playback, that means the server will take control of how and what to play at the client side. And it should work fine when the client has no requirement, the server can decide the ABR, which is the server-side ABR.

But what if the client has some functional requirements and needs to update/initialize another subscription, like the client needs to support the seeking function? We don't have a message for the client to request that the server send PUBLISH_DONE+PUBLISH to update/reinitialize the subscription. Or if the client sends UNSUBSCRIBE+Joining FETCH, it will break the control of the server publishing.

So my question would be:
* Should the seeking not be allowed when server PUBLISH?
* Or we should figure out a solution to support this? 
* Or is there a solution that supports it without breaking the control of the server publishing?

comments.author: sharmafb
comments.body: The specification explicitly permits the subscriber to update a subscription regardless of who initiated it, using a SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE.

comments.author: laiDisney
comments.body: That means that we don't have any reference on which side controls the publishing

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> That means that we don't have any reference on which side controls the publishing

I'm not sure what you mean by this comment.  The publisher always controls the publishing. The subscriber can control the filter, priority, forward state and timeout of the subscription.

When it comes to how MOQ supports VOD, see also #1316.  In general using SUBSCRIBE to retrieve past data is not supported at relays right now.  You need to use FETCH.

comments.author: laiDisney
suhasHere
comments.body:
if the server as a publisher wants to change the subscription, it can send either ReqeustUpdate or finish the existing publishing by sending PublishDone and Send a new Publish.

Regardless, the receiver client needs to send Subscribe so that relay can forward publish to the receiving client.

comments.author: laiDisney
comments.body:
After going through the Subscription Section in 15, I found I was wrong on the "server-control-everything" thinking, so this issue shouldn't exist.

> Relays MUST NOT send any PUBLISH messages without knowing the client is interested in and authorized to receive the content. The communication of intent and authorization can be accomplished by the client sending SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, or conveyed in other mechanisms out of band.

It has limited the relay cannot send any PUBLISH without client interested, so "server-control-everything" is impossible. I will close this issue as resolved.

issues.title: Section 10.3.1, Table 4: The table has duplicate rows with different "Type" values.
issues.author: kirki58
issues.body:
In the "Data streams and Datagrams > Datagrams > Object Datagram" Section of the draft document, We can see 2 table entries that are duplicates of 2 others and they defy the bitmask logic behind Object Datagram Type values.

These are:

- `0x2C` --> is a duplicate of `0x28` yet, it has a different type value plus the binary representation of the table in the form of (Status? - 0 - [Priority?]' , [ObjectId?]' , EndOfGroup?, Extensions?) doesn't really come to add up to `0x2C` in hex but rather adds up to `0x28`.
- `0x2D` --> is a duplicate of `0x29` yet, it has a different type value plus the binary representation of the table in the form of (Status? - 0 - [Priority?]' , [ObjectId?]' , EndOfGroup?, Extensions?) doesn't really come to add up to `0x2D` in hex but rather adds up to `0x29`.

Thanks to @zafergurel for double-checking this, As he stated the issue is probably caused by a copy-paste of rows and than those rows being forgotten to have an update on their values

I can't really assume what is being purposed with those 2 rows but the possibe fix to the issue is updating the rows as:

| Type | End Of Group | Extensions | Object ID | Priority Present | Status / Payload |
|---------|---------------------|-----------------|----------------|------------------------|-------------------------|
| `0x2C` | No                  | No               | No              | No                       | Status                  |
| `0x2D` | No                  | Yes               | No              | No                       | Status                  |

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I think this was an editorial mistake -- unless anyone has actually implemented.

issues.title: Can a publisher 'lie' about what Largest Object is? And does Largest Object need to exist?
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
I believe the answer is that its ok if the Publisher lies, as long as it's internally consistent within the Session and that there's no need for the Largest Object to actually exist. Previously we've said it's ok for the Publisher to start at the beginning of what is actually the Largest Object if it decides to, instead of waiting for the next largest to arrive, allowing it to immediately start sending data.

What I'm thinking is that if a Publisher/Relay knows that the Subscriber wants to start at the beginning of the Group, ideally explicitly (PR# 1362), it can say that the Largest Object is in the prior Group and give the Subscriber the entire Subscription via SUBSCRIBE, avoiding splitting the Subscription between FETCH and SUBSCRIBE streams and avoiding the Object Unknown issues entirely.

The only challenge I can see is a Schrodinger's cat sort of situation where if one did a TRACK_STATUS, followed by a SUBSCRIBE, it'd be weird to have Largest Object go backwards, but if they're on separate streams, there might be cases that'd happen anyway.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Current text:

> Some filters are defined to be relative to the Largest Object. The Largest Object is the Object with the largest Location ([Section 1.4.1](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#location-structure)) in the Track from the perspective of the publisher processing the message. Largest Object updates when the first byte of an Object with a Location larger than the previous value is published or received through a subscription.

So sending a different value from this definition seems going against the spirit without some text changes.  The primary purpose is to communicate to the subscriber what their relative filter was set to, and define the end of a potential joining fetch (though see also #1335), but it can have application uses too.

comments.author: gwendalsimon
comments.body:
Both this issue and #1362 are attempts to remove or sidestep Joining FETCH. Whether it is "Largest Group" or "lying about LargestObject", it is the same idea: replacing Joining FETCH with a Subscribe-only mechanism, especially for the offset=0 case. I do not think we need multiple issues to discuss the same direction.

Today, the streaming industry has well-established use cases that depend on joining with a controlled offset behind live: betting around 1s, premium leagues would like to be around 3s, broadcast-aligned events aims at around 5s, and more relaxed live workflows around 10s or more. All of these rely on joining the stream at a group boundary that is immediately decodable (to reduce startup delay), while allowing the application to choose an appropriate buffer depth.

From this perspective, let me state again the requirement: we need an explicit mechanism to join at offset X groups behind the live edge, not only at 0. Joining FETCH already provides a straightforward way to express this range of offsets, including 0.

If there is interest in revisiting how offset=0 is expressed or simplifying that path, that can be discussed. But whatever we do, we must preserve a reliable and explicit way to join at offset X>0, since many deployments depend on it. Any proposal should start from that requirement rather than working around the existing mechanism.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
> Both this issue and [#1362](https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/pull/1362) are attempts to remove or sidestep Joining FETCH. Whether it is "Largest Group" or "lying about LargestObject", it is the same idea: replacing Joining FETCH with a Subscribe-only mechanism, especially for the offset=0 case. I do not think we need multiple issues to discuss the same direction.
>

#1362 is an effort to work around a limitation in Joining FETCH, but it's a good point that if we were going to do it, it should be X groups behind the live edge, where X can be > 0.
 
> Today, the streaming industry has well-established use cases that depend on joining with a controlled offset behind live: betting around 1s, premium leagues would like to be around 3s, broadcast-aligned events aims at around 5s, and more relaxed live workflows around 10s or more. All of these rely on joining the stream at a group boundary that is immediately decodable (to reduce startup delay), while allowing the application to choose an appropriate buffer depth.
> 
> From this perspective, let me state again the requirement: we need an explicit mechanism to join at offset X groups behind the live edge, not only at 0. Joining FETCH already provides a straightforward way to express this range of offsets, including 0.
> 
> If there is interest in revisiting how offset=0 is expressed or simplifying that path, that can be discussed. But whatever we do, we must preserve a reliable and explicit way to join at offset X>0, since many deployments depend on it. Any proposal should start from that requirement rather than working around the existing mechanism.

I completely agree with the use case and want to preserve that.  In my more exploratory PR to remove FETCH entirely, I did add a Filter for N Groups before head: #1377

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I think lying may be a viable strategy in limited cases.  For example, if Largest Object is X,Y, and I have X,0 - X,Y-1 in cache, it may be safe to say Largest Object is X-1,maxint(?), and begin delivery from the beginning of the group.  This works best if there is only a single subgroup per group.  If the group is large and used datagrams or stream-per-object, rewinding could cause you to consume all available streams in the session, or cause datagrams to be dropped.

If you have an unknown gap (say cache has X,3 - X,Y-1), you can't rewind Largest Object past it, since you don't really know if it's coming or not, or if it was really the beginning of the group etc.  This is problematic especially around HEAD in the 2 subgroups/group case - it seems likely that you could have a gap there.

That said, it's not great to lie.  It would be better for the subscriber to opt into this behavior.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
While there's nothing we can do to prevent a relay from lying, I don't think we should permit it in the spec, and I think we should add normative text forbidding it.  It creates an interoperability hazard that some relays lie and others don't, and subscribers get different behavior based on relay implementation.

If you want this behavior, negotiate an extension like REWIND.

issues.title: Clarify what control messages can be sent on what stream
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
As a follow-up to #1344, the intent is to add a table similar to how QUIC indicates what frames can be sent at what level of encryption.

I'm filing an issue because I'd like to wait until any stream mapping changes are finished and do a thorough job of this.

issues.title: Consider possible follow-ups to moving SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE to a bidi stream
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
Some further possible changes after #1344:
- Don't send REQUEST_ERROR on errors, QUIC RESET_STREAM with the application error code. Loses Reason Phrase - This only makes sense if we move SUBSCRIBE and FETCH to bidi streams as well
- Don't send REQUEST_OK on success. Loses response parameters - Leaning towards no change
- Allow for subscribing to full Track names and not just Namespaces - No preference, but it's been mentioned
- Prohibit sending NAMESPACE_DONE before a NAMESPACE is received for a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE - Leaning Yes to this restriction
- Drop the redundant length from NAMESPACE and NAMESPACE_DONE - Leaning towards Yes
- Allow overlapping SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACEs - Currently disallowed because it was ambiguous why you received a given PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, but this removes that ambiguity.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> Don't send REQUEST_ERROR on errors, QUIC RESET_STREAM with the application error code. Loses Reason Phrase - This only makes sense if we move SUBSCRIBE and FETCH to bidi streams as well

Park this for now, but I am a strong believer in the value of reason phrases at this layer of the stack.

> Don't send REQUEST_OK on success. Loses response parameters - Leaning towards no change

Don't change this, send REQUEST_OK.

> Allow for subscribing to full Track names and not just Namespaces - No preference, but it's been mentioned

I can sort of see a use case here -- which is that you know the track you want and you are willing to wait for it to materialize via PUBLISH, rather than perhaps failing if you send SUBSCRIBE and publisher isn't there.  Maybe this is better as a subscribe feature.

> Prohibit sending NAMESPACE_DONE before a NAMESPACE is received for a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE - Leaning Yes to this restriction

Yes, seems like an error to receive NS_DONE A when I haven't received NS A yet.

> Drop the redundant length from NAMESPACE and NAMESPACE_DONE - Leaning towards Yes

Yes seems like the right answer, though this means they are no longer control messages, which could be fine.  Maybe reorganize them as sub messages in the SUBSCRIBE_NS section?

> Allow overlapping SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACEs - Currently disallowed because it was ambiguous why you received a given PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, but this removes that ambiguity.

My objection before was it was totally redundant - you would just receive multiple copies of every PUB_NS.   Especially given that the forthcoming _filters_ might be different, I think yes, we can allow this.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
One follow-up is whether there are recommendations on what NAMESPACES should (or shouldn't) be advertised.

For example, I would expect that End Subscribers would never send any NAMESPACE messages and maybe Original Publishers wouldn't either (only PUBLISH or PUBLISH_NAMESPACE?)?

If you learned about a namespace from the node that also sent a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, should you not send that namespace back, because obviously the peer knows about it?

I'm still a bit concerned about loops (#556), but I also think most networks will have internal protections from loops?

issues.title: Unclear how to use Joining FETCH with New Group Request
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
Per discussion on #1335 , there's an issue where if you use NGR, there are two possibilities:
 1) NGR will not produce a new group, so you'd like to Joining FETCH for the first part of the Group.
 2) NGR will produce a new group, so there's no need for a Joining FETCH

In the second case, if you issue a Joining FETCH, you get a gap between the current Largest Object and the start of the next Group, which is seemingly not the intent of Joining FETCH, but you also aren't going to use the Joining FETCH anyway so maybe it doesn't matter?

@suhasHere indicated he didn't use Joining FETCH with NGR, so maybe not a practical problem.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
My understanding is that the most interested users of NGR plan to issue a blind SUBSCRIBE, then issue either NGR, Joining FETCH, or wait for the next group to start naturally.

I've floated the idea before of moving this to the relay by including an object ID threshold, but no one seems to care.  I'm closing this.  @suhasHere please reopen if you want spec changes.

issues.title: NAMESPACE messages with multiple sub-namespaces in them?
issues.author: sharmafb
issues.body:
My understanding of the NAMESPACE message is as follows: Let's say that a subscriber sends a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE request to a publisher, with the namespace set to "foo/bar". The publisher, if it is advertising a more restricted namespace, for example, "foo/bar/baz/goo", can send "baz/goo" in the NAMESPACE response.

What if, however, in my previous example, the publisher is advertising "foo/bar/baz/goo" and "foo/bar/baz/moo"? There is no way for it to send both "baz/goo" and "baz/moo" in the same NAMESPACE message. Are we allowing for multiple NAMESPACE messages?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Yes you are supposed to get a sequence of NAMESPACE and NAMESPACE_DONE messages on the bidi stream.  Maybe that needs to be more clear?

comments.author: sharmafb
comments.body: It might be helpful to add a one-liner in the spec to clarify this for the sake of completeness. Though if others think this isn't really necessary, we can skip it.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
I feel like this is fairly clear: https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/blob/main/draft-ietf-moq-transport.md#subscribing-to-namespaces

But maybe there's a way to improve the text?  Suggestions welcome.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Maybe we can say "Each NAMESPACE message carries a single namespace."?

issues.title: Support the lingering SUBSCRIBE use case
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
At the recent interop, the Cisco implementation's implementation of SUBSCRIBE allows the SUBSCRIBE to linger even if nothing has been published yet.  Other implementations immediately returned when the Track hadn't been published.  There's a real use case here, which is to ensure the beginning of the Track doesn't get clipped off when a new Original Publisher joins.

This is very similar to what SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE allows, since it elicits PUBLISH from the Publisher for the specified namespace.  My best guess is that the gap here is that there are use cases you don't want to subscribe to the entire Namespace, but I'm not sure?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Example flows:

Lingering Subscribe:

```
S->R: SUBSCRIBE, MaxWait=T
No publishers yet, start timer
P->R: PUBLISH
R->S: SUBSCRIBE_OK
```

```
S->R: SUBSCRIBE, MaxWait=T
No publishers yet, start timer
P->R: PUBLISH_NAMESPACE
R->P: PUB_NS_OK, SUBSCRIBE
P->R: SUBSCRIBE_OK
R->S: SUBSCRIBE_OK
```

SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE

```
S->R: SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE
R->S: SUB_NS_OK
P->R: PUBLISH
R->S: PUBLISH
```

```
S->R: SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE foo
R->S: SUB_NS_OK
P->R: PUBLISH_NAMESPACE foo

crickets?
```
Maybe this is just not a valid design?

```
S->R: SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE foo
R->S: SUB_NS_OK
P->R: PUBLISH_NAMESPACE foo/bar
R->S: NAMESPACE [foo/]bar
S->R: SUBSCRIBE foo/bar, track=t
R->P: SUBSCRIBE foo/bar, track=t
```

comments.author: suhasHere
comments.body:
We did discuss this as part of IETF 125 , slides https://datatracker.ietf.org/meeting/122/materials/slides-122-moq-early-media-00

I think when  multiple clients try to pub and sub at the same time, there is a chance that the ordering of the control messages may cause media clipping

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
The response to the discussion at IETF was to address using SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE + PUBLISH.  Along with joining FETCH, it seems to functionally address the problem described.

What are the remaining gaps?

issues.title: Single Object Subgroups don't need a Subgroup ID
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
A key purpose of a Subgroup ID is to allow the second half of a Subgroup to be delivered on a different stream and put together with the first half if the stream is unexpected terminated for any reason.

If a Stream only has one Object, there's no need for that.  

This matters because currently Subgroup ID is a Varint, which is a huge space and a challenge for prioritization.  The Object per stream use case is the one case I expect there could be more than 256 Subgroups today.  If we could eliminate it, we could go down to one byte, just like Priority.

My strawman is to do what we do for Objects in Datagrams: https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/blob/main/draft-ietf-moq-transport.md#datagrams

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
There's already a way to convey a subgroup on the wire without a subgroup ID (see e.g. Stream Header Type 0x12).  There's only two other places where the subgroup ID matters:

1) it's included in FETCH responses
2) it's a tiebreaker for priority within the same track and group

I think 1 doesn't matter that much.

For 2, perhaps a concrete change is to eliminate subgroup ID as a tiebreaker, and use "the first object ID on the subgroup".  For multi-object subgroups, I expect there won't be that many, and publishers will differentiate on priority.  For many one-object subgroups (or datagrams), there's only one object ID anyways.  This makes it easier to compare subgroups and datagrams that have the same publisher priority too.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
I agree that 1 doesn't matter much.

First Object ID on the Subgroup seems sensible to me for prioritization.  I thought we already said that lower Object IDs are sent first if everything else is equal, but I can't find that text in the Priorities section (https://github.com/moq-wg/moq-transport/blob/main/draft-ietf-moq-transport.md#priorities-priorities).  Right now we explicitly say that Subgroup vs Datagram prioritization can be implementation dependent if everything else is equal.

I agree there likely won't be many multi-object subgroups, which is why I was trying to find a way to get Subgroup ID down to a byte.  I also think the Datagram Object framing makes a bit more sense for a single Object stream, as well as being slightly more compact.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: The only place the size of such a subgroup ID would matter is prioritization, so if we take it out of the prioritization algorithm, why do you want to make it a byte?  It's not sent on the wire anyways.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
Discussion of the PR so far indicates we don't really want to bother with #1593 

It still seems attractive to simplify the prioritization scheme, like #1446 proposed, but there wasn't appetite for that at the time it was proposed.

I'm inclined to close this issue with no action, but I'll put it before the WG to confirm.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: One idea I had when reviewing PR #1607 is we could force the Subgroup ID to be the Object ID of the first Object, and then it'd be unambiguous what the start of the Subgroup is.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
Feedback from the WG at today's interim was:
1) People agreed it was important to know what the start Object ID of the Subgroup (and possibly Group?)
2) People had different concerns about restricting the Subgroup ID to be starting Object ID at the Original Publisher.
3) There was some confusion about both this proposal and what is possible in today's Object model in terms of publishing Objects in a subgroup 'out of order'

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: Discussed in London: Close with no action

issues.title: Unknown Setup Parameters and Extension Negotiation
issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
The current draft states:

> Receivers ignore unrecognized parameters.

This applies to both setup and message parameters.

The current design is that a client includes parameters that represent extensions it supports and wishes to use and possibly parameters related to that extension.  ALPN is not suitable for this because of possible combinatorial explosion when there are N different extensions.

So as an example:

~~~
CLIENT_SETUP:
Parameters:
HOT_EXTENSION: 1
HOT_EXTENSION_DEFAULT_TEMP: 100
HOT_EXTENSION_MAX_TEMP: 1000

SERVER_SETUP that supports HOT_EXTENSION:
Parameters:
HOT_EXTENSION: 1
HOT_EXTENSION_MAX_TEMP: 500

SERVER_SETUP that has never heard of HOT_EXTENSION:
Parameters:
~~~

This design allows clients to speculatively add all the information necessary to setup to enable an extension without any risk of blowing up the session.

This design has been in place through all consensus calls issued in 2025, including the ALPN change in draft-15.

In #1390 discussions, some folks would like to revisit this design.

There's intersection with #1370, because allowing the control streams to be independent of one another has implications for how one negotiates extensions.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
I can imagine wanting to require auth, but that's defined in the core draft, so by definition it can't be unknown.

If the peer doesn't support something and you need it, and it's an extension (not a new alpn), then I think the only approach is to fail the handshake after finding out the peer doesn't support whatever extension you need.

This approach has worked quite well for QUIC, so I'm not sure why MoQ would be that different?

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body: I find this complaint odd, since this is very similar to how TLS, QUIC, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, and probably a lot of other protocols work.  I don't see really good alternatives (except maybe for ALPS, which would be an improvement in some sense, but sadly ALPS draft has been inactive for years).

comments.author: suhasHere
comments.body:
Here is my comment from the PR #1390  ( copying here for context) , which seems to not work in terms of extensibility.

By unrecognizable and ignorable, Setup parameter must be recognized by the Peer , but it need not have to be in a given protocol version. I am feeling bit uncomfortable to allow to blindly ignore setup parameter by the peer ( in this case relay)

Just thinking loud, say, i have a setup param, called disable_rtx_use_rs_fec_only and the publisher ignored it altogether. Should the receiver figure out the publisher doesn't support this behavior by observing data plane and seeing RTX packets or knows the peer understood by observing rs_fec packets or consider peer doesn't understand by seeing something like fec but which doesn't look like rs_fec but fails recovety?

May be I am thinking wrong here, but love to understand what am i missing ?

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
> Just thinking loud, say, i have a setup param, called disable_rtx_use_rs_fec_only and the publisher ignored it altogether. Should the receiver figure out the publisher doesn't support this behavior by observing data plane and seeing RTX packets or knows the peer understood by observing rs_fec packets or consider peer doesn't understand by seeing something like fec but which doesn't look like rs_fec but fails recovety?
> 

I agree that waiting for the dataplane to find out if an extension was supported by the peer would be a poor design, and I wouldn't design and extension like that. For extensions where both sides need to support it, both would specify the Setup Parameter.  If the server (who may or may not be a publisher), ignores it, the client can decide to fail the handshake at that point if support is a hard requirement.

QUIC receive timestamps are a great example of something I might really want for a MoQ congestion controller (ie: a GoogCC style one), but if the peer doesn't support them, I might fall back to an alternative congestion controller.  Or I might fail the whole thing and fall back to TCP or WebRTC or something else.  As indicated by this example, I think it's very difficult for an extension designer to know if an extension is a hard requirement when designing it, so letting the client and server decide that makes sense.  As long as both know when they receive the peer's SETUP message, they can decide whether to fail the MoQ handshake entirely or adjust for the lack of extension support.

Two examples from QUIC:
* MP-QUIC does this by requiring both endpoints to send the initial_max_path_id transport param: https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-quic-multipath-18.html#section-2

* Alternatively, QUIC ACK_FREQUENCY is an optimization, and only uses one Transport Param to unilaterally advertise support: https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-quic-ack-frequency-13.html#section-3

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body:
> Just thinking loud, say, i have a setup param, called disable_rtx_use_rs_fec_only and the publisher ignored it altogether. Should the receiver figure out the publisher doesn't support this behavior by observing data plane and seeing RTX packets or knows the peer understood by observing rs_fec packets or consider peer doesn't understand by seeing something like fec but which doesn't look like rs_fec but fails recovety?

You almost always want both parties to negotiate support.  For instance, in object ACK extension, we require both peers to send supports_object_acks, and the extension is considered to be enabled only if both set the value to 1.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
@fluffy and I discussed this today and there were a few suggested changes:
1) Ensure we're not using the name Parameters in cases it's ambiguous which type of Parameter is being referenced.
2) Rename Setup Parameters to something that doesn't use the word Parameter, because it could be confusing.  'Setup Properties' was a proposed alternative.  Unlike Track and Object Extension Headers, Parameters do not share a registry between Setup Parameters and Message Parameters, and Message Parameters must be understood, unlike Setup Parameters, so they are substantially different.
3) Make it clear how we expect extensions to negotiate new Parameters and Message types using Setup.
4) Discuss what happens when requests with an extension are pipelined with SETUP.  Can extensions not be used, or not, etc. On a high level, this seems similar to QUIC 0-RTT, but there are some differences, so write them down.

If any other issues arise in the process of writing these down, I'll try to address them.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
AI offers:

Some alternatives:                                                                        
                                                                                            
  1. Setup Options - mirrors TCP options, which are also TLV-encoded and skippable          
  2. Setup Properties - as suggested                                                        
  3. Session Properties - emphasizes they're session-wide                                   
  4. Setup Settings - simple and descriptive                                                
  5. Capabilities - emphasizes the negotiation aspect                                       
                                                                                            
Setup Options since it has precedent in networking (TCP options use a similar TLV structure where unknown options can be skipped), and "options" implies "optional/skippable" which matches the behavior.

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body: Setup Fields or Setup Values maybe?  We got rid of all other fields in that message.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Discussed in Boulder:

Unknown Setup Options are fine.  Ian will address the other points above.  A new issue was filed about mechanism for designating track/object extensions that must be understood, and a relay that receives but doesn't understand has to UNSUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH_ERROR?  #1480

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Draft -17 now has the following text regarding setup and extension negotiation:

3.2 Negotiating Extensions:

> Endpoints use the exchange of Setup messages to negotiate MOQT extensions. Extensions can define new Message types, new Parameters, or new framing for Data Streams and Datagrams.
> 
> The client and server MUST include all Setup Options ... required for the negotiated MOQT version in SETUP.
> 
> Each endpoint declares the extensions it supports and provides any initial values required by those extensions as Setup Options in SETUP. Once an endpoint has both sent and received SETUP messages, it determines the set of negotiated extensions.
> 
> New versions of MOQT MUST specify which existing extensions can be used with that version. New extensions MUST specify the existing versions with which they can be used.

9.4 SETUP:

> An endpoint that is not offering extensions which modify control message semantics MAY pipeline other control messages after SETUP without waiting for the peer's SETUP.
> 
> The messages contain a sequence of key-value pairs called Setup Options; the semantics and format of which can vary based on whether the client or server is sending. To ensure future extensibility of MOQT, endpoints MUST ignore unknown Setup Options.
> ...
> Receivers MUST ignore unrecognized Setup Options. 
> ...
> Receivers MUST allow duplicates of unknown Setup Options.

What additional text is required to close this issue?

issues.title: [Potential DoS risk] Continuously adding parameters in REQUEST_UPDATE message
issues.author: sharmafb
issues.body:
If implementations store parameter sets per request, a peer can bloat per-request state by continually adding parameters through REQUEST_UPDATE messages. Although control message total size is capped at 2^16-1, repeated updates across many REQUEST_UPDATEs can still create unbounded aggregate state over a long session.

From my read of the specification, it doesn't look like there is a mechanism that prevents this from happening. Would it be worth it to add a short section in "Relay security considerations" about this?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Since they are hop-by-hop (now) and must be understood, is there significant risk? A sender can only include known params.  Are any of our existing message parameters additive in this way?  Filters might be, but there will be separate receiver declared limits.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: I think I agree with Alan that these don't pose a significant risk, given they must be understood.  If they didn't have to be understood, the risk does seem potentially unbounded, so good choice on our part in #1390.

issues.title: Increment stream count for empty subgroup?
issues.author: sharmafb
issues.body:
