> identification between relays, especially within one organization.

that seems true but out of scope for this draft.

issues.title: Mutual TLS
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body:
The draft says 

> However, in some deployments mutual TLS can also be used for end
> subscribers or original publishers. However, as only node level
> authentication is provided, what a particular identified node is
> allowed to do is not provided at TLS level.

It seems likely that mTLS would be a common scheme for a cloud based publisher for things like VOD, to authenticate to relays but I a bunch more text is needed to make this implementable and sort out how this maps to authentications.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> a bunch more text is needed to make this implementable and sort out how this maps to authentications

This doesn't seem actionable as written.  Can you provide more detail?

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body: Write enough specification on how to do secure mTLS such that it is implementable and secure.  The current text is not enough to be able to implement mTLS or understand what security properties it would provide.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> Write enough specification on how to do secure mTLS such that it is implementable and secure. 

If this can't be done in a couple sentences, then I think we should make an informational reference to some other document that has more details on the security properties and deployment of TLS in its various modes.  This document is about moq-transport.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: A reference to another RFC makes sense, but I'm not sure which is the best choice?

issues.title: Replay attacks
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body:
The draft says

> Replay protection for authorization tokens is the responsibility of
> the specific token scheme used. Token schemes such as [CAT] and
> [PPA] include requirements for relays when processing tokens and
> requests.

I would like this to push specific requirements on the token schemes.  In the case where the applications is running in web browser and the token will be visible to javascript and any browser extensions, we should require that the token can not be cut and paste to another browser and replayed by an entity that did not have the credentials to get a new token. 

Without this we have a risk of token being widely distributed across and attacker network and used to DDoS the relay or get unauthorized access to content.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Can you phrase that as a specific requirement?  And are you suggesting that MOQT can _only_ be used by token schemes that prevent replay?  It seems like that's not really enforceable?

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body: I will note that the two types of tokens we currently have defined both support replay protection.  I was suggesting the security considerations phrase it as if the deployment is in a place where coping token was a threat vectors, then then this needs to be protected. This is based on the belief that noon replay of tokens will up being a key part of our protection agains DOS of relays.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Ok, expressing the importance of addressing the threat replay vector up front seems doable.  I just didn't think it made sense to say something like "Every token scheme transported in MOQT_AUTHENTICATION parameters MUST prevent token replay attacks".

issues.title: E2E Encryption schemes
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body: The draft mentions various E2EE schemes but I think it should add that a key part of the design is to work with the existing DRM schemes widely deployed for HLS and DASH.  This is a pretty key part of meeting the security requirements of some of the main uses case.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Are you asking for a statement like "MOQT is designed to work with existing DRM schemes widely deployed for HLS and DASH"?

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body: Yes, with an informative reference to the scheme (not a ref to HLS or DASH). It's been a key thing since that start that has shifted some of the design.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I'm disinclined to add such a reference -- for example, HLS and DASH work fine without HTTP making a reference to their DRM schemes.  I'm not sure how this would add any value to the spec.

issues.title: Resource Exhaustion Section
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body:
This should be expanded to consider 

- number of connections for a user 
- ingress bandwidth
- egress bandwidth 
- ingress rate of objects
- egress rate of objects
- rate of controll messages
- cache usage

issues.title: Errors from missing data timeouts
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body:
The draft says

> Implementations are advised to use timeouts to prevent resource
> exhaustion attacks by a peer that does not send expected data within
> an expected time. Each implementation is expected to set its own
> timeouts.

I think we need more guidance on how to set these and the bounds as this sounds like it likely to lead to high unpredictable results in deployments.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
Some comments from Vienna:
- Explicitly communicating when it occurs is important
- Timeout for Subscriptions is useful, it's unclear if we need to communicate Fill timeout?

From Ian: Want to avoid application disruption, hence Subscription timeouts
 - Otherwise don't communicate the timeout beforehand, and it's commonly dynamic anyway

Ted suggested a principle: "Need to know which layer will take action"

issues.title: Explain how relay handles SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE or SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS when subscriber is only authorized for a subset
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body:
The draft says

> A Relay can use authorization rules in order to prevent subscriptions
> closer to the root of a large prefix tree. Otherwise, if an entity
> sends a relay a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE or SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS message with
> a short prefix, it can cause the relay to send a large volume of
> NAMESPACE or PUBLISH messages. As changes occur in the tree of
> namespaces, the relay would have to send matching NAMESPACE/
> NAMESPACE_DONE messages or initiate new PUBLISH streams.

but we should offer some mitigations of this. 

First would be clear authorization that allowed a token to limit the scope of the subscribe. In addition, it might make sense to rate limit the number of notifications from the subscribe.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> First would be clear authorization that allowed a token to limit the scope of the subscribe.

The text starts with:

> A Relay can use authorization rules in order to prevent subscriptions closer to the root of a large prefix tree.

So I think that's covered?

>  In addition, it might make sense to rate limit the number of notifications from the subscribe.

I don't see how we can build a functional system by restricting the notification rate.  When the relay is e.g. blocked by stream flow control from sending a publish, we send PUBLISH_BLOCKED (skipped), but that doesn't change the notification rate, and that's not even what's problematic about the SUBSCRIBE_NS/TRACKS. 

The other mitigation we currently have is NAMESPACE_TOO_LARGE -- the relay can just fail the SUB_NS/T.

> NAMESPACE_TOO_LARGE:
> In response to SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE or SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, the namespace prefix matches more publishers than the relay is willing to enumerate.

You marked this Design -- did you have some broader change in mind here?

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body:
So clearly asking for all the tracks in a given twitch live stream is very different from asking all the twitch tracks across every active stream.  We need to sort out an implantable way be able to authorize one but not the other. I think we need to design a mechanism that does this - the how to do it part of the design is easy but the how much flexibility does it have is the hard part to get the balance right on. It's really easy to design authorization schemes that are too fine grain. 

So the text we need is how this works, what the relays does, what it does for requests of unauthorized things, can you have access to part but not all of a namespace. Then this will inform requirements on how token schemes map their representation onto what the relay does when authorizing.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> what it does for requests of unauthorized things
> can you have access to part but not all of a namespace. 

Ok, I think I'm getting your case now.

This is something the relay doesn't explicitly allow or forbid today - eg SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS foo- but the relay looks at your auth token and says "I'm only going to forward tracks to you under foo-bar-123-".  Or look at it the other way, the relay got a PUBLISH matching your SUB_TRACKS prefix but clearly knows you are NOT authorized for it.

It has nothing to do with rate limits, but deserves text.  I'm going to use this issue to track it, unless you something else you'd like to change that has to do with limits.  @fluffy

issues.title: Nothing good comes from an implementation string
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body:
The draft says 

> Privacy-conscious deployments MAY omit the MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION
> option entirely or send a generic value.

History would suggest that things will check that and do stuff based on it and then applications will decide to act they are something too big to break.  This then results in further difficulty to debug or fix the root causes.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: There's no question its adding value to interop at the current stage.  Let's throw it in the pile with Reason Phrase and make a final call later.

issues.title: Media Type Registration
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body: Section 15.2 of draft 18 does not define a media type. MoQ is transport for existing media types such H.264

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: As I understand it, you are not allowed to specify a URI fragment without a media type.  We are defining the media type of a moqt resource, which is the session described by the transport document.  It is a media type that can carry other media types, such as H.264.  Does that make sense?

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body: I don't think this is blocked in any way on me.  You are correct URI fragments are used for media types.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
>  You are correct URI fragments are used for media types.

Then I don't understand what you are asking.  Closing

issues.title: Bike shed IMMUTABLE_PROPERTIES property naming
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body: I don't think we should have PROPERTIES in the name.

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body: Oh, and I am probably the person that did this. My apologies. But I still think it is worth fixing

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I think the name aptly describes what is in the value of the property, with the redundancy.  I'm inclined to keep as is.  Just calling it "IMMUTABLE" or "The Immutable Property" doesn't sound like an improvement to me.

issues.title: Standalone Fetch end limits
issues.author: fluffy
issues.body: The Standalone Fetch section does should specify what happens for a standalone fetch where the end location is larger than the largest object.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
The text you are looking for is in FETCH_OK:

> End Location: The end of the range covered by the FETCH response, using the same encoding as the FETCH request End Location (the last Object, plus 1; or 0 to indicate the entire Group). This is the End Location from the FETCH request unless the requested range extends beyond published data:
>
>If the requested FETCH End Location was beyond the Largest known (possibly final) Object, End Location is {Largest.Group, Largest.Object + 1} Where Fetch.End Location is either Fetch.Standalone.End Location or the computed End Location described in [Section 10.12.2.1](https://moq-wg.github.io/moq-transport/draft-ietf-moq-transport.html#joining-fetch-range-calculation).
>
>If End Location is smaller than the Start Location in the corresponding FETCH the receiver MUST close the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

perhaps a forward ref from FETCH would help

issues.title: Clarify retry interval = 0 with REDIRECT error code
issues.author: sharmafb
issues.body: REDIRECT says the requester SHOULD retry at the redirected location, while retry interval 0 says it SHOULD NOT retry. I think we should make retry interval = 0 and REDIRECT error code illegal. Thoughts on this?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I view the retry interval as applying to the original request, so I think it's ok, if a little odd?

comments.author: sharmafb
comments.body: What if the new request is exactly the same as the original request (i.e. the redirect structure didn't change anything)?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
So Err=REDIRECT, No URI, Retry Interval=0 ?

I suppose it's ambiguous which instruction wins (send this to me, except don't), but I'm not sure I foresee a huge interop gap here worthy of a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.  If anything, half a sentence saying which wins could suffice?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Retry Interval has a second role for REDIRECT — relay cache lifetime ("A relay MAY cache a REDIRECT response ... for up to Retry Interval milliseconds"). With 0 that cleanly means "don't cache," so 0 is already a meaningful, legal value. Making it illegal would lose that.

issues.title: Is an unexpected REQUEST_UPDATE a request or session error?
issues.author: RichLogan
issues.body:
The sender of a request can send `REQUEST_UPDATE` to modify it, and there is the additional case of a subscriber sending a `REQUEST_UPDATE` in the other direction when updating the subscribe-side params of a `PUBLISH` that it has accepted, if I understand correctly? 

I'm assuming that in any other case receiving a `REQUEST_UPDATE` on a request stream would be a `PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (rather than a `REQUEST_ERROR` response)? Not sure if the draft should be more explicit on that point if so.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> The sender of a request can send REQUEST_UPDATE to modify it, and there is the additional case of a subscriber sending a REQUEST_UPDATE in the other direction when updating the subscribe-side params of a PUBLISH that it has accepted, if I understand correctly?

That's correct.

Not sure if it should be a request error or session error though.  Maybe session error is better?

comments.author: RichLogan
comments.body: Yeah I think I agree it's a session error at that point. Originally I modelled it as request error, but if that flow for a given request *never* makes sense, and all parameters are explicitly defined in the draft so there's no extensibility there, then it does seem like it's just incorrect behaviour and should be treated as such(?).

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I hadn't thought about the extensibility angle, but any extension that wants to allow that will have to explain it's not a session error.

issues.title: Misleading language: "shares a common prefix"
issues.author: sharmafb
issues.body: In sections 10.18 (SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE) and sections 10.19 (SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS), we use "shares a common prefix" to describe illegal requests. However, this is misleading. For example, (foo, bar, baz) and (foo, cat, dog) share a common prefix, but I think they should be legal.

issues.title: REDIRECT ambiguity with empty namespace and empty name
issues.author: sharmafb
issues.body: Redirect uses "zero namespace + empty track name" as "same as original", but that is also a valid Full Track Name. Should we instead add an explicit flag?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: How thoroughly annoying.  Yes, we can respell with a flag (set to 1 if you want to change the namespace or name).  Alternately we can say you cannot redirect to the empty FTN, but that seems like an arbitrary restriction.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: I still think allowing empty names is not useful and creates a bunch of annoying edge cases like this.

issues.title: Track Aliases: allow re-use or not?
issues.author: sharmafb
issues.body: Section 11.1 allows Track Alias reuse when not simultaneous. However, I think we should outright disallow it. A datagram can arrive arbitrarily late and cause ambiguity, so I don't think it's ever safe to reuse.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: We just landed #1775 which allows re-use for the _same track_ at least.  In theory it's not ever safe for different tracks, but in practicality, there's a threshold after which you can reasonably do it.  Since the 1 byte code space is limited and wire image may be important, I think we can keep it; buyer beware.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: CC: track alias enthusiasts @suhasHere @fluffy

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: I'm inclined to keep it as it and allow re-use, though I am fine with: "SHOULD NOT reuse Track Alias across multiple Subscriptions except when its the same track."  Maybe that embodies the idea that its probably a bad idea, but we can't really stop you?

comments.author: martinduke
comments.body: In Vienna, people seemed OK with this, but if no one has a use case better than saving a byte, IMO we should disallow this just to make things cleaner, rather than creating weird failure modes.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Discussed in Vienna: allow re-use, add some cautionary text about the footgun.

issues.title: PUBLISH_OK parameters can have unpredictable results
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
When writing a PR to fix #1660 and reviewing #1673, I realized that changing parameters of a Subscription was only safe for some parameters (ie: Priority) and had unpredictable behavior for Forward and Location Filters.  In particular, anything that changes what Objects are sent for a Subscription (ie: Forward or Filters) has a stale Largest Object, as pointed out in #1673, so its unclear what Objects a Subscriber expects to get.

Additionally, a Subscriber can immediately send a REQUEST_UPDATE after the PUBLISH_OK, so there's no real need to update any Subscription parameters in PUBLISH_OK.  As a result, this doesn't change the functionality of MoQ at all, just the message sequence.

I wrote #1790 with this in mind.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I think setting some things in PUBLISH_OK is fine/desirable -- eg priority or NGR?

The main troubles come when setting filters/forward as you say, and it intersects with #1673.  I'm tempted to land that, which more or less says "don't send those in PUBLISH_OK", and not make any other changes.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: Discussed yesterday in person, and it was agreed it'd be helpful to share this with the WG.  Also, we should ensure that PUBLISH_OK needs to come before REQUST_UPDATE, but that should already be true and is orthogonal to this issue.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
NGR is not currently allowed, and I think it's another case you'd want an OK/ERROR in response, so I don't think its safe to put in PUBLISH_OK.

As a result, it seems like Priority is the one thing that's definitely safe to update, but allowing updating that one Parameter in PUBLISH_OK doesn't seem very useful.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: Discussed in Vienna, there was support for adding this restriction to simplify the protocol.

issues.title: Optimal Routing and Loop Prevention are useful
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
Adding a hop count or something similar to NAMESPACE (formerly ANNOUNCE) has been discussed before, but it was recently added to moq-lite, so I thought it might be worth reconsidering.
https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-lcurley-moq-lite-04.html#section-7.4

Or maybe its an extension?
@kixelated 

https://github.com/englishm/moq-relay-dos/issues/24 is the issue in the DoS repo

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: This feels like an extension at this point, but I'm interested in collaborating.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
For reference:

> In particular, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE SHOULD NOT be used to find paths through richly connected networks of relays.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
See a WIP extension for carrying this information and feel free to file issues or contribute there:

https://github.com/moq-dev/drafts/blob/main/draft-lcurley-moq-relay-hops.md

CC: @kixelated

issues.title: NAMESPACE doesn't allow parameters like PUBLISH_NAMESPACE
issues.author: kixelated
issues.body:
I realized when writing my extension that it can't work with SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE. I need some way to indicate the number of hops for a given NAMESPACE: https://github.com/moq-dev/drafts/blob/main/draft-lcurley-moq-relay-hops.md

This is also important because relays are expected to wait for a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, while clients are expected to send a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE. However this means any parameters from the original publisher can't be proxied by a relay.

Related to #1798

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> However this means any parameters from the original publisher can't be proxied by a relay.

I believe it's intentional that the NAMESPACE message doesn't have parameters.  Parameters in MOQT are hop-by-hop anyways since they can be aggregated by relays, and unknown parameters are always rejected.

Your extension is of course welcome to add parameters to any existing message, or define a new message that carries them.

That said, I think your extension is quite valuable.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
> I believe it's intentional that the NAMESPACE message doesn't have parameters. Parameters in MOQT are hop-by-hop anyways since they can be aggregated by relays, and unknown parameters are always rejected.

Sure.

It's still inconsistent that PUBLISH_NAMESPACE has parameters but NAMESPACE doesn't, even if it doesn't matter end-to-end.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> It's still inconsistent that PUBLISH_NAMESPACE has parameters but NAMESPACE doesn't, even if it doesn't matter end-to-end.

Yes and this difference was intentional.  PUBLISH_NAMESPACE is intended to only be sent _to_ a relay and NAMESPACE is only sent _from_ (for non-relays, 🤷 do what you want).  PUBLISH_NS needs params (eg AUTH) but NAMESPACE does not.  It was previously completely symmetric (through draft-14?) as SUB_NS solicited PUB_NS messages, but the group wanted the separation.

Yes I know your implementation preferred the symmetry.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: As @afrind suggested, I think having your extension negotiate a NAMESPACE_WITH_PARAMS message type is probably the cleanest option here?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: The extension is extending NAMESPACE, which is the intended design. Closing

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body: I think this is a flaw in the draft we should address. I'm up to 2 extensions that have to independently say NAMESPACE should have parameters but they don't in the base draft for some reason.

issues.title: Reconsider "OR" functionality in range filters
issues.author: vasilvv
issues.body: We added those to range filters to address scenarios like "a relay has two different sets of filters and it wants to combine them".  Now that we have multiple subscriptions (for similar reasons), is this still the right design?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
In fine MOQ tradition, we now have more than one way to do the same thing - 

1) I can make two subscriptions with different filters
2) I can make one subscription with OR'd filters

Today the Location filter and Forward are always AND with other filters, but we could change that.

The publisher also controls the max number of filter ranges per subscription and the max number of subscriptions (via bidi credit) per session, so there can be cases where you can do one but not the other.  Additional subscriptions take more publisher resources than an additional OR'd filter (it needs QUIC machinery).

CC: @mzanaty

comments.author: mzanaty
comments.body: Aggregating subs with disjoint filters was a big driver behind adding OR filters. But there is also general app utility, like filtering for high temp OR pressure (properties). OR seems very useful for the Property Filter applied to several properties.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Given we just discussed this and landed filters, should we wait a bit before discussing this again, or do we want to take this up in Vienna?  CC: @vasilvv

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body:
Not sure about Vienna, but maybe at a virtual call after?

My argument is roughly:
- There is a spectrum of how simple vs flexible we can make filter.
- The version without OR is a good spot in terms of complexity vs use cases addressed.
- We can ship a more complex scheme in the future when we get more experience with what people actually want in practice.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
Within a given property OR seems like it has a number of use cases (Highest and lowest values, video_codec=av1 or hevc, etc), but the main cases I have for OR across filters/properties are for a relay aggregating upstream.

The challenge of implementing this seems very similar to implementing multiple subscriptions with de-duplication.  So at least at the moment, the OR filters offer slightly different functionality because multiple subscriptions do not de-duplicate.

That's not to say I think the extra complexity is worthwhile.  There are some other details about the filters framing and behavior I think it's worth fixing before tackling this issue.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> multiple subscriptions do not de-duplicate.

This is the key difference.  If I SUBSCRIBE t1, color=Red and SUBSCRIBE t1, priority=7, all objects that match both are delivered twice.  If I SUBSCRIBE t1, color=Red SetID=0, priority=8, SetID=1, I only get them once.

comments.author: fluffy
comments.body:
Alan's point is very strong. Think about the case where this goers to the Original Publisher and that publisher is a cell phone on an ingest case with poor upload bandwidth. That case seems like a place where it would be good to avoid having the same object sent twice. 

That said, I would want to see a specific use case where this type of thing happened and was a problem. It also seems like something we could add later if it does become a problem.

issues.title: How do you know what Parameters a PUBLISH has?
issues.author: ianswett
issues.body:
Fixing #1660 allows SUBSCRIBE parameters on SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, but it's also possible to update those parameters.

How does a Subscriber know what Parameters were used to create the subscription?  There are two cases, FORWARD and GROUP_ORDER where we echo that back in the PUBLISH today.

There's also the case when a PUBLISH arrives that is not associated with a SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS.  It seems somewhat important to know the effective values for other Parameters, such as SUBSCRIBER_PRIORITY, as well as FORWARD and GROUP_ORDER?

In the virtual interim on July 6th, some people were concerned about creating another error condition if a Publisher specifies a Parameter that doesn't match one in the original SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS.

Ideas I posted on #1660:
1) Assume that people can figure out what the initial parameters are, so omit them. (Status quo)
  - Pro: Easy, Status quo
  - Con: If you update SUB_TRACKS, then how do you know which params are in use? Doesn't tell you anything about bare PUBLISH
2) Reference the Request ID of the SUB_TRACKS or subsequent REQUEST_UPDATE to indicate which params are in use
  - Pro: Only one field, simple validation.
  - Con: Instead of being racy, now you need to store all params ever sent on a SUB_TRACKS for an unknown time.  Doesn't tell you anything about bare PUBLISH
3) Repeat all the SUBSCRIBE parameters in the PUBLISH
  - Pro: No new framing or codepoints. They also don't conflict, so there's no ambiguity.  Could be useful in bare PUBLISH?  Similar to what we do for FORWARD and GROUP_ORDER today.
  - Con: Some SUBSCRIBE parameters don't make that much sense in the PUBLISH and aren't allowed there today. Could conflict with the SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, which creates another error condition.
4) Create a parameter that contains all the parameters the Subscription was initialized with (ie: SUBSCRIBE_PARAMS?)
  - Pro: Don't have to think about whether a Parameter might have a different meaning depending on which perspective it comes from (it probably shouldn't anyway, though?)
  - Con: Another nested parameter. Could conflict with the SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, which creates another error condition.
5) Use a potential new frame (ie: SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_UPDATE) to communicate the Subscription state
 - Pro: Could re-use a mechanism we (probably) want for DTS and Switch
 - Con: Arrives after the PUBLISH instead of in the PUBLISH. Could conflict with the SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, which creates another error condition.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: 2 seems to solve the use case with the minimal delta and data sent on the wire, so I'm leaning that direction.

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body: To me, the main negative of 2 is it doesn't tell you anything about a bare PUBLISH.  But maybe that's not important because the Publisher is going to decide what to send you?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
Shrug. Unsolicited publish has some oddities, like the subscriber can’t change the group order, and what _is_ the subscriber priority between publish fwd=1 and publish_ok?

I’m unenthusiastic about all the options

comments.author: ianswett
comments.body:
> Shrug. Unsolicited publish has some oddities, like the subscriber can’t change the group order, and what _is_ the subscriber priority between publish fwd=1 and publish_ok?
> 
> I’m unenthusiastic about all the options

Me too, which is why I haven't written a PR.  Other suggestions are very welcome.

comments.author: martinduke
comments.body:
echoing makes some sense; though AUTH probably shouldn't be?

There's some tension between something that definitely works all the time and something that is bit-efficient.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Discussed in Vienna: sounds like the easiest thing is to copy the subscription params into publish.  But we need to be careful -- e.g. AUTH shouldn't be copied.

issues.title: Subgroup Delivery Timeout and Timestamp have same value 0x06
issues.author: mzanaty
issues.body: Can't reopen #1647 so creating a new issue. This issue was caused by a bad merge in MOQT PR#1605 making MOQT internally inconsistent in adjacent tables for 0x06 (Subgroup Delivery Timeout and LOC Timestamp). LOC-03 fixed this by moving its Timestamp to 0x0A. MOQT is still internally inconsistent and needs a fix to move Timestamp to 0x0A.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: Fixed by #1807

issues.title: Semantics for PUBLISH_BLOCKED when additional stream credit is received
issues.author: sharmafb
issues.body:
Let's say we have a Relay, and that an endpoint sends a SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS to it. Let's also suppose that the Relay doesn't have bidi stream credit to send all of the PUBLISHes that it wants to send to that endpoint, and therefore sends PUBLISH_BLOCKED.

Is the Relay obligated to remember all of the tracks it should send PUBLISH for, in order to send them once bidi stream credit opens up? Or should the subscriber send a SUBSCRIBE when it is willing to open up credit? I would assume that the onus is on the subscriber, but perhaps we should make that language more clear.

issues.title: What is a subscriber entitled to observe after an Object becomes unavailable?
issues.author: ojhermann
issues.body:
## Summary
§9.1 lets a relay update a cached Object from existing to not existing, but only as a MAY, and only on receiving another Object at that Location. I can't find text saying what a subscriber is entitled to observe when the relay doesn't.

Concretely:

1. The Original Publisher publishes Object `(g, o)` with payload `P`.
2. A relay subscribes upstream, receives it, caches it.
3. `(g, o)` becomes unavailable at the origin.
4. A subscriber subscribes to the relay and is served `(g, o)` = `P` from cache.

As far as I can tell step 4 is conforming, and unboundedly so: §9.1's update is a MAY, nothing obliges the origin to send anything, there is no revalidation requirement, and absent MAX_CACHE_DURATION §12.3 permits retention until eviction.

**Is that intended?**

- **If yes** — a subscriber's view may reflect a past state of the origin, with no staleness bound beyond cache retention — §2.1 or §9.1 should say so. §2.1 currently states the three Object states from the perspective of "a subscriber or a cache" without distinguishing them, which invites the stronger reading that the two track each other.
- **If no** — absence is meant to propagate — the mechanism is underspecified. §9.1 item 1 gives the relay permission to update, but puts no obligation on anyone to trigger it.

The practical impact is that two conforming relays can diverge permanently: if A applies the update and B ignores it, A's subscriber records not-exists — which §2.1 makes permanent and authoritative — while B's subscriber holds the Object. Nothing reconciles them.

## Detail

**What triggers the §9.1 update?** I can't find a signal an origin can legally send that would cause a relay to transition an Object it already holds from existing to not existing. The three non-existence signals I can find are all prefix-shaped, and each is malformed when it covers something already delivered:

- End of Group (0x3) and End of Track (0x4) are Object Status values, present only on SUBSCRIPTION delivery, and both speak about Objects at or after a Location. §2.4.2 item 4 makes a Group malformed if an Object is received whose Object ID is larger than the END_OF_GROUP final Object — so an End of Group that retroactively covers an already-delivered Object puts the Track in a malformed state at every receiver that already has it.
- Prior Object ID Gap (§12.9) describes Objects that "do not, and will never, exist" prior to the current Object, and §12.9 explicitly makes the Track malformed if the gap covers an Object the endpoint previously received.

If that's right, §9.1 item 1 is only reachable for an Object the relay has *not* already delivered downstream, and withdrawal of a delivered Object has no wire representation at all. That would make the "if no" branch above the only consistent reading, and would mean the gap is a missing mechanism rather than a missing sentence. If there is a vehicle I've missed, that's the answer to this issue and I'd be glad to be corrected.

**Related issues.** #1703 asks whether the §9.1 update permission is a good idea; this issue is about the case where a relay declines it, which stays open under either resolution there, since the permission is a MAY in both. #1582 is the same question one level up for error codes — and its London resolution bounds error staleness by the Retry Interval, where Objects have no analogous bound. #1732 established that expiry yields _unknown_ rather than not-exists, so MAX_CACHE_DURATION doesn't answer this either.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
There is no publisher initiated signal to forcibly transition a previously published object from existing to not existing.  The mechanism is to use MAX_CACHE_DURATION - the relay cannot serve from cache after this time, and if a subscriber requests the object, the relay has to refetch from the publisher, at which time it can signal non-existence via a FETCH gap.  This is more or less analogous to HTTP.  The section 9.1 update refers to this process.

I can imagine introducing a couple ways we accomplish do what you are asking (either a MAX_LIFETIME property, which relays can use to auto-expire objects, or an explicit control message like PURGE?), but so far the above mechanism seems acceptable to the wg.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I'm going to close for now.  If the existing mechanisms are insufficient, please reopen and indicate the use case.

issues.title: §9.4 justifies subscription aggregation with a widening restriction I can't find in the draft
issues.author: ojhermann
issues.body:
## Summary

**The problem.** §9.4 tells relays that aggregate subscriptions they can use a Largest Object Location filter upstream, "Because MOQT restricts widening a subscription" — but §10.9.1 describes widening in both directions as ordinary behaviour, and I can't find a restriction anywhere in the draft. (see [The two passages](#the-two-passages), below)

**Consequences.** The clause is the stated *justification*, not an aside: it is why that upstream filter is presented as safe even when downstream subscribers have "disparate filters". A Largest Object filter starts after everything already published, so if widening is in fact permitted, the premise fails and §9.4's recommended strategy is left without a stated basis — while §5.1.2 explicitly permits a subscriber to ask for earlier Objects. An implementer reading §9.4 on its own gets a strategy plus a reason to trust it, and the reason doesn't hold. (see [Why it matters](#why-it-matters), below)

**Possible solutions.** Either drop the clause and state the actual reason the filter is safe — presumably that §5.1.5's Joining FETCH is how downstream subscribers obtain earlier Objects, which would also be worth a pointer from §9.4 — or, if the restriction is intended, make §10.9.1 and §10.2.9 say so, since they currently read as permitting exactly what §9.4 calls restricted. (see [Suggested resolutions](#suggested-resolutions), below)

I may simply have missed the rule; if so, that's the answer to this issue and a pointer would be welcome.

---

## The two passages

§9.4 (Subscriber Interactions):

> Relays MAY aggregate authorized subscriptions for a given Track when multiple subscribers request the same Track. [...] **Because MOQT restricts widening a subscription**, relays that aggregate upstream subscriptions can subscribe using the Largest Object Location filter to avoid churn as downstream subscribers with disparate filters subscribe and unsubscribe from a Track.

§10.9.1 (Updating Subscriptions), on the same operation:

> When a subscriber **decreases** the Start Location of the Location Filter (see Section 5.1.2), the Start Location **can be smaller than the Track's Largest Location**, similar to a new Subscription. FETCH can be used to retrieve any necessary Objects smaller than the current Largest Location.
>
> When a subscriber **increases the End Location**, the Largest Object at the publisher might already be larger than the previous End Location. This will create a gap in the subscription. The REQUEST_UPDATE_OK will include the LARGEST_OBJECT parameter, and the subscriber can issue a FETCH to retrieve the omitted Objects, if any.

Both of those are widening, and §10.9.1 describes each as ordinary — down to naming the remedy for the resulting gap.

Two further places I looked and found no restriction:

- §10.2.9 says LOCATION_FILTER "MAY appear in a SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH_OK or REQUEST_UPDATE (for a subscription) message", with no constraint on which direction its Start Location or End Group Delta may move.
- Searching the whole document for *widen* / *narrow* returns only the §9.4 clause above and §10.9.1's paragraph about **narrowing** ("When a subscriber narrows their subscription (increase the Start Location and/or decrease the End Group), it might still receive Objects outside the new range…"), which constrains nothing about widening.

So as far as I can tell the clause is either stale — describing a restriction that was removed when REQUEST_UPDATE gained the §10.9.1 semantics — or it refers to something I've missed.

## Why it matters

A Largest Object Location filter resolves at the publisher processing the message, so the aggregated upstream subscription starts after everything already published, and the shared cache §9.4 offers as the remedy only ever holds what that subscription delivered.

If widening is permitted, the premise doesn't hold, and §9.4 gives no guidance on what an aggregating relay should do for a subscriber whose filter starts earlier — which §5.1.2 explicitly permits:

> AbsoluteStart (0x3): The filter Start Location is specified explicitly. The specified Start Location MAY be less than the Largest Object observed at the publisher.

§10.9.1 names FETCH for the analogous REQUEST_UPDATE case; §9.4 doesn't mention it. I'd rather keep that as a separate question and settle the factual point here first.

## Suggested resolutions

Whichever matches the intent:

1. **The restriction doesn't exist** — drop the clause, and if the Largest Object Location filter is still the right default for aggregation, state the actual reason (e.g. that §5.1.5's Joining FETCH is how downstream subscribers are expected to obtain earlier Objects). A pointer from §9.4 to FETCH would also close the gap with §10.9.1.
2. **The restriction is intended** — then §10.9.1's first two paragraphs and §10.2.9 need to say so, since they currently read as permitting exactly what §9.4 says is restricted.

comments.author: sharmafb
comments.body: #1735 is meant to address this, please see the discussion on that PR.

comments.author: ojhermann
comments.body:
Thanks — I'd missed #1735 (my search covered issues, not PRs). Its description answers the factual question directly:

> Draft-14 forbade the widening of subscriptions, but draft-18 doesn't.

That's the point I was unsure about, so the clause is stale rather than referring to something I overlooked.

What I don't think #1735 settles yet is the second half — what the *actual* reason is that a Largest Object Location filter is safe for an aggregating relay. The review thread on that PR leaves exactly that open: on the replacement wording ("Because changing the range of an established subscription is not retroactive and can create gaps that require FETCH requests to fill"), the response was "I'm not sure this is the reason?", followed by "Should I just remove that sentence altogether?" and then a hold pending #1673 and #1765. Nothing since 2026-07-06.

Of those two, #1765 merged on 2026-07-06 and the clause survived it — `main` at dea37d03 still reads "Because MOQT restricts widening a subscription". #1673 is still open, and it "Removed the Joining version of FETCH", which bears on the wording: the replacement rationale I suggested above (pointing §9.4 at Joining FETCH as the way downstream subscribers obtain earlier Objects) wouldn't survive that PR, and fill-fetch streams would change what an aggregating relay is expected to do.

So I'd suggest leaving this open until replacement text lands, since the sentence is currently in the draft and the PR that removes it is parked on an unresolved question about what to put in its place. Happy to be corrected if #1735 is how the WG prefers to track it — in that case feel free to close this as covered there.

issues.title: Is query in URI scoping?
issues.author: michalhosna
issues.body:
Is the draft's Scope section talking about `path` in RFC 3986 sense, or PATH option/HTTP `:path` sense? 

### Background:
- [RFC 3986 | Section 3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc3986/#section-3) defines `path` and `query` as two distinct components
- HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (and thereof WT) defines: The ":path" pseudo-header field includes the path and query parts of the target URI

### MOQT Text:
> **2.4.3 Scope**
> Unless the application has additional information, two tracks are assumed to belong to the same scope if and only if the authority and the _path_ values are equal. The authority and the path values are communicated through the CLIENT_SETUP message in case of raw QUIC, and through HTTP request header fields in case of WebTransport

> **10.3.1.2. PATH**
> When connecting to a server using a URI with the "moqt" scheme, the client MUST set the PATH option to the path-abempty portion of the URI; if query is present, the client MUST concatenate ?, followed by the query portion of the URI to the option.

comments.author: michalhosna
comments.body:
I think the query should not be scoping. 

I would argue that having query scoping is non-obvious. Furthermore, I would also expect many exceptions in real-world, as we see with HTTP. 
Compared to HTTP we already have more levels (authority, path, track namespace, track name) for identifying content. 

This would allow us to communicate non-scoping information in the connection URI to the server, for which we currently have no options.

comments.author: michalhosna
comments.body: Note: There seem to be unclear definition in WT itself: https://github.com/ietf-wg-webtrans/draft-ietf-webtrans-http3/issues/287

comments.author: wilaw
comments.body: +1 to query not being part of scope. RFC3986 treats query as an opaque sequence of characters. It does not mention key=value pairs, ampersands (&), or any specific parameter ordering rules. The arrangement, meaning, and interpretation of individual query items are left entirely to the specific application. This looseness should not be baked into the scope, which is a fundamental naming concept for MOQT.

issues.title: FETCH and REQUEST_ERROR encoding
issues.author: mengelbart
issues.body:
I am trying to generate parser and serializer code for control messages, which is harder for FETCH and REQUEST_ERROR than for other messages because these can have different formats depending on the values of other fields in the same messages: FETCH changes format based on the `Fetch Type` field, and REQUEST_ERROR can have a `Redirect` field if the `Error Code` has a certain value. For all other messages, I can just define the list of fields and their types, and then copy code to parse and serialize each field. This doesn't work for FETCH and REQUEST_ERROR, because their formats depend on these other fields.

Would it be possible to use the `Message Type` to encode the format instead? E.g., similar to SUBGROUP_HEADER, which uses different types depending on which fields are present, FETCH could use three message types to indicate the type of FETCH request. And REQUEST_ERROR could be split into REQUEST_REDIRECT (which contains only `Retry Interval`, `Error Reason` and `Redirect`), and REQUEST_ERROR (which doesn't need the `Redirect` field).

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
How ugly is your parser for these cases?  The FETCH spelling has been there a long while, though I think @martinduke had similar gripes.

I think the cognitive load of additional messages in the protocol for these cases is higher than having value-dependent fields.  Note that e.g. Object Status in the data plane functions similarly when length = 0, i think?

comments.author: martinduke
comments.body: it wasn't a big deal to me code-wise but I did find three separate formats for the FETCH message to be bit-inefficient and editorially hard to read. I guess two of the formats are going into a parameter so I think this problem is taking care of itself?

comments.author: mengelbart
comments.body:
The code is not very ugly. Now I just generate code for the messages that are easy, and implement the others manually. That works, but it is slightly annoying, especially when upgrading to new versions.

You're right, object status has the same issue, but objects also have that issue in general, because their format can change based on the type of the subgroup header message that opened the stream on which they are sent.

I wouldn't be concerned about the load of additional messages. We also already have, I think, 48 different subgroup header messages, some of which have the same format.

However, if this has been discussed before and it will be solved by parameters anyway, I'm fine with closing this.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I'll leave it open a little while to see if anyone wants to +1 here.  If there's not momentum by September 1, will close with no action.

issues.title: Semantics of multiple AUTHORIZATION TOKEN parameters in one message
issues.author: michalhosna
issues.body:
10.2.2 allows repetition:

> The AUTHORIZATION TOKEN parameter MAY be repeated within a message..."

From the discussions, I understand that at least part of the WG assumes this should be handled in an "or" manner, i.e. at least one token must be valid.

But the current text doesn't really specify how this should be handled on the receiving side, or what the semantics are in general. The section defines per-token error handling, but nothing about how multiple tokens combine into a single authorization decision. 13.3 (Authorization) only says "Relays will verify the token to ensure that the request is authorized" (_singular_).

Furthermore, the following part is probably not compatible with the general "or" idea, even though I am not sure what "invalid" covers here.

> The receiver of a message containing a well-formed Token structure but otherwise invalid AUTHORIZATION TOKEN parameter MUST reject that message with an MALFORMED_AUTH_TOKEN error.

Should we codify "or" behaviour? How prescriptive should the text be?

E.g.:

> Unless the application has additional information, when a message carries more than one AUTHORIZATION TOKEN parameter, the receiver is expected to evaluate each token. The request is assumed to be authorized if verification succeeds for at least one of the tokens.

Or just something like:

> The receiver MUST ignore any AUTHORIZATION TOKEN value it doesn't understand.

----

Related:
- #722
- #996 + #1276 added uniqueness requirements.
- #1724

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
CC: auth design team @englishm @fluffy 

The current posture of MOQT towards auth is that it's providing space to carry the things without assigning specific semantics and rules to them.  To that end, MOQT by itself doesn't tell you how to authorize to a particular endpoint.

> The receiver MUST ignore any AUTHORIZATION TOKEN value it doesn't understand.

I see why a statement like this would be useful: my client can talk to 3 CDNs, and have a valid token for each.  I form my request with all three, and don't care where I land.

The problem is that the `Auth Token Type` field is the same for all tokens of a given type.  If all my CDNs are using cat4moq, then my requests contain 3 tokens of the same type.  Does the relay "understand" the two that fail decryption with its key?

comments.author: englishm
comments.body:
> my client can talk to 3 CDNs, and have a valid token for each. I form my request with all three, and don't care where I land.

> The problem is that the Auth Token Type field is the same for all tokens of a given type. If all my CDNs are using cat4moq, then my requests contain 3 tokens of the same type. Does the relay "understand" the two that fail decryption with its key?

One alternative design I've discussed with @suhasHere for this is to handle multi-CDN scenarios in the token layer by allowing multiple claims that pertain to different providers to exist in the same token. The main thing that needs to be distinct for each provider is some kind of identifier of a scope. 

But that may not handle every scenario we need to support. For example if one CDN only supports token type A and another only supports token type B, then you would need separate tokens for each and a resolution/codification of this "OR" behavior.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: I think it would be nice if endpoints didn't fail my request if I include a token they didn't issue, but I don't know that we want to codify "OR"?  Wouldn't that preclude schemes that require multiple tokens?

issues.title: Interaction of INCLUDE_PROPERTIES=0 and mandatory track properties.
issues.author: sharmafb

Let's suppose we have a track that requires mandatory property X, which a subscriber doesn't understand. If a subscriber sends a message with INCLUDE_PROPERTIES=0, the publisher would omit X, and the subscriber never learns that X is required and processes the track anyway.

Should we carve out an exception for mandatory track properties when INCLUDE_PROPERTIES=0?

issues.title: Timeout overrides for subgroups not propagated by Relays that join in middle
issues.author: sharmafb
issues.body:
The spec says that a timeout override for a subgroup is carried only on the first object in a subgroup.

If we have a situation in which a relay joins in the middle of a subscription (say group=10, object=50), then it could miss the timeout override and not propagate the timeout value for that subgroup to the downstream.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: It's also true if you filter out the object carrying the timeout.  I'm not sure there's anything we can do about it though.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: To be more specific, the timeout overrides are carried in the data plane, which is inherently unreliable for multiple reasons (datagrams, filters, mid-subgroup join, etc).  But I think carrying them in the dataplane is a feature -- if it were in the control plane, it would be on a different stream, and might arrive out of order with the affected data.

issues.title: [MoQT] Recommendations for CAT token expiration & renewal in control signaling
issues.author: leonardovon-mcqueen
issues.body:
In the definition of Authorization under the [MoQT](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-transport-19.html#name-authorization) protocol, the CAT (Common Access Token) authentication method is provided. Per the [CAT](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-moq-c4m-01.html#name-multiple-actions) specification, Authorization supports token expiration(like CWT/JWT exp claim) and renewal. 
However, the control‑signaling interaction protocol does not define how the client notifies the server to renew the token, nor how the server alerts the client of an upcoming token expiry. Could the working group share any recommendations for handling token expiration and renewal within control‑signaling interactions?

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
I believe this is the intended use of the EXPIRES parameter.  The expected flow might be:

SUBSCRIBE track
AUTH_TOKEN=<cat token>

Publisher verifies token, extracts expiration

If valid:

SUBSCRIBE_OK
EXPIRES=<time>

In invalid

REQUEST_ERROR
AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED

comments.author: leonardovon-mcqueen
comments.body:
Perhaps my earlier description was not clear enough. For action requests such as Publish/Subscribe, the workflow does support checking whether a token has expired, with the result carried in the returned ACK message. However, there is another scenario:
- Step 1: An AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN is included in the SETUP flow. Its expiry time is set to T1, the current time is T0, and authentication succeeds.
- Step 2: When the time is approaching T1 — for example, 30 seconds before T1 — the client needs to update the token’s expiry time to T2 to prevent the token from expiring.

The question is: the MoQT protocol does not define control signaling for the server to notify the client of an impending token expiry, nor for the client to renew the token.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
>  the MoQT protocol does not define control signaling for the server to notify the client of an impending token expiry, nor for the client to renew the token.

That is correct.  This is the design.

> An AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN is included in the SETUP flow

This is a gap.  I don't have a great idea how to close it, because SETUP is unidirectional from each end, not request response.  There's nowhere to convey the session expiration.

Shining the Auth Design Team bat signal: cc @englishm @fluffy

issues.title: [MOQT] New Prior Subgroup ID Gap
issues.author: yuyou
issues.body:
The Range Filter introduced in MOQT v19 defines one or more Subgroup Filters, allowing subscribers to specify the subgroups they are interested in receiving. When a relay dynamically filters out one or more subgroups, the receiving subscriber may observe gaps in the Object ID sequence. To explicitly indicate that these missing objects were intentionally omitted by the applied range filters, rather than lost due to network congestion, MOQT may need a new **Prior Subgroup ID Gap** mechanism, analogous to the existing Prior Group ID Gap and Prior Object ID Gap fields.

## Prior Subgroup ID Gap

Prior Subgroup ID Gap only applies to Objects, not Tracks.

- Prior Subgroup ID Gap (Property Type: 0x3F): A variable-length integer containing the number of Subgroups prior to the current Subgroup ID (within the current Group) that do not and will never exist because they were conditionally filtered out.
 
(or similar spec. defined in 12.9 Prior Object ID Gap)

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: @yuyou What is the concrete problem / use case that warrants this property?  Group and Object gaps are signals to a cache so it knows not to fetch an object, but subgroups are used to organize objects - a cache does not need this signal.

comments.author: yuyou
comments.body:
Understood and thanks for the clarification. The subgroup id gap, however, may be useful for real-time scenarios.

Following are some rationales (polished by AI)

While the current MOQT design treats **Subgroups** primarily as delivery vehicles rather than addressable units for caching, there are several technical justifications for why a **Subgroup ID Gap** could be beneficial in **real-time scenarios** for both subscribers and relays. 

In real-time delivery, the "Completeness" of a group is time-sensitive. Below is a suggested technical explanation for the potential need for such a signal:

### 1. Intentional Layer Skipping (ABR Logic)
In real-time interactive applications, a publisher might use subgroups to separate different media "layers" (e.g., Subgroup 0 for base layer, Subgroups 1–3 for enhancement layers),. 
*   **The Problem:** If a publisher's local uplink is congested, it may decide to only publish the base layer (Subgroup 0) and skip the enhancement layers for a specific group. 
*   **The Need for a Gap:** Without a Subgroup ID Gap, a real-time subscriber or relay has no way of knowing if Subgroup 1 is merely delayed by the network or if it will **never arrive**. 
*   **Benefit:** A Subgroup ID Gap would signal that the publisher intentionally omitted those streams, allowing the subscriber's jitter buffer to immediately proceed with decoding the base layer rather than idling in a "waiting" state, thereby **minimizing latency**.

### 2. Parallel Stream Management and Resource Pruning
MOQT leverages parallel QUIC streams to avoid head-of-line blocking, with each subgroup typically mapped to its own stream,.
*   **The Problem:** A relay must maintain state for every active track it is forwarding. For a single group, a relay might be prepared to receive multiple streams based on the track's typical structure.
*   **The Need for a Gap:** If the publisher sends Subgroups 0 and 2 but skips 1, the relay might keep resources (or flow control credits) allocated for the "missing" Subgroup 1 stream,.
*   **Benefit:** A signal that Subgroup 1 is a gap allows the relay to immediately **prune its stream-management state** for that group and redistribute flow control or scheduling priority to other active subgroups,.

### 3. Application-Level Dependency Awareness
Subgroups are often organized based on dependency relationships; for example, Object B in Subgroup 2 might depend on Object A in Subgroup 1.
*   **The Problem:** If a subscriber receives Subgroup 2 but is missing Subgroup 1, it may delay processing Subgroup 2 while waiting for its dependency.
*   **The Need for a Gap:** While the `Prior Object ID Gap` tells the subscriber that specific objects are missing, it does not explicitly tie those objects back to the **delivery structure (Subgroup ID)**. 
*   **Benefit:** A Subgroup ID Gap provides a higher-level signal that the entire delivery chain for a specific substream is broken. The application logic can then immediately trigger **error concealment** or discard dependent data in other subgroups without performing an expensive Object-by-Object gap analysis.

### 4. Fetch Optimization for Relays
When a relay misses data and tries to "fill" its cache via an upstream `FETCH`, it retrieves objects sequentially by Object ID,.
*   **The Problem:** In a real-time "Join" scenario, a relay might want to know the **structure** of the group it is fetching to prepare downstream streams for its own subscribers.
*   **The Need for a Gap:** If the fetch response has a gap in Object IDs, the relay doesn't inherently know if those objects were originally part of a specific subgroup it was already serving to other clients.
*   **Benefit:** Signaling gaps at the Subgroup level allows the relay to maintain a consistent **stream-to-subgroup mapping** for its downstream subscribers even when the upstream data is arriving via a single-stream `FETCH`.

### Summary of Evidence
*   **Objects/Groups are for Caching:** Relays identify cached data by Track/Group/Object ID. Since Subgroup ID is not part of this "primary key," the cache itself has no need for a Subgroup Gap signal.
*   **Subgroups are for Real-Time Delivery:** Subgroups exist to leverage QUIC's parallel streams and prioritization,,. Therefore, any "Gap" signal for a Subgroup ID is purely a **signaling optimization** for the **transport and playback layers** to handle intentional data drops in live, low-latency environments.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
@yuyou please do not paste LLM output directly into GitHub issues.

I would only be convinced to add this header to the moq-transport if there is a strong use case _for a relay_.  All properties currently in the document fit that test.  Your proposed property could still be valuable for applications (publishers and subscribers), in which case it can be defined in an extension or streaming format document.

My read on relay need:

> 1. The Need for a Gap: Without a Subgroup ID Gap, a real-time subscriber or relay has no way of knowing if Subgroup 1 is merely delayed by the network or if it will never arrive.

The relay generally doesn't care if a subgroup arrives from upstream or not.  If it arrives and passes filters, it will get delivered downstream.  Applications usually know their subgroup structure and/or can learn it out of band from e.g. a catalog.

> 2. The Need for a Gap: If the publisher sends Subgroups 0 and 2 but skips 1, the relay might keep resources (or flow control credits) allocated for the "missing" Subgroup 1 stream,.

No relay pre-allocates stream / flow control credits based on anticipated subgroup numbering today -- it's not clear why they would.

> 3. The Need for a Gap: While the Prior Object ID Gap tells the subscriber that specific objects are missing, it does not explicitly tie those objects back to the delivery structure (Subgroup ID).

This is an application level concern, not something the relay needs to know.  In this example, there wouldn't be a gap header -- the subscriber would wait for 1 and needs to have timeout based logic to detect if it is dropped.

> 4. The Need for a Gap: If the fetch response has a gap in Object IDs, the relay doesn't inherently know if those objects were originally part of a specific subgroup it was already serving to other clients.

Locations in a gapped range in FETCH do not exist.  Objects that are served contain their subgroup id.  A relay that cares can detect the subgroup gaps.  Relays detect gaps in object ID space and send upstream FETCHes to fill them, regardless of how the subgroups are organized.

I wonder if you are asking for something different, which is a MOQT level drop notification -- e.g. sent by a _relay_ (not original publisher) that drops or resets data due to delivery timeouts.  In other words, the exact opposite of this proposal - you want to know when a subgroup _definitely exists_ that you're not going to get, rather than when there's no subgroup at all.  The gap property approach still leaves you with "maybe the publisher doesn't use gap headers" or "there is a subgroup here, which may be coming, or not".  This has been discussed before but didn't receive enough support to continue #423.

issues.title: MOQT should define Track and Object properties to signal payload compression
issues.author: wilaw
issues.body:
MSF is an example application which uses MOQT to transmit media data. MSF defines [Track and Object properties to signal that the payload is compressed](https://moq-wg.github.io/msf/draft-ietf-moq-msf.html#compression-signaling), along with an IANA registry to list various popular compression standards which might be used.

This requirement to signal that payloads are compressed is a general one for any application leveraging MOQT. Instead of having hundreds of applications defining different Track properties all saying that the payload is gzipped, this should be a core transport capability.

Suggestion is for MOQT to define the following properties

**Track Property** : Signals that ALL object payloads in the track are compressed using the specified algorithm.

**Object Property:** Signals compression on individual object payloads using the specified algorithm, allowing a mixture of compressed and uncompressed objects within the same track.

MOQT should also create an IANA registry listing compression types which can be referenced by these properties, for example gzip, Brotli, Zstandard etc.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body: If we want to have such properties defined in a reusable place (e.g. not MSF), I would recommend an extension draft rather than the core draft.  The only properties we define in moq-transport are the ones required for basic operation (e.g. delivery timeout, gaps)

issues.title: to PUBLISH_NAMESPACE or to not PUBLISH_NAMESPACE
issues.author: kixelated
issues.body:
I think this is a major interop issue, and it keeps biting me.

There are implicitly three roles in the moq-transport draft:
- publisher
- relay
- subscriber

While not stated, there's an implicit assumption that:
- **publishers** should send `PUBLISH_NAMESPACE`
- **subscribers** should send `SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE`
- **relays** should wait for `PUBLISH_NAMESPACE` and `SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE`

The problem is that my library supports:
- publishers connecting directly to subscribers (P2P): results in both messages
- relays connecting to other relays (S2S): results in neither message.

**There's no in-transport mechanism to know if the peer will PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE.** 

My workaround has been to always send both `PUBLISH_NAMESPACE` and `SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE`. But that's not ideal,  and then publishers complain that they get `PUBLISH_NAMESPACE` messages for random shit, as they expected the relay to wait for a `SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE`.

The other alternative is to have the application indicate if the peer is a relay just to decide whether to PUBLISH or not. I really don't like this approach.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body: And I'm focusing on `PUBLISH_NAMESPACE` but this should apply to `PUBLISH` as well. A publisher is expected to `PUBLISH` but a relay is expected to wait for a `SUBSCRIBE`.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> While not stated, there's an implicit assumption that:
> 
> publishers should send PUBLISH_NAMESPACE
> subscribers should send SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE
> relays should wait for PUBLISH_NAMESPACE and SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE

I think this is the wrong framing.

Applications know what they want to do and will send the messages they need to send to relays to make things work.  If your application needs to publish - send PUBLISH (not PUBLISH_NAMESPACE).  If your application wants to wait for subscribers to express interest, send PUBLISH_NAMESPACE.

The same is true for subscribers.  If you know what you want, send SUBSCRIBE.  If you need to do some form of track discovery, send SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE.

> publishers connecting directly to subscribers (P2P): results in both messages

Seems like this can be worked out by the application (always PUBLISH after connect?).

> relays connecting to other relays (S2S): results in neither message.

This is explicitly out of scope.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
> Applications know what they want to do and will send the messages they need to send to relays to make things work.

Generic CDNs (ex. cloudflare) are oblivious to the intent of the application. 

Unless you're implying that a generic CDN MUST:
1. wait for a (unique) SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE from a subscriber, and then forward it to all connections.
2. wait for a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE from a publisher, then forward it to all connections.

It would be quite difficult to do 1, especially without a way to update a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE because they work via prefix matching. 
I'm basically always doing 2 for IETF compatibility but then folks get annoyed during interop because publishers don't want to know about other broadcasts, yet my relay doesn't know if you're a publisher or a subscriber.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
When a client connects, my generic relay has no idea what broadcasts they're interested in, and blinding sending PUBLISH/PUBLISH_NAMESPACE feels objectively wrong, especially then there are optional tracks involved. 

Ideally, my relay could wait for explicit interest via SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE or SUBSCRIBE, but if the application expects a PUBLISH, then I have no choice than to firehose. I'm stuck sending unsolicited messages because I don't know if the peer will solicit them.

comments.author: afrind
comments.body:
> Generic CDNs (ex. cloudflare) are oblivious to the intent of the application.

moq-transport is not about how to build the inner workings of a CDN.  That is explicitly out of scope.  A CDN is a **single relay** from the perspective of the document.

> Unless you're implying that a generic CDN MUST:
> 
> 1. wait for a (unique) SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE from a subscriber, and then forward it to all connections.

A relay never forwards a SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE to connected clients.

> 2. wait for a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE from a publisher, then forward it to all connections.> 

A relay never forwards a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE to connected clients.

Client's send these messages to a relay (or CDN acting as a relay).  The relay sends only SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH and NAMESPACE (via SUB_NS reply stream) messages to clients.

> publishers don't want to know about other broadcasts, yet my relay doesn't know if you're a publisher or a subscriber.

Count me among the people who are annoyed ;)  I think where you're running into trouble is you are trying to make relays that connect to your relay identical to end clients.  I like symmetry too, but when you think about practical deployments, relays that connect to other relays are going to have different authentication/authorization profiles.  You don't dump the internal state of your relay to any old Joe who connects.

> When a client connects, my generic relay has no idea what broadcasts they're interested in, and blinding sending PUBLISH/PUBLISH_NAMESPACE feels objectively wrong, especially then there are optional tracks involved.

Blindly sending PUBLISH / PUBLISH_NAMESPACE _is_ wrong, see above.  Relays never send PUBLISH_NAMESPACE.  Wait for the client to SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS to solicit PUBLISH (for which they are authorized) or SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE to solicit NAMESPACE.

> Ideally, my relay could wait for explicit interest via SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE or SUBSCRIBE, but if the application expects a PUBLISH, then I have no choice than to firehose.

"I have no choice than to firehose" -- I think you've come down on the wrong side of this question.  The application has to ask for what it wants, and the relay has to validate that the client is authorized to receive it.  If the app wants a PUBLISH, it sends SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS.

>  I'm stuck sending unsolicited messages because I don't know if the peer will solicit them.

A client that doesn't send any requests gets exactly what it deserves?

pulls.title: Initial track PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE
pulls.author: kixelated
pulls.body:
Closes #13 #12 

This covers a few use-cases:

1. The sender can advertise support for multiple codecs/containers.
2. The receiver can request a specific track, for example: english or japannese audio.
3. The receiver can request one of many tracks, so the server can perform ABR. For example: one of 480p, 720p, or 1080p.
4. The receiver can request multiple tracks of the same rendition for multicast. For example: 480p, 720p, and 1080p.
5. The receiver can request only tracks it supports. For example: no 1080p due to an unsupported profile.
6. The receiver can seamlessly switch between enabled tracks. For example: send me the ad track while enabled, then switch to the content track.
7. The sender can pre-emptively send tracks before the PLAY message, avoiding a round trip.


There's a few use-cases that aren't covered:

1. The receiver wants to specify when the track should be switched (timestamp).
2. The receiver wants to go rewind and request older content for a track.

comments.author: vasilvv
comments.body:
I guess I have two thoughts regarding the track listing.

First of all, I am not sure we should be describing media parameters ourselves. MP4 already has fields for video width and length (in fact, a typical moov atom would have those repeated at least twice), so ideally we would just defer to those, since otherwise we're stuck recording more and more media-specific fields, which is something deferring to an existing container was supposed to avoid.

Second, this is definitely the solution that covers the most complex scenario (delivery with multiple formats), but I would also like us to support the simplest case (which would probably be ingestion where all formats are fixed at the start), and then extend up to the complex solution where the use case requires it.  That probably means we should make adding tracks mid-session a negotiated extension.

Viewer use-case:
```
sender           receiver
----------------------------

 CONNECT     -->
 TRACK (1)   -->
 TRACK (2)   -->
 TRACK (3)   -->
 TRACK (4)   -->
 SEGMENT (1) -->
 SEGMENT (2) -->
             <--  PLAY (1,4)
             <--  STOP_SENDING (2)
 SEGMENT (1) -->
 SEGMENT (4) -->
```

In both cases we send media pre-emptively, instead of waiting for the receiver to receive TRACK and then issue a PLAY. If the sender guesses wrong, then receiver can issue a PLAY message and STOP_SENDING the segments it doesn't care about.

sender           receiver
----------------------------
 CONNECT     -->

             <--  CONNECT

```

sender           receiver
----------------------------

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
To explain a bit more in-depth:

The goal of the dependency list was to give relays the information required to know which frames are droppable. This doesn't actually accomplish that goal since a frame could be a reference for a future frame. It's a lot of state to keep track of and it's unlikely to be used by even the smartest relay. It's much simpler and probably a better user experience for a relay to obey the delivery order.

The decoder doesn't actually need this list since the references are stored in the codec itself. A mismatch between the Warp dependency list and the codec reference list sounds pretty awful. Accurately populating the Warp dependency list requires parsing the codec bitstream, which is more difficult and expensive than it needs to be.

The only immediate use-case for the dependency list is to mark init segments. We could have a separate field for that, or put the init segment in the CATALOG itself. There's a possible use-case for SVC but again, a relay can just follow delivery order and the decoder _should_ be able to piece together dependencies from the underlying codec.

Plus I'm less of a fan of the specifications that always have a box length (ex. TLS, MP4). It's absolutely more difficult to encode and I'd rather go the QUIC style where versions/extensions are explicitly negotiated.

Where an explicit message length can help is for writing parsers that aren't smart enough to parse a partial message.  Eg: you buffer enough to read the type and length, then buffer up the the message payload, then parse.  That makes more sense for smaller messages or endpoints that will need the entire message anyways.  For OBJECT it doesn't make sense I agree.
